items.title: 2.2 Entity store
items.text:
• Status: in progress
  • Pull request: –
  • Records: DD-043 to DD-048, DV-14 to DV-16; relies on ADR 023, ADR 047, DD-028 to DD-031, DD-039 to DD-041

items.title: Scope
items.text:
The entities' storage in Elasticsearch, in aurelius-atlas-core: what AtlasEntityStoreV2 and EntityGraphMapper keep in the graph, without the request logic around it, which 2.3 to 2.5 port. ADR 047 leaves the storage layout, the identifier strategy and the consistency model to the design log; this increment records them.

Module What it holds stored_entity StoredEntity: an entity as stored, its system properties and attribute values unique_key UniqueKey: one unique attribute value of one entity type, the id of its reservation entity_documents EntityDocuments and its Elasticsearch implementation: indices, reads, conditional writes, reservations, journal entity_store EntityStore: GUIDs, reads by GUID and unique attributes, all-or-nothing writes, recovery, type usage testing/memory MemoryEntityDocuments, for tests

The server builds the entity store at start-up, recovers interrupted writes, and gives the typedef store its type usage check (DD-030). It also answers GET /api/atlas/admin/patches, promised by 1.5 (DD-031).

Not in scope:

Not delivered here Delivered by Reading entities over REST, with relationships and classifications (EntityGraphRetriever) 2.3 Creating and updating entities from requests: discovery, references, relationships (EntityGraphMapper) 2.4 Deleting entities: soft, hard and purge 2.5 Indexing attribute values for search (the attribute mapping) 4.1 A recorded migration mechanism for mapping changes that move data (ADR 023) when first needed

items.title: Semantics
items.text: Id Rule ENS-01 Entities live in one index behind the alias aurelius-atlas-entities, one document per entity with the GUID as its id; its system properties are mapped for exact lookup, its attribute values are stored but not indexed until 4.1 (DD-043). Unique value reservations and the write journal have an index each, aurelius-atlas-unique-values and aurelius-atlas-entity-journal. Preparing the store creates what is missing and changes nothing that exists ENS-02 A new entity's GUID is a random UUID in its canonical lower-case form, as Java's UUID.randomUUID() (DD-044) ENS-03 An entity is stored with its GUID, type name, every super type name, state, createTime and updateTime in epoch milliseconds, createdBy and updatedBy, version, isIncomplete, provenanceType, homeId, labels, custom attributes and attribute values. Attribute values are stored under the attribute's qualified name (Referenceable.qualifiedName) as the codec writes them (DD-039). Creating sets both times to the request's time and the state to ACTIVE; version is the entity's own, never incremented by the store (getEntityVersion) ENS-04 Entities are read by GUID, one or many, as last written: a read never waits for an index refresh. An unknown GUID reads as nothing ENS-05 An ACTIVE entity holds one reservation for each unique attribute with a value: of its entity type, the attribute's qualified name and the normalised value (PER_TYPE_UNIQUE). A write that needs a value another entity holds fails, writing nothing, with an error naming the value and its holder; Atlas fails such a write with an internal error (AtlasSchemaViolationException), and 2.4 decides the answer to a request. A value is released when the entity changes it, or leaves ACTIVE (removeProperty(uniquePropertyName) on delete) (DD-045) ENS-06 An entity is found by unique attributes: the ACTIVE entity of the type holding every given unique value; else, for a type with sub types, of the first sub type that has one (findByUniqueAttributes). Values of attributes that are not unique, and null values, are ignored; none left finds nothing ENS-07 A write is a batch of new and changed entities, all or nothing (DD-046): every reservation and check is made before any entity is written; a failure during the write restores every entity written to its state before; a write interrupted by a crash is undone by the next recovery. A reader may see part of a write while it is being written (DV-16) ENS-08 A changed entity is written only over the state it was read in; another process's write in between fails the batch with a version conflict, for the caller to read again and retry (DD-047) ENS-09 A type is in use while an entity of it exists, in any state (typeHasInstanceVertex); the typedef store asks before deleting a type (DD-030, DD-048) ENS-10 GET /admin/patches answers {"patches": [...]}, the patch records of the typedef document (DD-031) sorted by id, each as AtlasPatch writes it; Atlas's Java patches are not among them (DV-14)

items.title: 2.3 Entity read REST
items.text:
• Status: in progress
  • Pull request: –
  • Records: DD-049 to DD-051, DV-17 to DV-19; relies on DD-039, DD-040, DD-043 to DD-047, DV-15

items.title: Scope
items.text:
The read endpoints of EntityREST under /api/atlas/v2/entity, on the entity store of 2.2: Atlas's EntityGraphRetriever and the read methods of AtlasEntityStoreV2.

Endpoint Answers GET guid/{guid} AtlasEntityWithExtInfo GET guid/{guid}/header AtlasEntityHeader GET uniqueAttribute/type/{typeName}?attr:<name>=<value> AtlasEntityWithExtInfo GET uniqueAttribute/type/{typeName}/header?attr:<name>=<value> AtlasEntityHeader GET bulk/uniqueAttribute/type/{typeName}?attr_<n>:<name>=<value> AtlasEntitiesWithExtInfo GET bulk?guid=<guid>&guid=… AtlasEntitiesWithExtInfo

In aurelius-atlas-core, entity_retriever (EntityRetriever) builds entities and headers from stored ones; the server's routes/entity answers the endpoints. StoredEntity gains isProxy, which Atlas stores and reads back.

Not in scope:

Not delivered here Delivered by Creating and updating entities over REST, and scenarios that create what they read (DD-051) 2.4 Relationship attribute values (relationshipAttributes hold none until relationships are stored) 3.1 Classifications of an entity (classifications, classificationNames), guid/{guid}/classifications 3.3 bulk/headers (headers by classification update time) 3.4 Audit events ({guid}/audit) 3.5 Meanings (glossary terms) and business attributes of an entity 5.2, 5.3 Access checks (ENTITY_READ) 6.2

items.title: Semantics
items.text: Id Rule ERD-01 A GUID or type name in the path, and each guid of bulk, longer than 4096 characters fails with INVALID_QUERY_PARAM_LENGTH (400) before anything is read (Servlets.validateQueryParamLength) ERD-02 guid/{guid} answers the entity with that GUID, in any state, with its extended info; an unknown GUID fails with INSTANCE_GUID_NOT_FOUND (404). bulk answers the entities of every guid given, in order, sharing one referredEntities; one unknown GUID fails the request, and no guid fails with INSTANCE_GUID_NOT_FOUND naming [] ERD-03 An entity has its system properties as stored: guid, typeName, status, version, createTime, updateTime, proxy, isIncomplete, provenanceType, and homeId, createdBy, updatedBy and customAttributes when it has them; labels always, empty or not. classifications, meanings, businessAttributes and pendingTasks are left out (3.3, 5.2, 5.3) ERD-04 attributes holds every attribute of the entity's type, inherited ones included, null when the entity has no value (mapAttributes). A date reads as epoch milliseconds, an enum as its value, a struct as an AtlasStruct with every attribute of its type, arrays and maps as their elements read so (DD-049) ERD-05 An attribute that refers to entities reads each as an object id: GUID, type name and the referenced entity's unique attribute values that are not null. An owned reference (ownedRef) reads as GUID and type name only and adds the referenced entity to referredEntities: in full, or with minExtInfo=true with its system properties and those of its type's minimal-info attributes that have a value. An entity is built once per response, the first way it is reached. A reference to an entity that does not exist, and a null element of an array or map of references, reads as nothing (DD-049) ERD-06 Unless ignoreRelationships=true, relationshipAttributes names every relationship attribute of the type: null for a SINGLE end and [] for a LIST or SET end, as an entity without relationships reads (DD-050). referredEntities never holds the entities the response answers with (compact) ERD-07 guid/{guid}/header answers the entity's header: typeName, guid, status, isIncomplete, labels, classificationNames and classifications empty, meanings and meaningNames empty, each header attribute (the unique ones, name, description, owner, createTime) with its value or "", and displayText: the type's display text attribute, else name, displayName, qualifiedName, when one has a value (mapVertexToAtlasEntityHeader). The header by unique attributes is the same without classifications ERD-08 The unique attributes of uniqueAttribute reads are the query parameters attr:<name>, each with its first value; of bulk/uniqueAttribute, the parameters attr_<n>:<name>, one set per <n>, each with its first value; an attr_ parameter without : is ignored. An unknown entity type fails with TYPE_NAME_INVALID (400, ENTITY), no attribute or one that is not a unique attribute of the type, system attributes included, with ATTRIBUTE_UNIQUE_INVALID (400); the bulk read checks every set before reading any, and answers {} for none ERD-09 A read by unique attributes finds the ACTIVE entity of the type or of its first sub type holding the values, each normalised by its attribute's type (ENS-06); none fails with INSTANCE_BY_UNIQUE_ATTRIBUTE_NOT_FOUND (404) naming the type and the attributes as {name=value}. A unique system attribute (__guid) finds nothing (DV-17). The bulk read answers the sets in the order their indices first appear (DV-19) and leaves out those that find none ERD-10 Every endpoint reads from a registry no older than the refresh interval (TDS-13) and answers Atlas JSON (SRV-04, SRV-05)

items.title: 2.4 Entity write REST
items.text:
• Status: in progress
  • Pull request: –
  • Records: DD-052 to DD-055, DV-20 to DV-24; relies on DD-026, DD-039, DD-043 to DD-051, DV-15, DV-16, DV-18

items.title: Scope
items.text:
The create and update endpoints of EntityREST under /api/atlas/v2/entity, on the entity store of 2.2 and in the stored form 2.3 reads (DD-049): Atlas's createOrUpdate, updateByUniqueAttributes and updateEntityAttributeByGuid of AtlasEntityStoreV2, with the discovery of the entities a request names (AtlasEntityGraphDiscoveryV2, IDBasedEntityResolver, UniqAttrBasedEntityResolver), the comparison that skips unchanged entities (AtlasEntityComparator) and the mapping of values to what is stored (EntityGraphMapper).

Endpoint Takes Answers POST / AtlasEntityWithExtInfo EntityMutationResponse POST bulk AtlasEntitiesWithExtInfo EntityMutationResponse PUT uniqueAttribute/type/{typeName}?attr:<name>=<value> AtlasEntityWithExtInfo EntityMutationResponse PUT guid/{guid}?name=<attribute> a JSON value EntityMutationResponse

In aurelius-atlas-core, one module per Java class: entity_discovery (EntityDiscovery: the walk, the references and their resolution), entity_mapper (EntityMapper: values to the stored form), entity_comparator (EntityComparator) and entity_writer (EntityWriter: the store's write methods and their mutation context). In aurelius-atlas-typesystem, the entity type's dynamic attributes (DD-026). The server's routes/entity answers the endpoints. The parity harness gains {run}, a value unique to each run of a scenario (DD-055).

Not in scope:

Not delivered here Delivered by Deleting entities; a reference an update removes is dropped, where Atlas keeps it as a deleted edge (soft delete) 2.5 Relationships: relationship attribute values, inverse references (inverseRef), relationship GUIDs (DD-053) 3.1 Deleting an owned entity whose reference an update removes; reviving a deleted owned entity 3.2 Classifications given with an entity (classifications), which are ignored 3.3 Business attributes given with an entity (businessAttributes), which are ignored; the label endpoints 5.3 Import (createOrUpdateForImport), shell entities for missing references (create.shell.entity.for.non-existing.ref) 6.3 Access checks (ENTITY_CREATE, ENTITY_UPDATE) 6.2

items.title: Semantics
items.text:
"Assigned" GUIDs are non-empty and do not start with -; "unassigned" ones start with -; either is valid (AtlasTypeUtil). An entity read from JSON without a guid has a new unassigned one, - and a number (nextInternalId). Errors name values as Java's toString writes them.

Id Rule EWR-01 guid, name and typeName longer than 4096 characters fail with INVALID_QUERY_PARAM_LENGTH before anything else (Servlets.validateQueryParamLength) EWR-02 POST / and POST bulk create or update their entities (createOrUpdate, not partial). A request without entities fails with INVALID_PARAMETERS (no entities to create/update.; a bulk request without entities too, DV-24), a null entity in it with INVALID_PARAMETERS (found null entity), an entity whose type is no entity type with TYPE_NAME_INVALID (ENTITY, the name) EWR-03 Before an entity is walked, each dynamic attribute of its type (a string attribute named by an entity type option dynAttribute:<name>, others ignored) is set to its template evaluated on the entity, a dynamic attribute another one's template names first: text before a brace as it is, {attribute} the entity's value of that attribute as Java's text, {a.b} the text TEMP; text after the last brace is dropped, as Java's templateSplit drops it. When an attribute named is null, the dynamic attribute keeps its value EWR-04 The request's entities are walked, then each entity of referredEntities whose GUID a walked entity names, until none is left; others are ignored. Walking an entity records its GUID and visits each of its relationship attributes (from relationshipAttributes, else attributes) and its other attributes that are given: references in object id values, arrays, maps (keys and values) and structs, at any depth. A reference records its GUID when it has a valid one, else its type and unique attributes. A reference that is no object id or map, or whose map has neither a valid GUID nor a type and unique attributes, fails with INVALID_OBJECT_ID (the value); a struct value that is no struct or map fails with INVALID_STRUCT_VALUE EWR-05 Each recorded GUID resolves to the stored entity with that GUID when it is assigned; else, when the request has an entity with that GUID, to the ACTIVE entity holding that entity's unique values (ENS-06); else an unassigned GUID with no entity in the request fails with REFERENCED_ENTITY_NOT_FOUND (the GUID), and an assigned GUID that resolves to nothing fails likewise. An unassigned GUID that resolves to nothing names an entity to create. Each reference by unique attributes resolves to the stored ACTIVE entity of its type or a sub type holding them, or fails with REFERENCED_ENTITY_NOT_FOUND (the object id): an entity the same request creates cannot be named by its unique attributes EWR-06 Each entity of the request among the recorded GUIDs, in their order, is updated when its GUID or its unique values resolved, else created; an entity named twice is handled once. A relationship attribute given in attributes moves to relationshipAttributes unless that holds it already (compactAttributes). An updated entity takes the stored GUID; a created one a new GUID (ENS-02). Each GUID that changes is a guidAssignments entry, from the request's GUID to the stored one. A full update of an incomplete entity makes it complete EWR-07 A created or fully updated entity is checked and normalised by its type (EVL-01 to EVL-09); a partially updated one for update (EVL-03). Before that: a GUID that is not valid fails with INVALID_OBJECT_ID (invalid guid <guid>); a custom attribute key longer than 50 characters with INVALID_CUSTOM_ATTRIBUTE_KEY_LENGTH, one with characters other than letters, digits, _, - and CJK ideographs with INVALID_CUSTOM_ATTRIBUTE_KEY_CHARACTERS (values are not checked: Atlas checks only keys without its special prefix, and its default empty prefix starts every key); a label longer than 50 with INVALID_LABEL_LENGTH, one with other characters with INVALID_LABEL_CHARACTERS. The type's messages, when there are any, fail the request with INSTANCE_CRUD_INVALID_PARAMS (the list of messages) EWR-08 An updated entity is skipped, neither written nor reported, when each attribute it gives that its type has, each relationship attribute it gives and, when given, its custom attributes equal the stored ones (areEqualValues, through guidAssignments). Labels, classifications and business attributes are not compared EWR-09 A created entity is stored ACTIVE, with the request's time as both times, its type's super types, version its own or 0, its custom attributes and its labels; isProxy, provenanceType, homeId and isIncomplete are not taken from the request. When it gives any attribute, every attribute of its type is mapped: a primitive one without a value takes its definition's defaultValue when there is one, else, when optional, its type's optional default (null for a string, 0, false or the epoch otherwise), else its type's default EWR-10 An updated entity maps the attributes it gives that its type has, with the defaults of EWR-09 for a null primitive one, and its custom attributes when given; its labels, version and other system properties stay. When it gives any attribute or relationship attribute, its updateTime becomes the request's time. A struct value updates the stored struct of its attribute, attribute by attribute; a null struct leaves it. An array or map of structs updates the stored struct at each index or key, and drops the others EWR-11 Values are stored as DD-049 holds them: a reference as the GUID it resolved to, a soft reference as typeName:guid from the object id given (a GUID assigned in this request for an unassigned one). Null elements of an array of primitives or structs are dropped; a null reference in an array or map fails with INVALID_OBJECT_ID (null). A SET array keeps its first of equal elements. A partial update of an array or map whose attribute has isAppendOnPartialUpdate appends to the stored elements, a map's entries replacing those of the same key (DV-23). References keep the request's order (DV-21) EWR-12 A single reference that is set where the stored entity had none, not soft, in an entity attribute or a struct's, makes the referenced entity updated: its updateTime becomes the request's time, and it is reported with the operation of the request, once, unless it is created in this request or skipped (EWR-08) EWR-13 The response's mutatedEntities has, under CREATE, the header of each created entity and, under UPDATE (PARTIAL_UPDATE for a partial update), of each updated one, as written, with classifications (ERD-07); then each entity EWR-12 made updated, with its header without classifications. An entity created in the request is reported only under CREATE; an operation with no entity is absent, and with no entity at all mutatedEntities is. guidAssignments is always there EWR-14 PUT uniqueAttribute/type/{typeName} checks the type and the attr: values as ERD-08 does; a body without an entity fails with INVALID_PARAMETERS (no entity to update.); no ACTIVE entity holding the values fails with INSTANCE_BY_UNIQUE_ATTRIBUTE_NOT_FOUND (the type and the values as {name=value}). The entity takes the found GUID and is partially updated EWR-15 PUT guid/{guid}?name= sets one attribute of the entity with the GUID (INSTANCE_GUID_NOT_FOUND when none) to the body: an attribute of its type, else its relationship attribute of that name, else UNKNOWN_ATTRIBUTE (the name, the type). A primitive attribute takes the body as it is; an object id attribute takes a string body as the GUID of an object id of the attribute's type, any other body as an object id; an attribute of another kind fails with ATTRIBUTE_UPDATE_NOT_SUPPORTED (the name, its type name). The entity is then partially updated EWR-16 A request's entities are written together, all or nothing (ENS-07). A write that loses a race with another (ENS-08) runs the whole request again, once; a second loss, or a unique value another entity holds (ENS-05), fails with INTERNAL_ERROR naming the cause (DV-20) EWR-17 Until 3.1, a relationship attribute's value is checked, normalised and its references resolved as Atlas does, and is stored as the value of the entity's attribute of the same name when its type has one (a legacy relationship end); any other is not stored (DD-053)

items.title: Deviations
items.text: DV-20: Atlas fails a write that needs a unique value another entity holds with JanusGraph's SchemaViolationException, an internal error answered with a plain-text logged id; Aurelius Atlas answers INTERNAL_ERROR with Atlas's error body naming the value and its holder, and the same for a write that loses two races (DD-052). DV-21: Atlas orders the references of an array by the hash order of their edges (CollectionUtils.union); Aurelius Atlas keeps the request's order. Entities EWR-12 makes updated are reported in the order they were reached, where Atlas uses a HashMap's. DV-22: until 3.1, a relationship attribute that is not also an attribute of the type is not stored (DD-053); ended by 3.1b (DD-064), whose REL-11 to REL-16 replace EWR-17's storage. DV-23: a partial update appending to an array or map of references fails in Atlas with INVALID_OBJECT_ID, since it maps the stored edges as values; Aurelius Atlas appends. DV-24: a POST without a body, or a bulk request without entities, fails in Atlas with a NullPointerException; Aurelius Atlas answers them as a null entity and as an empty list. A body that is not JSON, or not the request's model, is answered as DV-10 answers it for types.

items.title: 2.5 Delete semantics
items.text:
• Status: in progress
  • Pull request: –
  • Records: DD-056 to DD-060, DV-25 to DV-27; relies on DD-043 to DD-049, DD-052, DD-053, DV-16

items.title: Scope
items.text:
Deleting and purging entities: the delete endpoints of EntityREST, PUT admin/purge of AdminResource, the delete methods of AtlasEntityStoreV2 and the delete handlers (DeleteHandlerV1, SoftDeleteHandlerV1, HardDeleteHandlerV1, DeleteHandlerDelegate), including the cascade over owned references, which moves here from 3.2 (DD-060).

Endpoint Answers DELETE /api/atlas/v2/entity/guid/{guid} EntityMutationResponse DELETE /api/atlas/v2/entity/bulk?guid=<guid>&guid=… EntityMutationResponse DELETE /api/atlas/v2/entity/uniqueAttribute/type/{typeName}?attr:<name>=<value> EntityMutationResponse PUT /api/atlas/admin/purge with a JSON array of GUIDs EntityMutationResponse

In aurelius-atlas-core, one module per Java class: delete_type (DeleteType), delete_handler (DeleteHandler, DeleteHandlerV1's logic), soft_delete_handler and hard_delete_handler; EntityWriter gains the store's delete methods. EntityStore writes can remove documents (DD-056), and every entity document indexes the GUIDs it refers to, to find the entities that refer to a deleted one (DD-057). The server's routes/entity and routes/admin answer the endpoints; two settings choose the delete type (DD-059). The entity scenarios of 2.4 now delete and purge what they create, and then delete their types (DD-055).

Not in scope:

Not delivered here Delivered by Relationship edges of a deleted entity, inverse references, composition through relationshipDefs 3.1, 3.2 Deleting an owned entity whose reference an update drops 3.2 Classifications of deleted entities and their propagation 3.3, 3.4 Audit events of deletes and purges 3.5 Access checks (ENTITY_DELETE, ADMIN_PURGE) 6.2

items.title: Semantics
items.text:
"Deleting" below is a soft delete, a hard delete or a purge, as EDL-04 chooses. "A reference" of an entity is an object id value of one of its own attributes, or an element or value of one of its arrays or maps of object ids; soft references and references inside structs are none (Atlas keeps them as properties, not edges).

Id Rule EDL-01 guid, each guid of bulk and of purge, and typeName longer than 4096 characters fail with INVALID_QUERY_PARAM_LENGTH before anything else EDL-02 DELETE bulk without guid and purge without GUIDs fail with INVALID_PARAMETERS (Guid(s) not specified). DELETE uniqueAttribute checks the type as ERD-08 does (TYPE_NAME_INVALID); without attr: values it fails with INSTANCE_BY_UNIQUE_ATTRIBUTE_NOT_FOUND given one parameter, {}, so the message keeps {1}; the values are not checked to be unique ones EDL-03 A GUID no entity has, or values no ACTIVE entity holds (ENS-06), deletes nothing and is no error. A delete skips an entity already DELETED; a purge takes only DELETED entities. A request that deletes nothing answers {} EDL-04 A delete is soft unless the server's default delete type is hard (atlas.DeleteHandlerV1.impl); with the override enabled (atlas.rest.enable.delete.type.override, off by default) the query parameter deleteType chooses: soft or hard in any case, anything else the default. A purge is hard EDL-05 Each entity to delete is deleted with the entities it owns, transitively: those its owned reference attributes name (ownedRef, single, array or map, a soft one by the GUID in typeName:guid), each once, skipping those in the state EDL-03 skips. Each deleted entity's header is taken before it is deleted, as toAtlasEntityHeader gives it; a purge's headers also have classifications: [] EDL-06 A soft delete sets the entity's state to DELETED and its updateTime and updatedBy; its attribute values stay, references included, as Atlas keeps soft-deleted edges that reads still follow. A hard delete and a purge remove the entity. Either way the entity holds no unique value any more (ENS-05) EDL-07 Each entity with a reference to a deleted one, unless itself deleted by this request or DELETED, is changed: a hard delete and a purge remove the reference (a single one becomes null, an element or entry is dropped), a soft delete keeps it; its updateTime becomes the request's time. A mandatory single reference fails the request with INTERNAL_ERROR (Cannot unset required attribute <attribute> on <guid> edge = <label>), and so does a mandatory array or map holding no more than its minimum count (Cannot remove array element from required attribute …, Cannot remove map entry …) (DV-26) EDL-08 The response's mutatedEntities has the deleted entities under DELETE (PURGE for a purge) in the order they were reached, then, except for a purge, the entities EDL-07 changed under UPDATE, with their headers after the change (DV-25). It has no guidAssignments EDL-09 A request's deletes and changes are written together, all or nothing, documents removed with the others (DD-056); a lost race runs the request again once, as EWR-16 EDL-10 Every entity document holds, indexed, the GUIDs of its references; the entities referring to one are found by searching them after a refresh (DD-057). Preparing the store adds the field to an existing entity index

items.title: 3.1b Relationship attributes
items.text:
• Status: in progress
  • Pull request: #116
  • Records: DD-064 to DD-067, DV-31, DV-32; supersedes DD-050 and DD-053; relies on DD-049, DD-052, DD-061, DD-062

The second part of increment 3.1 (DD-063): the relationship attributes of entities. An entity write creates, reuses and deletes relationships for the values of its relationship attributes; an entity read answers them in relationshipAttributes, and the legacy ends among its attributes, through the relationships.

items.title: Scope
items.text:
No new endpoint: the entity endpoints of 2.3 to 2.5 change.

Endpoint Change POST /api/atlas/v2/entity, POST /entity/bulk Relationship attribute values become relationships (REL-11 to REL-16) PUT /entity/uniqueAttribute/type/{typeName}, PUT /entity/guid/… The same, for a partial update and a single attribute GET /entity/guid/{guid}, /entity/bulk, /entity/uniqueAttribute relationshipAttributes and legacy ends read through relationships (REL-17, REL-18) DELETE /entity/…, PUT /admin/purge Owned relationship attributes are followed (REL-19)

In aurelius-atlas-core: graph_helper (GraphHelper's edge lookups, over an entity's stored relationships), relationship_mapper (RelationshipMapper, the relationship side of EntityGraphMapper), and changes to entity_mapper, entity_writer, entity_comparator, entity_retriever, delete_handler, relationship_store and stored_relationship.

Not in scope:

Not delivered here Delivered by Deleting the owned entity of an owned relationship an update replaces or drops (DV-31) 3.2 Classifications propagated over relationships 3.4 parentCategoryGuid in the relationship attributes of a related AtlasGlossaryCategory 5.2 Import's relationship GUIDs (isImportInProgress) 6.3 Inverse references whose inverse attribute is not a relationship attribute (DV-32) –

items.title: Semantics
items.text:
A relationship of an attribute is one of the entity's relationships with the attribute's edge label, in the attribute's direction: OUT when the entity is its end 1, IN when it is end 2, BOTH either way. Its other end is the end that is not the entity (end 2 when both are). The relationships are in the order the entity lists them (DD-061).

Id Rule REL-11 A write maps an entity's relationship attributes before its attributes (mapRelationshipAttributes): on create every relationship attribute of its type, on an update those given; a legacy end given in attributes has moved to relationshipAttributes (EWR-06). The attribute is the one of the relationship type the value names (relationshipType), else of the attribute's first. Its value is written as relationships, never as an attribute value (DD-064); its references resolve as 2.4's do (INVALID_OBJECT_ID, EWR-17). An update that gives relationship attributes changes the entity's updateTime and updatedBy REL-12 A single end. The current relationship is the one the value's relationshipGuid names, else the attribute's relationship that is ACTIVE, else its latest updated DELETED one. Given a value: with a current relationship whose other end, by the attribute's direction, is the value's entity, that relationship stays; with another, REL-13 gets or creates one from the current one's end 1 to the value's entity (OUT), from the value's entity to the current one's end 2 (IN), or from the value's entity to the entity (BOTH), and the value's entity becomes updated. Without a current relationship, REL-13 gets or creates one from the entity to the value's entity (from the value's entity to the entity for IN), and the value's entity becomes updated. A current relationship the result is not, or a null value on update, is deleted as REL-15 deletes it REL-13 Getting or creating a relationship of type T from entity A to entity B: an ACTIVE relationship from A to B with the label REL-05 gives them is reused, unchanged. Else one is created as REL-05 creates it, after REL-04's checks of T, the ends' types, and its attributes (INVALID_VALUE, INVALID_RELATIONSHIP_END_TYPE, RELATIONSHIP_CRUD_INVALID_PARAMS) but not RELATIONSHIP_ALREADY_EXISTS: with a new GUID, version 0, provenance type 0, and the attributes the value's relationshipAttributes gives, null for the others. Both ends list it (DD-061) and it is written with the entities, all or nothing (DD-066) REL-14 A LIST or SET end. The current relationships are the attribute's, in any state, ordered by their index when the first has one (DD-065). A partial update of an attribute with isAppendOnPartialUpdate keeps the current ones and adds the given ones (DV-23). Each given element is mapped as REL-12 maps a value, the current relationship being the one at its position, but its entity becomes updated only when its relationship replaces the current one or is created by this request. Unless the type's appendRelationshipsOnPartialUpdate option names the attribute, each current relationship not among the mapped ones is deleted (REL-15); the ones that stay (soft-deleted, or kept by appending) come before the mapped ones. Each ACTIVE one gets its position as index. A null value on update maps no element REL-15 A relationship an update replaces or drops is deleted with the write's delete type (EDL-04): a soft delete sets it DELETED, its updateTime and updatedBy, unless it is already DELETED, which changes nothing; a hard delete removes it and both ends stop listing it. The entity at its other end (by the attribute's direction) becomes updated, unless the attribute is owned (DV-31) REL-16 An attribute with an inverseRef constraint: after REL-12 or REL-14 maps an element to a relationship, the inverse attribute of the relationship's end 2 gets, through REL-13, a relationship from end 2 to end 1 of its own relationship type, with the element's relationship attributes, when that attribute is a relationship attribute of end 2's type (DV-32). For a single inverse attribute, end 2's relationship of it, when another, is deleted (REL-15); end 2 becomes updated unless its relationship stayed the same, or for an array, was reused REL-17 Unless ignoreRelationships=true, relationshipAttributes holds every relationship attribute of the type. Its relationship type is the attribute's only one, else the type of the first relationship the entity is end 2 of that is one of the attribute's, else its first; the end of that type the entity's type and the attribute's name match decides the cardinality. A SINGLE end reads REL-12's current relationship, a LIST or SET end all of the attribute's, in any state. Each is an AtlasRelatedObjectId: the other end's guid, typeName, entityStatus, displayText (as ERD-07 finds it) and qualifiedName when it has one; relationshipType, relationshipGuid, relationshipStatus and relationshipAttributes, a struct of the relationship's type with every attribute. An owned one adds the other entity to referredEntities (ERD-05). A legacy end that is not an attribute of the type is also answered in attributes, as object ids without the relationship, leaving out a DELETED relationship to an ACTIVE entity REL-18 An attribute that is a relationship end (a legacy end) reads through its relationships, in attributes, in headers and where the comparator reads it (EWR-08): a single one as REL-12's current relationship's other end, an array as the attribute's relationships' other ends in any state, ordered as REL-14 orders them, [] when there is none. Each is an object id with its unique attribute values; an owned one adds its entity to referredEntities and is named by GUID and type alone (ERD-04) REL-19 Deleting an entity also deletes, with it, the entities its owned relationship attributes name (EDL-05): for a single one the other end of its relationship with the attribute's label in which it is end 1, ACTIVE else latest DELETED; for an array the end 2 of each of the attribute's relationships; a relationship that is DELETED (ACTIVE for a purge) is skipped (DD-067)

• Status: in progress

The first part of increment 3.1 (3.1b brings relationship attributes to entity reads, writes and deletes): relationship instances themselves, through RelationshipREST.

items.title: Scope
items.text:
Endpoint Takes Answers POST /api/atlas/v2/relationship AtlasRelationship AtlasRelationship PUT /api/atlas/v2/relationship AtlasRelationship AtlasRelationship GET /api/atlas/v2/relationship/guid/{guid}?extendedInfo= – AtlasRelationshipWithExtInfo DELETE /api/atlas/v2/relationship/guid/{guid} – nothing (204)

In aurelius-atlas-model, AtlasRelationship and AtlasRelationshipWithExtInfo; in aurelius-atlas-typesystem, the relationship type's value side, which 2.1c left out. In aurelius-atlas-core, stored_relationship (StoredRelationship) and relationship_store (RelationshipStore, AtlasRelationshipStoreV2); relationships are documents of their own index, and both end entities list their GUIDs (DD-061). The entity store writes relationships with entities, all or nothing; deleting an entity deletes its relationships (DD-062); a type with relationship instances is in use. The server's routes/relationship answers the endpoints.

Not in scope:

Not delivered here Delivered by Relationship attributes of entities: relationshipAttributes in reads and writes, legacy ends as relationships 3.1b Composition cascades through relationships 3.2 Classifications propagated over relationships; propagatedClassifications, blocked ones 3.4 Access checks (RELATIONSHIP_ADD, RELATIONSHIP_UPDATE, RELATIONSHIP_REMOVE) 6.2

items.title: Semantics
items.text: Id Rule REL-01 AtlasRelationship reads and writes Atlas's JSON: guid, homeId, provenanceType, end1, end2, label, propagateTags, status, createdBy, updatedBy, createTime, updateTime, version, propagatedClassifications, blockedPropagatedClassifications, typeName, attributes. Read without them, guid is a new temporary GUID, provenanceType and version are 0, propagateTags and status null (init()). AtlasRelationshipWithExtInfo holds relationship and referredEntities, headers by GUID REL-02 A relationship type takes an AtlasRelationship, or null; anything else is invalid. With both ends, a relationship is valid when both ends name a type, each the end type's or a sub type's, and its attributes are valid for the struct side; else when both ends have a GUID; without both ends it is invalid. The same holds for update. Two relationships are equal when both are null, or their attributes, GUIDs, ends, labels, propagateTags and statuses are REL-03 guid longer than 4096 characters fails with INVALID_QUERY_PARAM_LENGTH REL-04 POST finds each end by its GUID, in any state, else by its type and unique attributes (ENS-06). It fails with INVALID_VALUE (unknown relationship type'<name>') for an unknown type; RELATIONSHIP_END_IS_NULL (the type's end 1, then end 2 type) for an end not found (DV-28); INVALID_RELATIONSHIP_END_TYPE (the type, its end 2 type, end 1's type) unless end 1 and end 2 are of the type's ends' types in either order; INVALID_PROPAGATION_TYPE (given, type name, type's) for a propagateTags other than NONE the type's does not allow; RELATIONSHIP_CRUD_INVALID_PARAMS with the struct side's messages; RELATIONSHIP_ALREADY_EXISTS (type, end 1 GUID, end 2 GUID) when one with the same label exists from end 1 to end 2, in any state REL-05 A created relationship has the given GUID when it is assigned, else a new one (ENS-02); status ACTIVE; both times the request's; version the given or 0; the given homeId and provenanceType; the label of end 1's relationship attribute, else the type's; the type's propagateTags, swapped ONE_TO_TWO/TWO_TO_ONE when end 1 is of the type's end 2 type; each attribute of the type with its given value. The end entities are not changed but for listing it (DD-061) REL-06 A relationship is answered as mapEdgeToAtlasRelationship maps an edge: its system fields, end1 and end2 as object ids with each end's GUID, type and unique attribute values, label, propagateTags, propagatedClassifications and blockedPropagatedClassifications empty until 3.4, and every attribute of its type, null when it has none. GET without extendedInfo=true answers it alone, with it also each end's header in referredEntities. An unknown GUID fails with RELATIONSHIP_GUID_NOT_FOUND REL-07 PUT fails with RELATIONSHIP_GUID_NOT_FOUND for no or an unknown GUID; RELATIONSHIP_UPDATE_TYPE_CHANGE_NOT_ALLOWED (GUID, stored type, given) for another type name ignoring case; RELATIONSHIP_UPDATE_END_CHANGE_NOT_ALLOWED (type, GUID, stored end GUID, given end GUID) for an end whose GUID, or the entity its unique attributes find, is another; an end given by unique attributes alone thus always fails, as Atlas compares the given GUID. It then checks as REL-04 does, sets the given propagateTags when it differs (DV-29), and each attribute of the type to its given value, or, when not given, to its non-empty default. Times, users and version stay REL-08 DELETE fails with RELATIONSHIP_GUID_NOT_FOUND for an unknown GUID and RELATIONSHIP_ALREADY_DELETED for a DELETED one. A soft delete sets status DELETED and its updateTime and updatedBy; a hard delete removes it (EDL-04). It answers 204 REL-09 Deleting an entity softly also soft-deletes its ACTIVE relationships in which it is end 2 (Atlas's incoming edges); a hard delete or a purge removes every relationship it is an end of, and drops them from the other end's list (DD-062). The other end is not otherwise changed REL-10 A relationship type is in use while a relationship of it exists, in any state: the typedef store refuses to delete it (TYPE_HAS_REFERENCES, relationshipTypeHasInstanceEdges)

items.text:
• Status: in progress

What is left of ownership after 2.5 and 3.1b (DD-060, DD-067): an entity write that replaces or drops an owned reference deletes the owned entity, as Atlas's deleteEdgeReference does, and an owned map entry naming a deleted entity revives it.

items.title: Scope
items.text:
No new endpoint: the entity writes of 2.4 change.

Endpoint Change POST /api/atlas/v2/entity, POST /entity/bulk, PUT /entity/uniqueAttribute/type/{typeName}, PUT /entity/guid/… Owned entities an update drops are deleted

items.title: Semantics
items.text: Id Rule OWN-01 An update drops an owned entity when an owned attribute of the entity it updates no longer names it: a plain one (not soft, EDL-05), single, array or map, whose stored value named it and whose new value does not; or a relationship one whose relationship to it REL-15 deletes, the entity being the relationship's end 2. A partial update that appends (EWR-11) drops none OWN-02 Each dropped entity is deleted with the write's delete type (EDL-04) as a delete of it deletes it (EDL-03 to EDL-07, REL-09, REL-19): with what it owns, and changing the entities that refer to it, as the update has changed them; one already DELETED is skipped; a mandatory reference to it fails the request (INTERNAL_ERROR). The deletes are written with the update, all or nothing (DD-068) OWN-03 The response lists the deleted entities under DELETE, after the created and updated ones and before those the request made updated (EWR-13); the entities the deletes changed are among the latter, under the request's operation. A deleted entity the request also made updated is listed under both, with the header taken before it was deleted; since 3.5a the response is pruned as Atlas prunes it, which lists it under DELETE only (AUD-02) OWN-04 An owned map entry, not soft, that keeps naming the entity it named makes that entity ACTIVE again when it is DELETED (updateInConsistentOwnedMapVertices, DD-069); nothing else of it changes, and it is not reported

items.title: Java origin

The second part of increment 3.3 (DD-073): bulk/setClassifications, Atlas's ClassificationAssociator.Updater, which sets the classifications of entities found by their unique attributes to those their headers give. bulk/headers moves to 3.5, since it lists the entities whose classifications changed from the audit (DD-074).

items.title: Scope

Endpoint Takes Answers POST /api/atlas/v2/entity/bulk/setClassifications AtlasEntityHeaders a JSON array of one summary per operation

In aurelius-atlas-core, classification_associator (ClassificationAssociator, its Updater), built on 3.3a's EntityClassifications. The server's routes/entity answers the endpoint.

items.title: Semantics
items.text: Id Rule CLA-01 Each header of guidHeaderMap, in the request's order, is handled on its own. One of a type that is no entity type adds <type>: (Skipped). The entity is the ACTIVE one of the type, or a sub type, holding the unique values among the header's attributes (ENS-06); none adds Entity:<type>:<name>:[Not found]:(Skipped), where <name> is the attribute name qualifiedName when the header's attributes have it, else the type's first unique attribute's name CLA-02 The header's classifications are those its entityGuid names the header's guid, or none, or the header has no guid; the entity's, as CLS-02 reads them, likewise for the entity's GUID. Matched by type name: the entity's without an incoming one are deleted, the incoming ones the entity has are updated (in the entity's order), the others added; nothing when both are empty CLA-03 Deletes run first, one by one (CLS-09), then the updates as one request (CLS-08), then the adds as one request (CLS-04, CLS-05); each changes the store at once. Each step adds <Delete\|Update\|Add>:<guid>:<type>:<name> -> <classification names, comma separated>:<status>, the status (Done), or (Partial) when a request of the step failed CLA-04 The answer is a JSON array of the summaries, in the order they were added; [] for none

items.text:
• Status: in progress
  • Pull request: #118
  • Records: DD-070 to DD-073, DV-34, DV-35; relies on DD-043 to DD-049, DD-052, DD-056, DD-061, DD-062

The first part of increment 3.3 (DD-073; 3.3b brings bulk/setClassifications and bulk/headers): classifications attached directly to entities, through EntityREST and entity creates, read back with the entities.

items.title: Scope
items.text:
Endpoint Takes Answers GET /api/atlas/v2/entity/guid/{guid}/classifications – AtlasClassifications GET /api/atlas/v2/entity/guid/{guid}/classification/{classificationName} – AtlasClassification POST /api/atlas/v2/entity/guid/{guid}/classifications a list of AtlasClassification nothing (204) PUT /api/atlas/v2/entity/guid/{guid}/classifications a list of AtlasClassification nothing (204) DELETE /api/atlas/v2/entity/guid/{guid}/classification/{classificationName} – nothing (204) POST, PUT /api/atlas/v2/entity/uniqueAttribute/type/{typeName}/classifications?attr:… a list of AtlasClassification nothing (204) DELETE /api/atlas/v2/entity/uniqueAttribute/type/{typeName}/classification/{name}?attr:… – nothing (204) POST /api/atlas/v2/entity/bulk/classification ClassificationAssociateRequest nothing (204)

Entity reads answer classifications, and headers classificationNames and classifications; an entity create attaches the classifications it gives; deletes delete an entity's classifications with it.

In aurelius-atlas-model, AtlasClassifications and ClassificationAssociateRequest. In aurelius-atlas-core, stored_classification (StoredClassification) and entity_classifications (EntityClassifications: the classification methods of AtlasEntityStoreV2 and EntityGraphMapper); classification instances are documents of their own index, listed by the entity they are attached to (DD-070), written with entities all or nothing (DD-071). The server's routes/entity answers the endpoints.

Not in scope:

Not delivered here Delivered by POST bulk/setClassifications (ClassificationAssociator), GET bulk/headers?tagUpdateStartTime 3.3b Propagation: propagated classifications, associatedEntityGuid, propagation tasks (DV-34) 3.4 Classifications of updated entities in an import (replaceClassifications) 6.3 Audit events and notifications of classification changes 3.5, – Access checks (ENTITY_ADD_CLASSIFICATION, …) 6.2

items.title: Semantics
items.text: Id Rule CLS-01 AtlasClassifications is Atlas's PList of classifications: list, startIndex 0, pageSize and totalCount its length, sortType NONE. ClassificationAssociateRequest reads and writes classification, entityGuids, entitiesUniqueAttributes and entityTypeName CLS-02 An entity reads its classifications in classifications, in the order they were attached, absent when it has none (mapClassifications). Each has its typeName, every attribute of its type (null when it has no value), entityGuid, entityStatus, propagate, removePropagationsOnEntityDelete, and validityPeriods when stored (toAtlasClassification). A header has their names in classificationNames (ERD-07), and where ERD-07 and EWR-13 give classifications, them CLS-03 GET guid/{guid}/classifications answers the entity's classifications as AtlasClassifications; an unknown GUID fails with INSTANCE_GUID_NOT_FOUND. GET guid/{guid}/classification/{name} fails with TYPE_NAME_INVALID (CLASSIFICATION, name) for a name no classification type has, and answers the first classification of that name, ignoring case, attached directly (entityGuid empty or the entity's), else the first of the name; none fails with CLASSIFICATION_NOT_FOUND. A path parameter over 4096 characters fails with INVALID_QUERY_PARAM_LENGTH CLS-04 Adding classifications to an entity fails with INVALID_PARAMETERS (Guid(s) not specified, classifications(s) not specified) without a GUID or classifications, and with INSTANCE_GUID_NOT_FOUND for an unknown entity, in any state. Each classification is then checked and normalised by its type: CLASSIFICATION_NOT_FOUND for an unknown type, INVALID_PARAMETERS with the type's messages (validity periods included, EVL-07); then each fails with INVALID_PARAMETERS (entity: <guid>, already associated with classification: <name>) when the entity has one of its name attached directly, and with INVALID_ENTITY_FOR_CLASSIFICATION when its type may not classify the entity's type (THY-07) CLS-05 Each added classification, unless it says propagate and names another entity, is attached as a new classification instance: propagate true when not given (DD-072, DV-34), removePropagationsOnEntityDelete false when not given, entityGuid the entity's when not given, entityStatus ACTIVE when not given, its validity periods and its attributes as their types store them (DD-049). The entity's updateTime and updatedBy change. The request answers 204 CLS-06 The uniqueAttribute forms find the entity as ERD-08 and ERD-09 do: TYPE_NAME_INVALID (ENTITY) for an unknown entity type, INSTANCE_BY_UNIQUE_ATTRIBUTE_NOT_FOUND (type, values) when no ACTIVE entity holds the values; then they add, update or delete as the GUID forms do CLS-07 bulk/classification fails with INVALID_PARAMETERS (no classification) without a classification type name, and (Need either list of GUIDs or entity type and list of qualified Names) without GUIDs and without both the entity type and unique attribute sets. With both, it checks the type (TYPE_NAME_INVALID), adds the GUID of each set's ACTIVE holder, skipping sets that find none, and fails (No guid found for given entity Type Name and list of attributes) when there is then no GUID. It checks the classification once (CLS-04), each entity (INSTANCE_GUID_NOT_FOUND, the association checks) before changing any, then attaches it to each (CLS-05), all in one write CLS-08 Updating classifications fails with INVALID_PARAMETERS without a GUID (Guid not specified) or classifications, and with INSTANCE_GUID_NOT_FOUND; each is checked as CLS-04 checks it. Each, in turn: one naming another entity fails with CLASSIFICATION_UPDATE_FROM_PROPAGATED_ENTITY; one the entity has not attached directly with CLASSIFICATION_NOT_ASSOCIATED_WITH_ENTITY; it is checked for update by its type (CLASSIFICATION_NOT_FOUND, INVALID_PARAMETERS); then its given attributes replace the stored ones, its validity periods, propagate and removePropagationsOnEntityDelete when given replace theirs, and the entity's updateTime and updatedBy change. A change of propagate propagates nothing until 3.4 (DV-34) CLS-09 DELETE guid/{guid}/classification/{name} fails with TYPE_NAME_INVALID for an unknown classification type, INSTANCE_GUID_NOT_FOUND, NO_CLASSIFICATIONS_FOUND_FOR_ENTITY when the entity has no classification attached directly, and CLASSIFICATION_NOT_ASSOCIATED_WITH_ENTITY when none of them has the name (exactly). The instance is removed, whatever the delete type, and the entity's updateTime and updatedBy change. One naming another entity in associatedEntityGuid fails, until 3.4 brings propagated classifications, with PROPAGATED_CLASSIFICATION_NOT_ASSOCIATED_WITH_ENTITY (name, that entity, the entity), as Atlas answers when it has none CLS-10 An entity create attaches the classifications the entity gives, after its attributes, as CLS-05 does, without CLS-04's checks: one of an unknown type fails with CLASSIFICATION_NOT_FOUND (DV-35). Its CREATE header is taken before they are attached, so it shows none (constructHeader). An update ignores them, as Atlas's createOrUpdate does without replaceClassifications CLS-11 Deleting an entity softly keeps its classifications, entityStatus DELETED; a hard delete and a purge remove them. A purge's headers have the purged entity's classifications (EDL-05) CLS-12 A classification type is in use while a classification instance of it exists, in any state: the typedef store refuses to delete it (TYPE_HAS_REFERENCES)

items.title: 3.4a Classification propagation
items.text:
• Status: in progress
  • Pull request: #122
  • Records: DD-075 to DD-078, DV-37; ends DV-34; relies on DD-061, DD-062, DD-066, DD-068, DD-070, DD-071

The first part of increment 3.4 (DD-078; 3.4b defers propagation to tasks, as Atlas does by default): classifications reaching the entities related to their entity, computed and written within the request that causes them, as Atlas does with atlas.tasks.enabled=false.

items.title: Scope
items.text:
No new endpoint. Classification adds, updates and deletes (3.3a), relationship creates, updates and deletes (3.1a), entity writes that create or remove relationships (3.1b, 3.2) and entity deletes (2.5) propagate; entities read propagated classifications among their own (CLS-02), relationships their propagatedClassifications and blockedPropagatedClassifications.

In aurelius-atlas-core, tag_propagation (TagPropagation: the propagation of DeleteHandlerV1, EntityGraphRetriever and GraphHelper), and changes to entity_classifications, relationship_store, entity_writer, delete_handler, relationship_mapper and entity_retriever. Entities are found by the classification instances they list through an indexed field (DD-076).

Not in scope:

Not delivered here Delivered by Deferred propagation tasks (atlas.tasks.enabled), pendingTasks, admin/tasks, DELETE_TAG_PROPAGATION_NOT_ALLOWED 3.4b Classification text (__classificationsText) and notifications 4.1, –

items.title: Semantics
items.text:
An entity's propagation-enabled classifications are those it lists, attached or propagated, whose propagate is true. A relationship propagates from end 1 for ONE_TO_TWO, from end 2 for TWO_TO_ONE, from both for BOTH.

Id Rule PRO-01 The entities a classification reaches from an entity are found breadth first (traverseImpactedVertices): from each entity reached, over its ACTIVE relationships whose label is one of its type's tag propagation edges (THY-11) and that propagate away from it, skipping a relationship the step excludes and, for a given classification, those that block it; each entity once, the starting one not among them unless the step includes it PRO-02 Propagating a classification to entities (addTagPropagation) skips its own entity, one that lists it already, and one whose type it may not classify; each other entity lists it, after its own (DD-075). Nothing else of the entity changes PRO-03 Adding a classification with propagate true propagates it to the entities it reaches from its entity (PRO-01, no classification given). Updating propagate from false to true propagates it to those it reaches, its blocks counted; from true to false removes it from every entity it was propagated to. Deleting a classification attached directly first removes it so when its propagate is true PRO-04 A created relationship (CLS-05 order: blocked classifications first) propagates, for each end it propagates from, that end's propagation-enabled classifications to the other end and the entities they reach from it, the new relationship excluded PRO-05 Updating a relationship's propagateTags to another value recomputes, for the propagation-enabled classifications of its ends before and after, the entities each reaches from its entity, and adds or removes the differences. Otherwise, blockedPropagatedClassifications when given replace its blocks: each one matching one of its ends' propagation-enabled classifications by type name and entity GUID blocks it, others are ignored; each classification whose block changed gains the entities it now reaches and loses those it no longer does (evaluateClassificationPropagation) PRO-06 A relationship removed (a hard delete over REST, a hard REL-15 delete, an end removed by a hard delete or purge) removes, of its propagatable classifications whose removePropagationsOnEntityDelete is true, each from the entities it no longer reaches without it; a soft delete removes none. Propagated classifications to a deleted relationship's ends stay otherwise PRO-07 Deleting an entity removes every propagation of its directly attached classifications whose removePropagationsOnEntityDelete is true. Its attached ones are then DELETED (soft) as CLS-11 says, or removed (hard, purge) unless other entities still list them, which keep them, entityStatus PURGED; the propagated ones it lists go with it, or stay listed after a soft delete PRO-08 DELETE guid/{guid}/classification/{name}?associatedEntityGuid= naming another entity removes the classification of that name propagated from it: PROPAGATED_CLASSIFICATION_NOT_ASSOCIATED_WITH_ENTITY when the entity has none, PROPAGATED_CLASSIFICATION_REMOVAL_NOT_SUPPORTED (name, that entity) while its entityStatus is ACTIVE; else the entity stops listing it, and the instance is removed when no entity lists it any more PRO-09 A relationship reads, from its ends' propagation-enabled classifications (none while it is DELETED), those it blocks in blockedPropagatedClassifications and the others in propagatedClassifications (readClassificationsFromEdge); with extendedInfo, each one's entity header is among referredEntities PRO-10 Propagation is written with the request that causes it, all or nothing (DD-071, DD-077)

items.title: 3.4b Propagation tasks
items.text:
• Status: in progress
  • Pull request: #125
  • Records: DD-079 to DD-081, DV-38; ends DV-37; relies on DD-071, DD-075 to DD-078

The second part of increment 3.4 (DD-078): propagation deferred to tasks, as Atlas does by default (atlas.tasks.enabled=true). A request records a task with its change; a worker in every server process runs the tasks after it, each as one write (DD-080). The propagation itself is 3.4a's.

items.title: Scope
items.text:
Endpoint Takes Answers GET /api/atlas/admin/tasks?guids=<guid>&… – a list of AtlasTask DELETE /api/atlas/admin/tasks?guids=<guid>&… – nothing (204)

Entities read their pendingTasks. In aurelius-atlas-model, AtlasTask. In aurelius-atlas-core, stored_task (StoredTask), task_management (TaskManagement: Atlas's TaskManagement, TaskRegistry and TaskExecutor) and classification_tasks (ClassificationTasks: ClassificationPropagationTasks and ClassificationTask); tasks are documents of their own index, listed by the entity they are queued on (DD-079). The server runs a worker and answers admin/tasks; AURELIUS_ATLAS_SERVER_TASKS_ENABLED chooses (DD-081).

Not in scope:

Not delivered here Delivered by Audit reduction tasks (AuditReductionTaskFactory) and the dashboard's task tab 3.5, –

items.title: Semantics
items.text: Id Rule TSK-01 AtlasTask reads and writes type, guid, createdBy, createdTime, updatedTime, startTime, endTime, parameters, attemptCount, errorMessage and status (PENDING, IN_PROGRESS, COMPLETE, FAILED); times as epoch milliseconds, nulls left out. A new task is PENDING, has a new GUID, both times now and no attempts TSK-02 With tasks enabled, a change that 3.4a propagates at once records a task instead, written with the change (DD-079), its GUID added to pendingTasks of the entity it is queued on: CLASSIFICATION_PROPAGATION_ADD for an added classification that propagates (on its entity), for an update giving propagate true (likewise, whatever it was), and for a created relationship, one per propagation-enabled classification of each end it propagates from (on the other end, with the relationship's GUID), except one the same request adds, which has its own; CLASSIFICATION_PROPAGATION_DELETE for an update giving propagate false, for a deleted classification that propagates, and for an entity deleted with a classification that removes propagations; CLASSIFICATION_PROPAGATION_RELATIONSHIP_UPDATE for every relationship update (on the relationship). Its parameters are entityGuid, classificationVertexId (the instance's GUID), classificationName and relationshipGuid, or relationshipEdgeId and relationshipObject (the update's JSON). Removed relationships and blocks on create propagate at once, as in 3.4a TSK-03 Deleting a classification that propagates fails with DELETE_TAG_PROPAGATION_NOT_ALLOWED (instance GUID, entity GUID) while a PENDING task names them both TSK-04 Tasks run after the request, oldest first, each once at a time (DD-080). ADD propagates the classification to the entity and the entities it reaches from it, the relationship excluded and its blocks counted (propagateClassification); DELETE removes every propagation of it and removes the instance when no entity lists it (deleteClassificationPropagation); RELATIONSHIP_UPDATE updates the relationship's propagation as PRO-05 does with the given relationship. An ADD whose entity or classification is gone, a DELETE whose classification is gone, and a RELATIONSHIP_UPDATE whose relationship is gone do nothing TSK-05 A task that runs to its end is removed, and so is its GUID from pendingTasks, in the task's write. One that fails is PENDING again with its attemptCount one higher and its errorMessage, FAILED from the third attempt, and is no longer listed in pendingTasks either; one with three attempts is not run TSK-06 GET admin/tasks answers every task, oldest first, or those of the given guids that exist, in their order; DELETE admin/tasks removes those of the given guids, and answers 204 TSK-07 An entity reads pendingTasks, the GUIDs of its tasks, when it has any TSK-08 With tasks disabled, propagation happens within the request, as 3.4a says, and no task is recorded

items.title: 3.5b Classification audit
items.text:
• Status: in progress
  • Pull request: #136
  • Records: DD-085, DD-086, DV-41, DV-42; relies on DD-074, DD-077, DD-079, DD-082 to DD-084

The second part of increment 3.5 (DD-082): audit events for classifications attached, changed and removed, and for those propagated or no longer propagated, recorded after the change as 3.5a's entity events are; and GET v2/entity/bulk/headers, which lists the entities whose classifications changed since a time (DD-074).

items.title: Scope
items.text:
Endpoint Takes Answers GET /api/atlas/v2/entity/bulk/headers?tagUpdateStartTime=<ms> the start, in ms AtlasEntityHeaders

In aurelius-atlas-core, the change notifier and the audit listener gain the classification methods of AtlasEntityChangeNotifier and EntityAuditListenerV2; TagPropagation records the propagations a request added and removed, as Atlas's RequestContext does (DD-086). The classification operations, the entity writer, the relationship store and the propagation tasks tell the notifier (DD-085). classification_associator gains ClassificationRetriever (ClassificationAssociator.Retriever); the audit repository finds the entities with classification events in a time range. The server's routes/entity answers bulk/headers.

items.title: Semantics
items.text: Id Rule CAU-01 A classification event names the entity and writes the classification as read (DV-42): on its own entity CLASSIFICATION_ADD Added classification: <JSON>, CLASSIFICATION_UPDATE Updated classification: <JSON>, CLASSIFICATION_DELETE Deleted classification: <name>; on another entity PROPAGATED_CLASSIFICATION_ADD Added propagated classification: <JSON>, PROPAGATED_CLASSIFICATION_UPDATE Updated propagated classification: <JSON>, PROPAGATED_CLASSIFICATION_DELETE Deleted propagated classification: <name> CAU-02 Adding classifications to an entity (also by bulk/classification, bulk/setClassifications and an entity create) records, per classification in the request's order, an add on its entity and on each entity it was propagated to within the request (none while tasks are enabled). An entity create records them before its entity events CAU-03 Updating classifications records, on the entity, on the entities the updated classifications are propagated to when their attributes, validity periods or removePropagationsOnEntityDelete changed, and on those propagate turned on reached, each ACTIVE, one update event per updated classification; on another entity an update is an add when the request propagated it there, a delete when it removed it. Those propagate turned off removed it from then record a delete CAU-04 Deleting a classification records a delete on each entity its propagation was removed from within the request, then on its entity. Removing a propagated classification of a deleted entity (associatedEntityGuid) records nothing CAU-05 After an entity write or delete, and after a relationship is created, updated or deleted, each entity the request propagated a classification to records an add, and each it removed one from a delete, unless the request deleted it (notifyPropagatedEntities); an add CAU-02 recorded is recorded again, as Atlas does CAU-06 A propagation task records its own changes: ADD an add on each entity it propagated to, DELETE a delete on each it removed the classification from, RELATIONSHIP_UPDATE as CAU-05 CAU-07 bulk/headers answers, in guidHeaderMap, the header with classifications of each entity with a CLASSIFICATION_ADD, CLASSIFICATION_UPDATE or CLASSIFICATION_DELETE event (propagated ones not counted) from tagUpdateStartTime (default 0) to now, both included; entities that can no longer be read are left out. A start after now fails with BAD_REQUEST fromTimestamp should be less than toTimestamp CAU-08 A tagUpdateStartTime that is no Java long fails with BAD_REQUEST (DV-41)

items.title: Java origin

items.text:
• Status: in progress

  • Records: DD-082 to DD-084, DV-39, DV-40; relies on DD-049, DD-059

The first part of increment 3.5 (DD-082): an audit event for each entity a write, delete or purge creates, changes, deletes or purges, kept in an index of its own, and Atlas's GET v2/entity/{guid}/audit to read them, which is what the dashboards' audit tab calls. 3.5b adds the classification events and bulk/headers.

items.title: Scope
items.text:
Endpoint Takes Answers GET /api/atlas/v2/entity/{guid}/audit startKey, auditAction, count, offset, sortBy, sortOrder a list of EntityAuditEventV2

In aurelius-atlas-model, audit (EntityAuditEventV2, EntityAuditActionV2). In aurelius-atlas-core, entity_change_notifier (EntityChangeNotifier: Atlas's AtlasEntityChangeNotifier), entity_audit_listener (EntityAuditListener: EntityAuditListenerV2) and entity_audit_repository (EntityAuditRepository and its Elasticsearch implementation: HBaseBasedAuditRepository); testing/memory.py gains InMemoryEntityAuditRepository. The entity writer tells the notifier what it changed (DD-084). The server's routes/entity answers the endpoint.

Not in scope:

Not delivered here Delivered by Classification and propagated classification events; bulk/headers (DD-074) 3.5b Term, label, business and custom attribute events (TERM_*, LABEL_*, *_ATTRIBUTE_UPDATE) 5.2, 5.3 Import events (ENTITY_IMPORT_*) 6.3 admin/audits (AtlasAuditService), audit age-out (AtlasAuditReductionService) –

items.title: Semantics
items.text: Id Rule AUD-01 EntityAuditEventV2 reads and writes entityId, timestamp (epoch milliseconds), user, action, details, eventKey, entity and type, nulls included. Listed events have no entity and no type, as Atlas does not keep the entity definition (atlas.audit.persistEntityDefinition=false) AUD-02 After a write, delete or purge has committed, its response's entities are recorded (onEntitiesMutated): first pruneResponse takes from the created, updated and partially updated entities those DELETED, and from each list those a later kind names (purged over deleted, created, updated, partially updated; deleted over created, updated, partially updated; created over updated, partially updated; updated over partially updated); then the created, updated, partially updated, deleted and purged entities are recorded in that order, those of internal types left out AUD-03 A created entity records ENTITY_CREATE with the details Created: <JSON>, the JSON of the entity as read after the write without relationship attributes; an updated or partially updated one ENTITY_UPDATE with Updated: <JSON>, or ENTITY_CREATE with Created: <JSON> when it is incomplete and its create and update times are the same; a deleted one ENTITY_DELETE with Deleted entity; a purged one ENTITY_PURGE with Purged: <JSON>, the JSON of an entity made from its header (its type name, attributes, GUID, status, classifications and meanings, isProxy and isIncomplete false, provenanceType 0) AUD-04 Details longer than 1,048,576 UTF-8 bytes are written again without the entity's attributes and relationship attributes; still longer, with an entity of only its GUID, type name, create and update times and users, status and version AUD-05 An event's timestamp is the time it is recorded, its user the request's, and its eventKey <entityId>:<timestamp>:<index>:<now>, index its position among the events of its kind of that request (DD-083) AUD-06 GET {guid}/audit needs an entity with the GUID, in any state, or an ENTITY_PURGE event of it; else it fails with INSTANCE_GUID_NOT_FOUND AUD-07 With sortBy or an offset above -1, every event of the entity (of auditAction when given) is sorted by user or action (ignoring case, then by timestamp) or else by timestamp, the whole order reversed when sortOrder is desc in any case, events otherwise in the newest-key-first order; the answer is count events from offset (a negative offset reads as 0, a negative count as 100, a count of 0 as all) AUD-08 Otherwise the events of the entity are answered newest key first (DD-083), from startKey on, that key included, when given; only those of auditAction when given; at most count (default 100), all for -1, none for any other negative count AUD-09 auditAction is an action's name or TAG_ADD, TAG_DELETE, TAG_UPDATE (Atlas's fromString; CUSTOM_ATTRIBUTE_UPDATE is not among them); count a Java short, offset an int. A value that is none of these fails with BAD_REQUEST (DV-39)

items.title: 4.1b Classification search
items.text:
• Status: in progress
  • Pull request: #142
  • Records: DD-090, DV-47; ends the classification part of DV-46; relies on DD-070, DD-087 to DD-089

The second part of increment 4.1 (DD-087): basic search by classification and tagFilters, as Atlas's ClassificationSearchProcessor and the classification filter of EntitySearchProcessor answer it, and entity filters on __classificationNames and __propagatedClassificationNames.

items.title: Scope
items.text: POST and GET /api/atlas/v2/search/basic take classification, and POST also tagFilters and includeSubClassifications. In aurelius-atlas-core, classification_search_processor (ClassificationSearchProcessor) finds the classification instances a search names (DD-090); search_context, entity_search_processor and discovery_service take them; search_fields adds the classification names of an entity. The free-text query and termName stay refused until 4.2 and 5.2 (DV-46).

items.title: Semantics
items.text: Id Rule CSR-01 classification is a comma-separated list of classification type names, names with *, *, _CLASSIFIED, _NOT_CLASSIFIED and _ALL_CLASSIFICATION_TYPES; other unknown names are left out, and when none is left the search fails with UNKNOWN_CLASSIFICATION naming the whole list. _NOT_CLASSIFIED among them stands for entities without classifications; else *, _CLASSIFIED or _ALL_CLASSIFICATION_TYPES for entities with any CSR-02 An entity matches the classification types when it lists, attached or propagated, an instance of one of them or, with includeSubClassifications (the default), of a sub type. With a name containing *, an entity matches when one of its classifications' type names matches one of the names, * standing for any characters, ignoring case (DV-47) CSR-03 tagFilters are filters as SRC-05 and SRC-06 state them, on the attributes (system attributes such as __entityStatus included) of every classification type given, else the search fails with UNKNOWN_ATTRIBUTE naming the type (_ALL_CLASSIFICATION_TYPES for any); with a name containing * other than * itself they fail with BAD_REQUEST TagFilters specified with wildcard tag name. An entity matches when one of the instances it lists matches them CSR-04 With typeName too, an entity must match both, and the entity filters; without, entities of every type match. excludeDeletedEntities applies as in SRC-07. With tagFilters, approximateCount is -1, as Atlas's classification processor answers it; sortBy orders only with typeName CSR-05 An entity's __classificationNames are the type names of the classifications attached to it, __propagatedClassificationNames those propagated to it, each as \|a\|b\|, and entity filters match them as SRC-06 states

items.title: 4.1a Entity search
items.text:
• Status: in progress
  • Pull request: #140
  • Records: DD-087 to DD-089, DV-43 to DV-46; relies on DD-043, DD-055

The first part of increment 4.1 (DD-087): basic search for entities by type, attribute filters, state, sort and paging, as Atlas's EntityDiscoveryService.searchWithParameters answers it with an EntitySearchProcessor. Entity attributes are indexed for it in typed search fields named after the type that defines them (DD-088). 4.1b adds classification search.

items.title: Scope
items.text:
Endpoint Takes Answers POST /api/atlas/v2/search/basic SearchParameters AtlasSearchResult GET /api/atlas/v2/search/basic typeName, sortBy, sortOrder, excludeDeletedEntities, limit, offset, marker AtlasSearchResult GET /api/atlas/v2/search/attribute attrName, attrValuePrefix, typeName, limit, offset AtlasSearchResult

In aurelius-atlas-model, discovery (SearchParameters, FilterCriteria, AtlasSearchResult). In aurelius-atlas-core, search_fields (the typed search fields of an entity, Atlas's vertex property keys), search_context (SearchContext), entity_search_processor (EntitySearchProcessor, the Elasticsearch query) and discovery_service (EntityDiscoveryService.searchWithParameters). The server's routes/discovery (DiscoveryREST) answers the endpoints.

Not in scope:

Not delivered here Delivered by classification, tagFilters, __classificationNames filters (DV-46 until then) 4.1b query (free text), search/fulltext, search/quick, search/suggestions 4.2 search/dsl 4.4 search/saved 4.5 termName 5.2 relationshipName, relationshipFilters, search/relationship, search/relations, search downloads –

items.title: Semantics
items.text: Id Rule SRC-01 SearchParameters, FilterCriteria and AtlasSearchResult read and write Atlas's fields, nulls left out; includeSubTypes and includeSubClassifications default to true, the other flags to false, approximateCount to -1. An operator reads any of its symbols (=, eq; startsWith, STARTSWITH, begins_with, …) and writes its first; an unknown symbol reads as none. sortOrder is ASCENDING or DESCENDING SRC-02 POST basic fails with BAD_REQUEST for a negative limit or offset (Limit/offset should be non-negative), for entityFilters without typeName (EntityFilters specified without Type name), for tagFilters without classification (TagFilters specified without tag name); with INVALID_SEARCH_PARAMS when none of typeName, classification, query and termName is given; with INVALID_QUERY_PARAM_LENGTH for a typeName, classification or sortBy over 4,096 characters SRC-03 typeName is a comma-separated list of entity type names and _ALL_ENTITY_TYPES; unknown names are left out, and when none is known the search fails with UNKNOWN_TYPENAME naming the whole list. _ALL_ENTITY_TYPES stands for every entity; otherwise the types and, with includeSubTypes, their sub types SRC-04 Each attribute an entity filter names, and sortBy, must be an attribute (a system attribute such as __guid included) of every type given, else the search fails with UNKNOWN_ATTRIBUTE naming it and the type (_ALL_ENTITY_TYPES for all). Each name in attributes must be an attribute or relationship attribute of the first type given, else UNKNOWN_ATTRIBUTE SRC-05 A filter is a criterion with a condition (AND, OR) over its criterion, or one on attributeName with an operator and an attributeValue, read as the attribute's type: LT, LTE, GT, GTE, EQ compare (strings by code point, case-sensitive), NEQ matches also entities without a value; STARTS_WITH, ENDS_WITH, CONTAINS, LIKE (DV-43) and NOT_CONTAINS test strings case-sensitively, and CONTAINS/NOT_CONTAINS an array's elements; IS_NULL, NOT_NULL and NOT_EMPTY test the value's presence; IN matches nothing; CONTAINS_ANY, CONTAINS_ALL and an unknown operator restrict nothing. A criterion on an attribute several types define matches any of them SRC-06 TIME_RANGE on a date or long takes <start>,<end> in epoch milliseconds, both included, or TODAY, YESTERDAY, LAST_7_DAYS, LAST_30_DAYS, THIS_MONTH, LAST_MONTH, THIS_QUARTER, LAST_QUARTER, LAST_3_MONTHS, LAST_6_MONTHS, LAST_12_MONTHS, THIS_YEAR, LAST_YEAR, computed as processDateRange does in UTC (DV-44). __isIncomplete EQ 0 or false, and NEQ 1, match complete entities; __labels and __customAttributes EQ, NEQ, STARTS_WITH and ENDS_WITH match one element (key=value for custom attributes) SRC-07 With excludeDeletedEntities only ACTIVE entities match. Matching entities are ordered by sortBy of the first type given (sortOrder ASCENDING by default, entities without a value last), else by creation time and GUID (DD-089); limit is 1 to 10,000, else 100, offset at least 0, and the answer's searchParameters show them so SRC-08 marker pages instead of offset: * starts, and nextMarker is the marker of the next page, -1 after the last. A marker with an offset above 0 fails with BAD_REQUEST Marker can be used only if offset=0., a marker that is not one of this search's with Invalid marker! (DV-45) SRC-09 The answer is queryType BASIC, the searchParameters, the entities' headers, their attributes being the header attributes, the requested attributes and the attributes the entity filters name, with their classifications when includeClassificationAttributes, and approximateCount, the number of matching entities. A requested attribute that refers to entities adds their headers to referredEntities. No match leaves entities out SRC-10 With excludeHeaderAttributes, attributes given and none of them a relationship attribute, the answer has, instead of entities, attributes: their names and, per entity, the values of the first type's attributes, "" for none SRC-11 GET basic searches with its query parameters, unvalidated; excludeDeletedEntities is true only for true in any case. GET attribute fails with INVALID_PARAMETERS attrName : <name>, attrValue: <value> for attribute search. without both, and searches for attrValuePrefix with STARTS_WITH on attrName, by default qualifiedName, or name where the type has no qualifiedName, validated as POST basic. A limit, offset or sortOrder that is no value of its type fails with BAD_REQUEST (DV-39)

items.text: DV-43: Atlas applies LIKE as its in-memory contains, and its index or graph query besides as a pattern; Aurelius Atlas applies the contains alone. DV-44: named time ranges are computed in UTC, where Atlas uses the server's time zone. DV-45: a marker encodes the search's hash and offset as Atlas's does, but with a hash of Aurelius Atlas's own, so Atlas's markers are not valid here.
