items.title: 4.2a Free text
items.text:
• Status: in progress
  • Pull request: #145
  • Records: DD-091, DD-092, DV-48, DV-49; ends the query part of DV-46; relies on DD-087 to DD-090

The first part of increment 4.2 (DD-091): free text, as Atlas's FreeTextSearchProcessor answers basic search's query through its Solr /freetext handler, weighted by the attributes' searchWeight, and GET v2/search/fulltext. 4.2b adds quick search with its facets and suggestions.

items.title: Scope
items.text:
Endpoint Takes Answers POST/GET /api/atlas/v2/search/basic query, with the other parameters of 4.1 AtlasSearchResult GET /api/atlas/v2/search/fulltext query, excludeDeletedEntities, limit, offset AtlasSearchResult of FULL_TEXT

In aurelius-atlas-core, free_text (the searchable text of the registry, Atlas's SolrIndexHelper weights, and the text a query asks for), search_fields (an entity's classification text), and the search query, processors and discovery service, which take the text. The server's routes/discovery answers fulltext.

Not in scope:

Not delivered here Delivered by GET/POST search/quick with facets, GET search/suggestions 4.2b Business metadata attributes in free text 5.3

items.title: Semantics
items.text: Id Rule FTX-01 A query longer than 4,096 characters fails with INVALID_QUERY_LENGTH. Basic search strips * from both ends of the query and uses the result when it holds a tokenising character (any but letters, digits and _; ., : and ' only next to a non-letter; CJK characters), else the query as given FTX-02 An entity matches a query when one of its words, in any case, matches one of the query's words, a word ending in * matching every word it begins (DV-48). Its searchable text is the string attributes of the non-internal entity types, weighted by their searchWeight (1 to 10, else 3), its classification text (10), labels (10), custom attributes (3) and type name (1) FTX-03 An entity's classification text is, for each classification it lists, attached or propagated, the type name and the values of its attributes FTX-04 With a query, basic search finds the entities matching it that also match the types, classifications and filters; without sortBy, the best match first, by the weights of FTX-02 FTX-05 GET fulltext answers queryType FULL_TEXT, queryText, and fullTextResult: for each entity matching the query, best first, its header and score, at most limit (normalised as SRC-07), offset not used; with excludeDeletedEntities, deleted ones left out. approximateCount counts every matching entity, deleted ones too (DV-49)

items.title: 7.0 Webapp foundation (umbrella)
items.text:
• Status: planned
  • Pull request: –
  • Records: ADR 053; DD-126 to DD-131

items.title: Scope
items.text:
This is an umbrella, not a buildable increment: it fixes the shape of the 7.x track and the rules every slice in it obeys. Each 7.x slice is specified and delivered in its own pull request (ADR 051).

The 7.x track rewrites the Aurelius Atlas web interface in this workspace as apps/aurelius-atlas-webapp (ADR 053). The starting material is apps/atlas plus the 20 @models4insight/* libraries of the aureliusenterprise/aurelius repository (Angular 17.3, 62 NgModules, a custom Redux wrapper).

What every slice in this track must satisfy, stated once here and referenced by each increment's Acceptance:

  • No NgModule in new code: standalone components, bootstrapApplication, zoneless change detection. The workspace has no @angular/platform-browser-dynamic to fall back on.
  • State is signals: signal() and computed(), following the signal-service pattern of aurelius-atlas-frontend-example. A slice that carries a BehaviorSubject store forward has not delivered its slice (ADR 053 R3).
  • Presentational components are dumb and shared: input()/output() only, no side-effect services, living in aurelius-atlas-ui, with a story. Brand tokens from @aurelius/atlas-brand, never redefined colours (ADR 053 R7).
  • Tests come with the slice: Vitest for logic, one Playwright scenario for the capability, the Aurelius Jest assertions re-expressed not dropped (ADR 053 R5). Coverage gates hold.
  • Localisation is built-in @angular/localize with XLIFF, not ngx-translate.
  • No hard-coded endpoints: runtime AppConfig from /config.json, base URL supplied by aurelius-atlas-data-access.

items.title: The slices, in build order
items.text:
Ordered so that a slice depends only on slices before it. Slices 7.1–7.2 need no catalogue API, which is what makes 7.1 the safe place to stand up the project.

# Slice Depends on 7.1 Shell and localisation: project, bootstrap, router, i18n bridge, OTel telemetry – 7.2 Design system: legacy shared components → aurelius-atlas-ui dumb components + stories 7.1 7.3 API client: libs/atlas/api (65 files) → aurelius-atlas-data-access, Keycloak auth wiring 7.1 7.4 Search: query and results, the first slice with real data 7.2, 7.3 7.5 Browse: domain browse, card grids 7.4 7.6 Entity details: header, attributes, relationships, lineage view 7.4 7.7 Create and edit entity: forms, validation 7.4, 7.6 7.8 Governance quality, classifications, domains 7.6 7.9 Delete, audit, and the remaining detail cards 7.6 7.10 Serving, and retirement of the example app 7.1 – 7.9

items.title: Not in scope
items.text: Not delivered here Delivered by Any catalogue REST endpoint the server does not answer yet increments 1.x – 6.x Authentication and authorisation semantics 6.1, 6.2 (wired here, not built) Apache Atlas dashboardv2 / dashboardv3 changes not planned (ADR 046, DD-001) Migration of a live Aurelius deployment not planned

items.title: Semantics
items.text:
The umbrella's own rules; the slice rules (SHL-NN, and each later prefix) live in their increment.

Id Rule WBP-01 aurelius-atlas-webapp builds in this workspace on the workspace's Angular, Nx, and TypeScript, with no dependency on the Aurelius repository WBP-02 No NgModule-decorated class, and no @models4insight/* import, exists in aurelius-atlas-webapp or in the Angular libraries it consumes WBP-03 No BehaviorSubject/Subject-owned application state exists in the webapp: state is a signal, derived state a computed WBP-04 A presentational component in aurelius-atlas-ui declares only input()/output() (or model()), injects no service with side effects, and has a story WBP-05 Every user-visible string is a localisation unit: no literal prose reaches a template, and the nl-NL XLIFF catalogues the whole surface in scope WBP-06 The Aurelius app keeps building and serving in its own repository throughout; the port adds nothing to it WBP-07 The Apache Atlas dashboards keep being served and keep passing their parity checks; the 7.x track changes nothing in them

items.title: Java origin
items.text:
None. The 7.x track ports an Angular front end written by Aurelius, not Apache Atlas code, so there is no release-2.4.0 class to cite and ADR 052's scenario format does not apply. The origin is the Aurelius source, cited by path:

  • apps/atlas/src/app/ — the screens: search/{browse,results,details,create-entity,edit-entity, meta,components,services,utils}, dashboards/{domains,mockups}
  • libs/atlas/api/src/ — the Atlas REST client: atlas, elastic, gov-quality, types
  • libs/redux/src/ — the custom store replaced by signals
  • libs/core/src/lib/core.ts — Core.imports, the module graph being dissolved
  • libs/{components,utils,shell,repository,directives,permissions,authentication,i18n} — shared code

items.title: Deviations
items.text: • DV-64: Aurelius Atlas serves a web interface of its own design once 7.10 lands, where Apache Atlas 2.4.0 serves its two dashboards. The REST contract is unaffected; the parity harness keeps reading the Atlas dashboards as the reference. Added to Deviations.

items.title: Acceptance
items.text:
The umbrella is accepted when 7.1 lands and demonstrates the shape, and each slice thereafter carries its own acceptance in its specification. Checks that every slice must pass:

nx build aurelius-atlas-webapp
nx test aurelius-atlas-webapp -c ci
nx test aurelius-atlas-ui -c ci
nx lint aurelius-atlas-webapp
nx e2e aurelius-atlas-webapp

WBP-02 and WBP-03 are checked by grep over the tree as well as by review, so a NgModule, a @models4insight import, or a state-owning Subject cannot arrive unnoticed.

items.title: 7.1 Webapp shell and localisation
items.text:
• Status: in progress
  • Pull request: #98
  • Records: ADR 053; DD-126, DD-127, DD-128, DD-129, DD-133; relies on ADR 007, ADR 018, DD-019

Part of the 7.0 umbrella, whose rules WBP-01 to WBP-07 this slice inherits and its Acceptance repeats.

items.title: Scope
items.text:
Stand up apps/aurelius-atlas-webapp as a real Angular 22 application in this workspace, and port the application shell — the part of the Aurelius interface that needs no catalogue API.

The Aurelius shell is genuinely thin, which is why it is first: app.component.html is a bare <router-outlet>, app.component.ts is 8 lines, and the routing module is 26. The Shell component of libs/shell is not part of the shell — it is applied by search-routing.module.ts and dashboard-routing.module.ts, so it arrives with 7.4 and 7.5.

  • apps/aurelius-atlas-webapp: project, main.ts with bootstrapApplication, app.config.ts with zoneless change detection and runtime config, routes.ts, the root component, global styles, Dockerfile, and Playwright e2e.
  • Localisation bridge: the Aurelius flat-JSON dictionaries (105 keys, en-US and nl-NL) become XLIFF catalogues under the built-in @angular/localize, and nx extract-i18n maintains them.
  • A placeholder route surface, so the router, the locale switch, and the build are all real and testable before any feature exists.

Not in scope:

Not delivered here Delivered by The Shell chrome (nav bar, breadcrumbs, app bar) 7.4 (search), 7.5 (browse) Any screen: browse, search results, entity details, editor 7.4 – 7.9 The Atlas REST client, and every call to it 7.3 Shared presentational components 7.2 Keycloak sign-in enforced on routes 7.3, which owns the auth wiring; 6.1 the semantics

items.title: Semantics
items.text:
Id Rule SHL-01 The application bootstraps with bootstrapApplication and provideZonelessChangeDetection, and declares no NgModule SHL-02 Bootstrap reads /config.json and validates it into the typed AppConfig; a missing, unreachable, or malformed file throws at bootstrap SHL-03 The root component renders a router outlet and nothing else, as the Aurelius root does SHL-04 GET /search/browse renders the browse placeholder, the Aurelius default destination SHL-05 An unknown path redirects to the default destination, matching the Aurelius ** fallback (one hop, DD-132) SHL-06 Scroll position is restored on browser back and forward, as scrollPositionRestoration: 'enabled' does in Aurelius SHL-07 The app is served in en-US and nl-NL; a build localises both, and nx extract-i18n regenerates the template catalogue SHL-08 Every one of the 105 Aurelius dictionary keys is present in the en-US catalogue with its Aurelius English text, and in the nl-NL catalogue with its Aurelius Dutch text SHL-09 No component in the webapp imports @ngx-translate/*, and no template uses the translate pipe SHL-10 No setting is read from a build-time environment file: base URLs, client ids, and export endpoints come from AppConfig SHL-11 The built image serves the app over TLS on 8080, proxies /api/ and /otel/ as the example app's nginx config does, and its CSP keeps connect-src 'self' SHL-12 A Playwright scenario loads the app in each of chromium, firefox, and webkit, reaches the browse placeholder, and switches locale SHL-13 Every signal, service, and pure function the slice adds has a Vitest test naming it, and the coverage gate for the app holds SHL-14 The app exports traces and Core Web Vitals metrics to the otelExporterUrl through aurelius-atlas-observability, records uncaught errors as span events, and propagates traceparent on HTTP calls (DD-129)

SHL-01 and SHL-10 are the point of the slice: they make the project real on this workspace's rules before any feature code arrives, so no later slice inherits a legacy scaffold.

SHL-08 keeps the Aurelius dictionary complete rather than migrating the keys a screen happens to use. A partial dictionary makes each later slice responsible for adding strings, and the gaps surface as missing translations in Dutch months later (DD-128).

items.title: Aurelius origin
items.text:
Cited by path in aureliusenterprise/aurelius at the cloned commit, so a reviewer can compare:

Aurelius Becomes apps/atlas/src/main.ts (platformBrowserDynamic().bootstrapModule) src/main.ts (bootstrapApplication) apps/atlas/src/app/app.module.ts src/app/app.config.ts providers; Core.imports is dissolved, not ported apps/atlas/src/app/app-routing.module.ts src/app/routes.ts apps/atlas/src/app/app.component.{ts,html,scss} src/app/app.component.* apps/atlas/src/environments/environment.ts src/app/config.ts + runtime /config.json apps/atlas/src/translations/{en-US,nl-NL}.json src/locale/messages{,.nl-NL}.xlf apps/atlas/src/styles.scss (and the @models4insight/styles it uses) src/styles.scss on @aurelius/atlas-brand tokens libs/i18n (I18nService, I18nModule.forRoot) @angular/localize + a locale service following the example app apps/atlas/proxy.conf.json, project.json targets the workspace's proxy.conf.json + inferred targets

@models4insight/google-analytics and the ClickstreamModule of libs/services/clickstream are dropped, not ported: the workspace observes itself through OpenTelemetry (ADR 016) and aurelius-atlas-observability, and a second telemetry path to a third-party analytics host would add an egress the CSP is built to refuse (DD-129).

items.title: Deviations
items.text: None against Apache Atlas: the Aurelius interface is Aurelius's own, and the Atlas dashboards are untouched (WBP-07). Against the Aurelius product, the two intended differences are recorded in design-log: telemetry goes to OpenTelemetry instead of Google Analytics (DD-129), and localisation moves from a TranslateService abstraction to the built-in one (DD-128).

items.title: Acceptance
items.text:
• apps/aurelius-atlas-webapp/tests (co-located .spec.ts, Vitest) — config parsing and the failure modes of SHL-02, the metrics-endpoint derivation of SHL-14; the route table of SHL-04, SHL-05, SHL-06; the root component of SHL-03; the locale service of SHL-07. SHL-13.
  • apps/aurelius-atlas-webapp/e2e/ — pytest + Playwright against the built image: SHL-12, plus SHL-11's TLS and proxy paths and the CSP check.
  • scripts/check-webapp-purity.sh (or an ESLint rule set) — WBP-02, SHL-01, SHL-09, SHL-10: greps the tree for @NgModule, platformBrowserDynamic, @models4insight/, @ngx-translate/, environment, and a state-owning new BehaviorSubject outside RxJS interop. Run in CI and by nx run aurelius-atlas-webapp:check-purity.
  • Dictionary completeness for SHL-08 — a Vitest test that loads the Aurelius JSON from the cloned reference checkout path recorded in the test, and asserts each key and value appears in both catalogues. Reference JSON is vendored into tests/fixtures/ (DD-128), so the test runs offline.
  • Umbrella checks: nx build, nx test -c ci, nx lint, nx e2e for the app.

items.title: Definition of done, in order
items.text:
1. nx serve aurelius-atlas-webapp starts and the app loads at /search/browse in a browser, zoneless, with no NgModule in the tree.
  2. The purity check passes and is wired into CI.
  3. Both locales build; the 105 keys are proven present in both.
  4. The e2e scenario passes in all three browsers against the built image.
  5. apps/aurelius-atlas-webapp/AGENTS.md and README.md describe the app and its removal, per ADR 003.

items.title: 7.11 Shell chrome
items.text:
• Status: in progress
  • Pull request: #102
  • Records: ADR 053; DD-145 (supersedes the Shell half of DD-143); relies on ADR 007, ADR 018, DD-128, DD-130, DD-135, DD-136, DD-141, SHL rules (7.1), UIC rules (7.2)

Part of the 7.0 umbrella, whose rules WBP-01 to WBP-07 this slice inherits and its Acceptance repeats.

items.title: Scope
items.text:
Port the Aurelius application chrome — the libs/shell header and footer that wrap every screen — onto the root component, replacing the 7.1 bare outlet:

  • the navbar (aurelius-atlas-ui-header, 7.2): app name to /search/browse, and on the right the Documentation link, the language dropdown, and the account dropdown
  • the footer: the Aurelius copyright line, app name, and version
  • the session chrome over Keycloak: the signed-in identity, Keycloak's account console, and logout (the bearer-token plumbing itself is 7.3, done)

The chrome is search-free: the legacy navbar's centrepiece (the global search bar inside the search route chrome) and the primary-nav buttons stay with the search slice (7.4, on hold — DD-140). What is ported here is the frame every Aurelius screen wears, proven against the landing page (7.5).

Explicitly not delivered here, with the increment that will:

Deferred Lands with Why Global search bar, primary-nav route buttons Search slice (7.4, gated by server 4.1/2.3, DD-140) Search navigation, on hold per the user's 2026-10-20 direction PWA install/update buttons (shell.header.install, .update) – (not planned) Aurelius ships a service worker (@angular/pwa) and its update prompt; the port ships no service worker — chrome with no SW Services dropdown (shell.header.services) – (not planned) Links to Models4Insight platform apps (Platform, Data2Model, Analytics) that are not part of Aurelius Atlas (standalone) Loading bar and pipeline progress (shell sticky block) With the slices that need them The loading bar tracks router navigation and the pipeline tracks import jobs; the landing slice has neither to show Language switch via ngx-translate runtime swap – (superseded) The locale builds are separate bundles (DD-128): switching is a full-page navigation into the locale tree the image serves

items.title: Semantics
items.text:
Each rule the behaviour must obey, in plain words, with an id that tests name (@pytest.mark.covers(..., rules=["SHC-NN"]); TS/e2e tests name the id in the test title).

Id Rule SHC-01 The root component is the shell: aurelius-atlas-ui-header above the router outlet, the footer below it (the Aurelius root renders <models4insight-shell>, which wraps its router-outlet in exactly this chrome — SHL-03's "bare outlet" reading lands here) SHC-02 The navbar's brand is the app name from the runtime config, linking to /search/browse (the Aurelius logo is a product asset not vendored to this workspace; the 7.2 header's name fallback is the brand). navbar-start is empty: Aurelius's only primary-nav item (the search route) is hidden, so the legacy navbar renders no nav buttons for this app SHC-03 The navbar end carries the Aurelius Documentation link (shell.header.documentation, the Aurelius Atlas documentation site, target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer") SHC-04 The language dropdown shows shell.header.language with the active locale (from the document's lang), and lists en-US and nl-NL; choosing one is a full-page navigation to /<locale>/<current path with any locale prefix stripped> — the locale builds are separate bundles (DD-128), and the image serves the locale tree (SHL-05's nginx) SHC-05 The account dropdown shows shell.header.welcome with the signed-in identity (preferred_username, falling back to email, read from the Keycloak token); its items are shell.header.security (opens Keycloak's account console) and shell.header.logout (ends the Keycloak session). No login button is ported: every route sits behind the root guard (APC-05), so the legacy logged-out navbar is unreachable SHC-06 The footer renders the shell.footer.copyright label, a copyright icon, the copyright year, the app name, and the app version — the Aurelius footer anatomy — with every value from the runtime config (/config.json), not an environment.ts (SHL-10, DD-130) SHC-07 Every chrome string carries its legacy libs/shell dictionary key as its i18n id (@@shell.header.*, @@shell.footer.*); the shell dictionaries (en, nl) are vendored as fixtures and bridged into the XLIFF catalogues beside the app and components dictionaries (SHL-08, UIC-04's category), and the completeness spec proves both locales SHC-08 The chrome is zoneless/Angular-idiom (standalone, OnPush, signals, inject()): the identity is a signal read from the Keycloak client at construction (the guard has resolved before any render), session actions call the Keycloak client directly, no store, no BehaviorSubject (DD-135, purity gate). The client is the Keycloak (keycloak-js) instance provideKeycloak registers — keycloak-angular v21's KeycloakService is the deprecated pre-v19 class and is not provided by it SHC-09 e2e (authenticated, chromium/firefox/webkit): the navbar shows the welcome line with the signed-in user (aurelius-writer); the language dropdown's nl-NL item navigates the page into the Dutch build (a real click, not a hand-written URL — the locale-tree channel proven end to end); the footer shows copyright year, app name, and version; the Documentation link points at the Aurelius docs with rel="noopener noreferrer"

items.title: Aurelius origin
items.text:
The Aurelius 17 app (.scratch/aurelius, commit pinned by 7-0), libs/shell/src/lib/:

  • shell.component.{ts,html} — the chrome layout (header, outlet, footer; the sticky loading/pipeline block is not ported)
  • header/header.component.{ts,html} — the navbar: brand, nav buttons (deferred), documentation, language dropdown, account dropdown, services/install/update (not planned); the session actions come from libs/authentication, here from Keycloak directly (DD-141)
  • footer/footer.component.{ts,html} — copyright icon, app name, version
  • shell-config.service.ts — the shell block of environments/environment.ts (appName, appCopyright, appLogoPath, standalone): its role moves to /config.json (SHL-10); standalone/hideDocumentation are config knobs Aurelius never flipped for atlas — not ported as flags, the atlas choices are baked (documentation shown, services hidden)
  • src/translations/{en-US,nl-NL}.json — the chrome strings (SHC-07)

items.title: Deviations
items.text:
Against Apache Atlas: none — this is an Aurelius product frame, Atlas has no UI.

Against the Aurelius product, recorded in design-log:

  • DD-145: the navbar is static, not is-fixed-top (the legacy pinned-to-top bar is cosmetic; the port keeps the Bulma navbar in flow), the login button is not ported (SHC-05), the language switch navigates (SHC-04), and the root composes the chrome directly — the Aurelius Shell module, its service (token-refresh-on-focus — keycloak-angular owns refresh, DD-141) and its reusable-route strategy are not ported (SHC-01, DD-135).

items.title: Acceptance
items.text:
• Vitest (nx test aurelius-atlas-webapp -c ci):
    • app.component.spec.ts — root renders header, outlet, footer (SHC-01); the old "bare outlet" spec is superseded here
    • shell/header.component.spec.ts — brand from config (SHC-02), documentation link (SHC-03), language items and computed locale hrefs (SHC-04), welcome line, Account-security and Logout actions on the Keycloak client (SHC-05), strings render from the bridge keys (SHC-07)
    • shell/footer.component.spec.ts — copyright/appName/version from AppConfig (SHC-06)
    • session.service.spec.ts — identity from the token, fallback to e-mail (SHC-08)
    • config.spec.ts — the new appName/appCopyright/appVersion fields validate and fail loudly when missing (SHL-02)
    • i18n-completeness.spec.ts — the shell fixtures join the parity check (SHC-07)
  • e2e (nx e2e aurelius-atlas-webapp): the SHC-09 scenarios; the 7.1/7.5 scenarios stay green (the landing keeps its anchors inside the new frame)
  • Purity gate green (SHC-08); example app untouched.

items.title: 7.12 Theme, branding and layout
items.text:
• Status: in progress
  • Pull request: #103
  • Records: ADR 053; DD-148 (the brand theme on Bulma 1), DD-149 (critical-CSS inlining off), DD-151 (the legacy text ramp on Bulma 1's channels), DD-152 (the accent ramp: teal primary, Bootstrap accents), DD-153 (the mobile burger chrome); relies on ADR 018, DD-126, DD-131, DD-145, SHC rules (7.11), UIC rules (7.2)

Part of the 7.0 umbrella, whose rules WBP-01 to WBP-07 this slice inherits and its Acceptance repeats.

items.title: Scope
items.text:
Make the 7.11 chrome look like the legacy Aurelius Atlas — the live demo at google.aurelius-atlas.com/demo/atlas is the reference — without porting the legacy @models4insight/styles package (DD-126 stands):

  • the Aurelius palette on Bulma 1's tokens: the Bootstrap accent map the legacy theme carried (link #0073dd, info/success/warning/danger), the blue footer band, the grey chrome bands, Bulma's own teal kept as primary (SHM-04, DD-152), and the legacy mobile burger chrome: grey burger, dropdowns blended into the band, the legacy logout anchor (SHM-04, DD-153)
  • the legacy body type: Bulma 0.9.4's system font stack, 16px, line-height 1.5, #4a4a4a ink — Bulma 1 ships Inter/1rem and renders the app in the wrong type — and the ramp below it: the neutral greys and the weights Bulma 1 re-tinted and re-weighted (SHM-03, DD-151)
  • the Aurelius Atlas logo as the navbar brand, sized by the legacy .logo rule (max-width 150px, max-height 50px) (SHM-02)
  • the legacy navbar anatomy: pinned to the top (is-fixed-top + body padding, the 4.25rem bar), content in a container (SHM-05)
  • the sticky footer: the content band grows to the fold, so the footer sits at the bottom of the viewport on short pages and at the bottom of the document on tall ones (SHM-05)
  • light mode forced: Bulma 1 follows the OS scheme, the legacy (Bulma 0.9.4) was light-only, and the app has no theme switch yet (SHM-01)

This slice does not deliver: the theme switch itself (a later slice flips the data-theme attribute — the brand tokens deliberately live outside the scheme machinery so both schemes keep the Aurelius colours), the navbar search bar and nav buttons (7.4, DD-145), the legacy hero/title colours beyond what the landing slice 7.5 owns.

items.title: Semantics
items.text: Id Rule SHM-01 The document root carries data-theme="light": the app renders the light scheme under any OS preference. The Aurelius brand colours are emitted outside Bulma's scheme machinery, so they survive a future dark scheme. (7.14 supersedes the mechanism — the static html pin becomes the no-stored-choice default applied pre-render, DD-159; this promise stands, SPL-05.) (7.14 supersedes the navbar half of the pin: in dark mode the navbar follows the scheme as the slate band, DD-168; the footer and the light-scheme chrome stand.) SHM-02 The navbar brand is the Aurelius Atlas logo (assets/aurelius-atlas-logo.png, from the legacy libs/assets), linking /, with the app name as its alt text; the ui-lib Header sizes it through its .logo rule (max-width 150px, max-height 50px) applied via the logoCssClass input (default logo). SHM-03 The type is the legacy Bulma 0.9.4 ramp: the BlinkMacSystemFont-first system stack, 16px, line-height 1.5, weight 400, ink #4a4a4a on white — and below the body, the neutral greys and weights Bulma 1 replaced (title 600/#363636, strong 700, button 400, navbar ink #4a4a4a, .content #4a4a4a with #363636 600 headings). The greys land on Bulma 1's channels (--bulma-text-h/s/l &c.) so every derived token follows; the weights land on the selectors Bulma scopes them on (DD-151). All values the live demo renders. SHM-04 The Aurelius palette lands on Bulma 1's tokens in the brand library: the accent map link #0073dd, info #17a2b8, success #28a745, warning #ffc107, danger #dc3545 (the Bootstrap colours the legacy theme carried), each with white solid-fill ink except warning, which keeps Bulma's dark one (DD-152); primary stays Bulma's teal #00d1b2 — the demo's landing icons — with its solid-fill ink pinned white; light/navbar band #f5f5f5 with #363636 invert, navbar hover/active #f5f5f5/#000; footer #0073dd with white text (the legacy footer's has-text-white). The mobile chrome (DD-153): burger ink #4a4a4a with a black hover plate, dropdown arrow #000, selected plate white/#000, and under the burger breakpoint the dropdowns blend into the band with no chevron (0.9.4's mobile rendering). Bulma scopes the navbar/footer tokens on its components, so those overrides are emitted on .navbar/.footer too. SHM-05 The chrome's navbar is pinned (is-fixed-top, the body padded by the 4.25rem bar via has-navbar-fixed-top), its content sits in a Bulma container (the legacy navbar anatomy), and the outlet band is the legacy .is-tall-container verbatim: body is a 100vh flex column, the band grows (flex: 1 1 auto) to a full viewport (min-height: 100vh), so the footer begins at the fold — never stranded mid-page on a short screen. SHM-06 The webapp's dev/e2e pages keep passing every 7.11 chrome scenario (SHC-02..09): the logo brand supersedes SHC-02's name-only brand (the name stays as the logo's alt); the pinned navbar does not cover the landing's top content; the footer keeps its three config values. SHM-07 Page content is inset by Bulma's grid, not hand-rolled margins: the landing wraps in section.section > div.container (the legacy page anatomy — the demo's hero box sits at x=56 in a 1280 viewport, the navbar brand's column) and the footer keeps its container (the legacy footer anatomy). The #f5f5f5 band behind the content stays full-bleed.

items.title: Aurelius origin
items.text:
The legacy sources whose rendering this ports (.scratch/aurelius):

  • libs/shell/src/lib/header/header.component.{html,scss} — the pinned navbar is-fixed-top inside a container, the .logo brand sizing, and the Logout as a.navbar-item[role=button] in navbar ink (no danger red, DD-153)
  • libs/shell/src/lib/footer/footer.component.html — the has-text-white level items on the blue footer band
  • libs/shell/src/lib/shell.component.{html,scss} — .is-tall-container (flex: 1 1 auto, the sticky-footer content band) and the has-background-light page band
  • libs/assets/src/assets/aurelius-atlas-logo.png — the brand mark
  • @models4insight/styles (Bulma 0.9.4 theme) — not ported as a package (DD-126); the metrics it ships (system stack, 16px/1.5, 4.25rem navbar, #f5f5f5 bands, #0073dd link/footer, the Bootstrap accent map) are the reference values SHM-03/04 pin

The live demo (google.aurelius-atlas.com/demo/atlas, version 0.0.0#aad352f) is the reference: every measured value in Acceptance reads from it.

items.title: Deviations
items.text:
Against Apache Atlas: none — this is an Aurelius product frame, Atlas has no UI.

Against the Aurelius product, recorded in design-log:

  • DD-148: the palette lands on Bulma 1 tokens (the legacy shipped Bulma 0.9.4 with SASS variables; Bulma 1 reads CSS custom properties, some scoped on .navbar/.footer); the sticky footer uses the modern flex-column body (the legacy achieves the same through .is-tall-container's min-height: 100vh); the brand greys are Bulma 0.9.4's #f5f5f5/#363636 pair, not Bootstrap's #f8f9fa;
  • DD-149: the prod build disables critical-CSS inlining — the zoneless CSR app never swaps beasties' media="print" sheet back, so the brand rules on .navbar/.footer (and Bulma utilities) applied in dev but not in the Docker/e2e build; the full stylesheet ships render-blocking instead;
  • DD-150: the first cut ported .is-tall-container as flex-grow only (footer flush with the fold) and left the landing edge-to-edge; the demo shows the legacy rule is flex: 1 1 auto plus min-height: 100vh (footer starts below the fold) and the legacy pages wrap in section > container (content inset on the navbar's grid). SHM-05/SHM-07 pin the measured legacy rendering;
  • DD-151: SHM-03's first cut pinned the body metrics only; Bulma 1 re-tinted the whole grey ramp 221 degrees and re-weighted title/strong/button, so the app rendered with a blue-grey cast. SHM-03 now covers the ramp, and the brand re-emits Bulma 0.9.4's neutral channels on Bulma 1's text* channel tokens;
  • DD-152: SHM-04's first cut mapped #0073dd onto primary as a placeholder; the demo's primary is Bulma's own teal (the landing icons are rgb(0,209,178)), and #0073dd is its link/footer colour. SHM-04 now carries the legacy theme's Bootstrap accent map, keeps Bulma's teal as primary with white solid-fill ink, and pins the navbar hover/active band the demo renders (#f5f5f5/#000);
  • DD-153: the mobile burger chrome — Bulma 1 tints the burger/chevron from link and leaves the burger menu's dropdowns as white plates (0.9.4 blends them into the band, and hides the chevron — a Bulma 1 regression the brand mirrors), and the first cut's Logout was a red <button> where the legacy is a plain navbar-ink anchor (a[role=button]); SHM-04/SHC-05 carry the legacy rendering;
  • the theme switch is not ported — light is forced via data-theme="light" (SHM-01), the switch is a later slice;
  • the legacy navbar's is-size-4 name next to the logo is not ported: the logo's alt carries the app name (SHM-02).

items.title: Acceptance
items.text:
• Vitest (nx test aurelius-atlas-ui -c ci, nx test aurelius-atlas-webapp -c ci):
    • header/header.component.spec.ts — logo brand with routerLink/alt (SHM-02), logoCssClass applied (default and custom), fixed pins the navbar (SHM-05), container wraps the navbar content (SHM-05)
    • shell/header.component.spec.ts — the Aurelius logo brand (SHM-02, superseding SHC-02's name-only check), pinned navbar (SHM-05)
    • app.component.spec.ts — the root frame gains the .is-tall-container band (SHM-05), chrome order kept (SHC-01)
  • e2e (nx e2e aurelius-atlas-webapp), each measured against the demo values:
    • test__navbar_carries_the_aurelius_logo — the brand image, 150px cap, links home (SHM-02)
    • test__body_uses_the_legacy_type_and_ink — stack, 16px, 24px line, #4a4a4a (SHM-03)
    • test__type_ramp_matches_the_legacy_page — title 40px/45 600 #363636, box/content #4a4a4a, navbar links #4a4a4a with 700 strong, button 400, 14px dropdown (SHM-03, DD-151)
    • test__chrome_bands_carry_the_aurelius_palette — navbar #f5f5f5, footer #0073dd white text, pinned 68px bar (SHM-04, SHM-05)
    • test__accent_ramp_matches_the_demo — primary teal #00d1b2 with white solid ink, link/info/success/warning/danger on the Bootstrap map, landing icons rgb(0,209,178)/rgb(23,162,184), navbar-link hover #f5f5f5/#000 (SHM-04, DD-152)
    • test__burger_menu_matches_the_legacy_mobile_chrome — at a phone viewport: burger #4a4a4a, the Logout anchor navbar-ink/transparent /start-aligned, no dropdown chevron (SHM-04, DD-153)
    • test__footer_sits_below_the_fold — band ≥ viewport, footer top ≥ viewport (legacy .is-tall-container, SHM-05, SHM-07)
    • test__landing_content_sits_in_a_container — hero box inset on the navbar container's column, band full-bleed (SHM-07)
    • test__app_stays_light_under_a_dark_os_preference — an emulated prefers-color-scheme: dark context renders the light bands (SHM-01)
    • the SHC-02..09 scenarios stay green (SHM-06)
  • The dev build renders the reference: logo, 68px pinned grey bar, #f5f5f5 content band, blue footer at the fold, system-stack 16px text (verified on nx serve at :4300 against the demo).
  • Purity gate green; example app untouched.

items.title: 7.13 UI components: details set
items.text:
• Status: in progress
  • Pull request: #104
  • Records: DD-154, DD-155, DD-156 (the dark ink ramp); relies on ADR 053, DD-135, DD-136, DD-142

Part of the 7.0 umbrella, whose rules WBP-01 to WBP-07 this slice inherits, and of the design-system track opened by 7.2, whose UIC rule ids (UIC-01..10) this increment continues (UIC-11..15).

items.title: Scope
items.text:
Port four more dumb, signal-driven components into aurelius-atlas-ui — the pieces the 7.6 (details) screens will compose, extracted early because their presentation is pure and their data wiring is not needed to build, spec and story them:

  • breadcrumbs ← apps/atlas/src/app/search/components/bread-crumbs — the Bulma nav.breadcrumb trail with per-item icons and a warning chip. The legacy component's BreadCrumbsService (a redux BasicStore) and its $APP_SEARCH_DOCUMENT_PROVIDER injection are data wiring: the ported component takes items/warning/activeGuid inputs and emits itemClicked; the trail-building service arrives with 7.6.
  • entity-card ← apps/atlas/src/app/search/components/cards/details-card (+ its entity-type-name/type-name badge) — the Bulma card: title link, type-name badge, [card-content]/[card-quality] slots, loading state. The legacy cardsByType/ngComponentOutlet per-type bodies are app anatomy (7.6); the port projects content. The card emits entityClicked(guid) — DD-154.
  • properties-item ← apps/atlas/src/app/search/details/components/properties/properties-item — the property-value renderer: strings/numbers/booleans as title-cased text, link arrays as anchors (emitting itemClicked), empty arrays as the N/A label.
  • select ← libs/components/src/lib/select — the Bulma select field: label, options, null/no-data messages, timestamp display, invalid help, and a search button that emits searchRequested — the legacy embedded SearchModal (repository-fed table) is app wiring, wired in 7.7: DD-155.

Not in scope:

Not delivered here Delivered by simple-search-input already ported as SearchField (7.2, DD-135) Trail-building service, iconsByType type→icon meta, search/details route wiring 7.6 (details) — the lib defines, the app composes The select's search modal + repository data 7.7 (editor), via searchRequested (DD-155) markdown, tree, date-picker (third-party deps: ngx-markdown, @angular/material) the 7.2 deferral stands; needs its own DD Wiring these components into webapp screens 7.6 / 7.7

items.title: Semantics
items.text: Id Rule UIC-11 breadcrumbs renders the Bulma nav.breadcrumb.is-small.has-arrow-separator; items are anchors, the activeGuid item gets li.is-active; a warning renders the legacy warning chip; clicking/Enter on a crumb emits itemClicked(guid). UIC-12 entity-card renders the Bulma card: title anchor (emits entityClicked(guid) on click/Enter), the type-name badge (icon-text: icon, typeAlias ?? typeName, optional base-type suffix), [card-content] and [card-quality] projection slots; loading() swaps the body for the legacy loading row (label + loader). UIC-13 properties-item renders a string/number/boolean value title-cased; an array of {guid, displayText} as anchors emitting itemClicked(guid); an empty array as the N/A label; other objects render nothing (the legacy behaviour). UIC-14 select renders the Bulma field: label, fullwidth native select bound two-way to value (model()), options from options() + displayField(), the nullInputMessage/noDataMessage placeholder option, isTimestamp() formats option labels, disabled(), invalid() paints is-danger + the required help, the search button emits searchRequested (DD-155). UIC-15 Every component: chrome strings are caller-supplied inputs with the legacy English defaults (DD-136); icons arrive as IconDefinition inputs (iconsByType is app meta); each ships a story, interactive ones a play() test; the purity gate (DD-131/DD-137) stays green.

items.title: Aurelius origin
items.text: The Aurelius (legacy) sources whose presentation this ports, so reviewers can compare: apps/atlas/src/app/search/components/bread-crumbs/, apps/atlas/src/app/search/components/cards/details-card.component.* + components/entity-type-name/ + components/type-name/, apps/atlas/src/app/search/details/components/properties/properties-item/, libs/components/src/lib/select/ (+ control-shell).

items.title: Deviations
items.text:
• Pulled forward: 7.2's deferral table sent select to 7.7 and the breadcrumbs/card anatomy to 7.4–7.6. Their presentation is pure, so it is ported now as dumb components; the data wiring each source carried (redux stores, repository services, cardsByType, the search modal) stays in its original slice. No deviations.md entry — this is sequencing inside the webapp track, not an Atlas deviation.
  • DD-154: the card emits entityClicked instead of the legacy self-navigation.
  • DD-155: the select emits searchRequested; the search modal is app wiring; the reactive-form/ControlShell base dissolves into model() (as DD-135 did for SearchField), and the compareWith default is strict equality, not lodash isEqual.

items.title: Acceptance
items.text:
• libs/angular/aurelius-atlas-ui/src/lib/{breadcrumbs,entity-card,properties-item,select}/*.spec.ts (Vitest) — behaviours naming UIC ids in the test names (UIC-11..14).
  • nx build-storybook aurelius-atlas-ui -c ci compiles the new stories; nx test-storybook aurelius-atlas-ui — the play() interactions pass (UIC-10 pattern).
  • check-purity (the lib test target) stays green (UIC-15).
  • Consumer regression: nx test aurelius-atlas-webapp -c ci (87) and nx test aurelius-atlas-frontend-example -c ci (75) unchanged — the apps consume no new component yet; nx build aurelius-atlas-ui compiles the extended public API.
  • Umbrella checks: nx lint both projects; nx e2e aurelius-atlas-webapp unchanged.

items.title: Definition of done, in order
items.text:
1. nx test aurelius-atlas-ui -c ci green.
  2. Every story renders; nx test-storybook aurelius-atlas-ui green.
  3. nx lint aurelius-atlas-ui, nx build aurelius-atlas-ui green.
  4. libs/angular/aurelius-atlas-ui/README.md and AGENTS.md list the new components.

items.title: 7.14 Settings panel
items.text:
• Status: in progress
  • Pull request: #105
  • Records: DD-157 (the drawer), DD-158 (telemetry toggle semantics), DD-159 (supersedes SHM-01: data-theme follows the stored choice), DD-160 (the settings facade and per-category owners), DD-161 (browser-scoped localStorage), DD-162 (the drawer's enter/exit animation), DD-163 (the drawer's token fallbacks), DD-164 (the Appearance select), DD-165 (About's one version), DD-166 (the routed drawer outlet), DD-167 (the review polish: lit gear, scheme band, Browser-default picker, .label headings), DD-168 (the dark navbar, the slate band), DD-169 (labels wired to controls), DD-170 (the active locale, filled blue); relies on ADR 053, DD-128, DD-135, DD-136, DD-156

Part of the 7.0 umbrella, whose rules WBP-01 to WBP-07 this slice inherits. It is a new feature, not a port: neither the Apache Atlas dashboards nor the legacy Aurelius shell has a settings control (verified in .scratch/aurelius's libs/shell header and dashboardv2's Header.html — the legacy header's right side is Documentation, language and account, and no theme or settings control exists). DV-65 records it as a deliberate addition.

items.title: Scope
items.text:
A settings panel in the webapp: a gear in the shell header's right side opens a drawer (a new aurelius-atlas-ui component) carrying five sections:

  • Appearance — the theme: Auto / Light / Dark, written to the document root the way Bulma's scheme machinery reads it (DD-156's ramp makes Dark legible).
  • Language — the same full-page locale navigation the header dropdown carried (SHC-04, DD-128); the dropdown leaves the navbar and its control moves into the panel, which is why the gear replaces it (the user's brief: "the button to open the settings can live in the app header where the language settings currently are").
  • Time zone — the display zone for dates, chosen from the ids the server publishes (GET /atlas/admin/session's timezones, ADM-05), applied through Angular's DATE_PIPE_DEFAULT_TIMEZONE provider.
  • Table page size — the default page size the 7.6 tables will paginate with.
  • Telemetry — the browser telemetry on/off switch (DD-158).
  • Plus an About footer: the app name and version (the runtime config, SHL-10 — the same values the footer shows, SHC-06/07) and the server version (GET /atlas/admin/version, ADM-01/DV-03).

Storage is per-browser localStorage (SPL-09). The architecture is a facade (DD-160): a SettingsService facade over one owner service per category; the theme's owner is the ui-lib's existing DarkModeService. Server-side per-user persistence (the Keycloak profile, or the Atlas session settings ADM-05 exposes) is a deliberate later slice — the seam is the UserPreference helper, so the owners' APIs, the facade and the panel do not change when it lands.

Not in scope:

Not delivered here Delivered by Server-side persistence of the settings a later slice, behind the UserPreference seam (DD-160) Date/time rendering wired to the time zone 7.6 (details) — the first screen with dates; the provider is set Pagination wired to the page-size setting 7.6/7.7 — the screens that paginate The navbar search bar (the header's other right-side control) 7.4 (DD-145) Runtime language switching (in-page string swap) none — one build per locale is the design (DD-128) Retiring the example app (it keeps its own header, and the dark-mode widget's home) 7.10 (DV-64)

items.title: Semantics
items.text: Id Rule SPL-01 The header's right side carries a gear button (navbar-item, a faGear icon, an accessible label shell.header.settings) that opens the settings panel and carries is-active (via routerLinkActive) exactly while the panel route is open (DD-167); the language dropdown (SHC-04) leaves the navbar and its control lives in the panel. Documentation (SHC-03) and account (SHC-05) are unchanged. SPL-02 Drawer is a dumb aurelius-atlas-ui component: Bulma-token styled fixed-right panel, active as a model(), a title heading, ariaLabel for the close control; dismiss() on the backdrop, the close button and Escape (the Modal's dismissal set, card anatomy); content is projected; opening moves focus into the panel, Escape returns it; it slides in on open and out on close, the layer living until the exit animation ends (DD-162); head and body carry the modal's padding, the scrim the modal's colour, each as a token with an explicit fallback (DD-163). Bulma 1 ships no drawer (DD-157). SPL-03 The Appearance picker — the ui-lib Select with searchVisible off, its rows the three modes, Auto first (DD-164) — writes the theme through the owner: Light/Dark set data-theme to light/dark on the document root; Auto removes the attribute, so Bulma's OS-scheme path (:root:not([data-theme]), DD-156's dark host) applies. An empty data-theme is never written — the empty attribute keeps the OS path from applying (DD-159). SPL-04 The choice persists: the key data-theme in localStorage (the key DarkModeService already owns), and the stored value is applied at bootstrap, before the first render, so a returning user never sees a flash of the other scheme. SPL-05 With no stored choice, the app renders the light scheme under any OS preference — SHM-01's user-visible promise, kept after its mechanism is superseded (DD-159): the light default is the DarkModeService mode default, not the html pin. A stored scheme repaints the whole page, the outlet band included — the band is Bulma's scheme-following .has-background, not the fixed light (DD-167). The navbar follows the scheme too, carrying the dark slate band that keeps the logo's navy wordmark legible (DD-168). SPL-06 The Language section keeps SHC-04's semantics inside the panel: the active locale (from the document's lang) is marked, en-US and nl-NL are listed, choosing one is a full-page navigation to /<locale>/<current path with any locale prefix stripped> (DD-128). The active locale is the build that is served; the panel stores no language preference. The marking is visible, not only semantic: the active link is a filled Aurelius-blue plate, the pair the footer pins (DD-170). SPL-07 The Time zone section stores the chosen IANA id (aurelius-atlas.settings.timezone), offers the ids the server's session publishes (ADM-05) with a "Browser default" first option, and applies it through the DATE_PIPE_DEFAULT_TIMEZONE provider read at bootstrap: a change takes effect on reload (DD-161). The store is browser-scoped and carries no user identity (DD-161). An unset zone shows "Browser default" in the picker — the stored value, not the browser's resolved zone (DD-167). SPL-08 The Table page size section stores the default page size (aurelius-atlas.settings.pageSize, a positive integer, default 10) for the 7.6 tables to read. SPL-09 Every setting lives in localStorage under a browser-scoped key — data-theme (SPL-04) and aurelius-atlas.settings.* — written only by its owner (SPL-10). This is a user experience convenience, not a data store: nothing that identifies a user, grants a permission, or belongs to the catalogue is kept there (DD-161). SPL-10 SettingsService is a facade: it exposes each category's signal and setter and delegates to exactly one owner service per category — theme → DarkModeService (ui-lib), language → LocaleNavigationService, time zone → TimezoneService, page size → PageSizeService, telemetry → TelemetryService. The owner is the sole writer of its storage key, and the panel and the bootstrap providers consume the facade/owners, never localStorage directly. Server-side persistence replaces a UserPreference owner's internals only (DD-160). SPL-11 The Telemetry switch stores its state (aurelius-atlas.settings.telemetry, default on). Off takes effect immediately: the trace and metric exporters stop sending. On takes effect on reload — the SDK bootstraps at startup (DD-158). The panel states this where the switch is. SPL-12 The About section shows the app name and version from the runtime config (SHL-10, the footer's SHC-06/07 values) and nothing else: app and server carry one version under the release strategy, so no server fetch and no server line (DD-165). SPL-13 Every chrome string is a @@shell.settings.*/@@shell.header.settings id with entries in both fixture locales, so the completeness gate (SHL-08) and the purity gate (DD-131/DD-137) stay green; Drawer ships a spec and stories (UIC-15's bar), the theme switch is verified against DD-156's dark ramp. Every section heading is a Bulma .label — the form-controls guide's field label, one shape for all six (DD-167), and every heading is its control's accessible name — label[for], the language group via aria-labelledby (DD-169). SPL-14 The panel is a routed overlay: a drawer named outlet at the app root, the panel the settings route in it, the gear a routerLink to it (a no-op while open — the router cancels the duplicate), dismissal navigating it away (DD-166). The open state rides the URL, so the language switch's full-page reload (SPL-06, DD-128) lands on the same page, panel open; future drawers are their own segments.

items.title: Aurelius origin
items.text:
Nothing is ported. The precedents the design leans on:

  • libs/shell/src/lib/header/header.component.html (.scratch/aurelius) — the header's right-side controls the gear joins and the language dropdown it absorbs; its setLanguage() runtime swap is not ported (DD-128: the locale builds are separate bundles, so SHC-04's navigation stays).
  • libs/shell/src/translations/{en-US,nl-NL}.json — the shell.header.* key naming the new settings.* keys follow.
  • Apache Atlas 2.4.0 AdminResource.Session — the timezones list SPL-07 offers (ADM-05, DV-05), and AdminResource.Version for SPL-12 (ADM-01, DV-03).

items.title: Deviations
items.text:
• DV-65 (new feature): Aurelius Atlas ships a settings panel; Apache Atlas 2.4.0 has none (its user-facing preferences live in the dashboard's UserSettings redux store, not in the header, and are not part of the REST contract). The panel is part of Aurelius's own interface (ADR 053, DV-64's framing), not a port, and touches no Atlas endpoint.
  • DD-159 supersedes SHM-01's mechanism (7.12): the html data-theme="light" pin is removed because it is read as an explicit choice and would outrank a stored Dark/Auto selection. SHM-01's promise stands — with no stored choice the app is light under any OS preference — delivered by the mode default (SPL-05). 7.12's own scope note anticipated this: "the switch is a later slice".
  • DD-161: the settings are browser-scoped localStorage, not the per-user store Atlas's UserSettings was; a shared browser shares the settings. Server-side persistence (Keycloak profile attributes, or the Atlas session settings) is the follow-up slice, and is why the UserPreference seam exists.

items.title: Acceptance
items.text:
• Vitest (nx test aurelius-atlas-ui -c ci, nx test aurelius-atlas-webapp -c ci):
    • drawer/drawer.component.spec.ts — active model opens/closes, dismiss() on backdrop/close/Escape, title and ariaLabel render, content projected (SPL-02); the close slides out and the layer drops on animationend, foreign animations are ignored, reopening mid-exit cancels it (DD-162)
    • dark-mode/dark-mode.service.spec.ts — setMode writes the attribute for light/dark and removes it for auto, persists to data-theme, defaults to light (SPL-03, SPL-04, SPL-05)
    • settings/settings.service.spec.ts — the facade delegates each category to its owner and exposes it read-only (SPL-10)
    • settings/*/*.service.spec.ts — UserPreference reads and writes its key (SPL-09); TelemetryService off stops the exporters, on is deferred to reload (SPL-11); TimezoneService id list and browser-default first (SPL-07); PageSizeService positive-integer guard (SPL-08)
    • shell/header.component.spec.ts — the gear is the (drawer:settings) routerLink (SPL-01, SPL-14) and lights is-active while the drawer route is open (SPL-01, DD-167), the language dropdown is gone from the navbar, Documentation and account unchanged (SPL-01)
    • settings/settings-panel.component.spec.ts — the routed panel renders open (SPL-14), the five sections render with .label headings (SPL-13, DD-167), every heading is its control's accessible name (SPL-13, DD-169), the Appearance select drives the theme (SPL-03, DD-164), the language links compute locale hrefs, the active locale is highlighted (SPL-06, DD-170), the zone picker shows "Browser default" while unset (SPL-07, DD-167), About shows the build's one version (SPL-12, DD-165), dismissal navigates the drawer outlet away (SPL-14, DD-166)
    • routes.spec.ts — the settings route sits in the drawer outlet and loads the panel (SPL-14, DD-166)
    • select/select.component.spec.ts — searchVisible off hides the search button, the dropdown stays (DD-164)
    • i18n-completeness.spec.ts — every new id exists in both locales (SPL-13)
  • Storybook (nx test-storybook aurelius-atlas-ui): Drawer Primary/Open/OnDark with play() tests; the theme switch flipped from the toolbar on a drawer story proves DD-156's ramp under Auto (SPL-13).
  • E2E (served app, nx e2e aurelius-atlas-webapp): the panel's rules are reviewable as code through the Vitest specs above; a served-app scenario (gear → dark → reload stays dark) lands with the 7.10 e2e set that serves the app.
  • Gate: nx run-many -t test e2e -c ci (levels 1 and 2), lint, build, the webapp purity gate, and uv run aurelius-atlas-trace check for the coverage rule.

items.title: 7.15 Alerts drawer
items.text:
• Status: in progress
  • Pull request: #107
  • Records: DD-171 (the alerts store: windowed grouping, cap), DD-172 (the ErrorHandler chain: alert then trace), DD-173 (the HTTP error reporter), DD-174 (the bell: severity badge, ring animation), DD-175 (the ui-lib split: AlertList and Badge are presentational), DD-176 (the live-review fix: the chip's pinned pair, Clear all in the drawer head), DD-180 (the inbox bar: severity chips, read tracking, Clear all in the bar), DD-181 (the drawer's body-scroll: the head and subhead stay fixed), DD-182 (the joined bar: ramp order, severity fills, actions as group members), DD-183 (the bar's equal height: the compacted count badge), DD-184 (the void chip: an empty severity greys out), DD-185 (show-all removed: the bar's shape never shifts); relies on ADR 053, DD-152, DD-157, DD-158, DD-166, DD-167

items.title: Scope
items.text:
A drawer that collects the app's alerts for the user — the errors the app hits while they work, and any app-level notification a future slice pushes — opened from a bell in the header, beside the settings gear. It delivers:

  • AlertsService: the in-memory alert store with windowed grouping (the door every alert walks through, ALR-03).
  • AlertsPanel: the routed drawer ((drawer:alerts)) rendering the feed, with per-alert dismissal and clear-all (ALR-01, ALR-06, ALR-07).
  • AlertList, Badge and AlertInbox in aurelius-atlas-ui: the reusable feed, the severity dot, and the inbox bar — presentational, spec + stories (ALR-10, ALR-11, UIC-15's bar).
  • The header bell: routerLink + is-active (the gear's pattern, DD-167), an unread badge, and a ring animation when a new alert group arrives (ALR-02, ALR-02a, ALR-12).
  • Read tracking: arrivals are unread, opening the drawer reads the feed, the bell dot and the inbox chips answer what has not been seen (ALR-12, DD-180).
  • Error capture: an ErrorHandler chain that records uncaught runtime errors as alerts and still delegates to the trace handler (ALR-04, SHL-14 kept), and an HTTP interceptor that reports failed /api calls (ALR-05).

It explicitly does not deliver: server-persisted alerts (the store is in-memory; a future slice has the server's own events to deliver), notification sources beyond runtime/HTTP errors (7.6+ feature slices push through AlertsService.add), auto-dismissal (everything lives until dismissed), per-group read toggling (read is per group, marked by arrival and by opening the drawer — ALR-12; no read-later list), or served-app e2e scenarios (the 7.10 set).

items.title: Semantics
items.text: Id Rule ALR-01 The bell opens the alerts drawer by navigating the drawer aux outlet to (drawer:alerts) (the DD-166 pattern), and is lit is-active while it is open (the gear's DD-167 pattern). The one named outlet swaps drawers: opening alerts replaces the settings panel and vice versa; dismissal navigates the outlet away. The segment rides the locale switch's full-page reload (SPL-14's mechanic, SPL-06's reload). ALR-02 The bell carries a badge — a small dot — while the store holds at least one unread alert, coloured by the highest unread severity (error > warning > info, DD-152's ramp: danger, warning, info). It is presence, not a count (ALR-12): opening the drawer reads the feed and the dot goes. The dot carries a ring in the navbar's ink so it clears 3:1 on both navbar bands (the slate, DD-168; the light band, SHM-04). ALR-02a When a new alert group arrives, the bell rings (a ~650 ms Web Animations swing). Merges into an existing group (ALR-03) do not ring; the badge appearing is the first arrival's ring, per group. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce the animation is skipped (the store is unchanged). ALR-03 The store is in-memory and capped (30 groups, oldest evicted). Alerts group in a quiet window: the key is severity + source + message; an alert whose key matches the newest group's and arrives within 60 s of that group's last alert merges into it (count +1, lastSeen moves); after the gap a new group starts, so the feed shows bursts as bursts. The store is a signal list, newest first. ALR-04 An uncaught runtime error (the Angular ErrorHandler) becomes an error alert (message: the error's; source: app), and the trace handler still receives it — the chain records, then delegates (SHL-14 untouched, DD-172). ALR-05 A failed /api call becomes an error alert: 5xx responses and network failures (a request that never got a response). 4xx stays silent — client-side corrections are the calling feature's own business (DD-173). The message names the method, path, and status (or "no response"); the source is http. ALR-06 Each row dismisses its own group (the whole burst goes); "Clear all" empties the store and rides the inbox bar (ALR-11) — a long feed must not bury the escape hatch, and the bar does not scroll (DD-176's fix, placed in the bar by DD-180). Shown only while the store has alerts. Dismissal is immediate; there is no undo. The badge follows the store: the last group's dismissal removes it. ALR-07 Rows are Bulma notifications on the brand ramp (is-danger/is-warning/is-info, DD-152): severity colours the row, the message is body text, the time renders lastSeen through DatePipe under the settings' zone (SPL-07's token), and a count chip (×N, translated, count > 1 only) marks a burst; the chip's pair is pinned white/dark ink — Bulma's is-light is a scheme trap (the brand's pinned plate under Bulma's scheme-following ink, DD-176). ALR-08 Every chrome string is a @@shell.alerts.* id with entries in both fixture locales, so the completeness gate (SHL-08) and the purity gate (DD-131/DD-137) stay green. The ui-lib components take their labels as inputs with English defaults (the Drawer.ariaLabel pattern), so the xlf dependency stays app-side. ALR-09 The feed is role="log" with aria-live="polite": alerts arriving while the drawer is open are announced. The drawer is the ui-lib Drawer (DD-157): backdrop, close button, Escape, focus capture and restore. Dismiss buttons are keyboard-reachable. ALR-10 AlertList, Badge and AlertInbox are ui-lib components: input()/output() only, no services, no app imports, spec + stories each (UIC-15's bar). AlertList renders a caller-supplied AlertGroup[] and emits dismiss(id); clearing the feed is the caller's action, projected into the inbox bar (DD-180) — the list is the rows, not the store's escape hatch. Badge wraps content and shows a severity-coloured dot on visible. The AlertGroup model is exported from the lib — it is presentation vocabulary. ALR-11 Above the feed rides the inbox bar (the ui-lib AlertInbox, DD-180): a full-width Bulma button group (buttons has-addons) of one chip per severity, in inbox order — info, warning, error, the ramp calm to urgent (DD-182) — a chip appears even for an empty severity, a filter with no results is still a filter. Each chip shows that severity's total group count (the chips are filters; the number is coverage, not news) and carries a dot while any of its groups is unread (ALR-12); a severity with no alerts greys out — the chip is disabled, unpressed, and takes no fill, a filter with nothing to show has nothing to toggle (DD-184). A chip toggles its severity's rows in the feed (pressed = shown); a shown chip rides its severity's pinned fill (DD-152's ramp, the inks the ramp's own inverts — Bulma's .button.is-* fills are scheme-following, SHM-04's trap, DD-182), an unpressed chip is a plain button. Which severities are hidden is the panel's view state, the store's counts and the bell ignore it. Clear all is a member of the same group, is-expanded like the chips (DD-182) — the strip is one joined bar. The bar shows no show-all control: appearing at full filtering it inserted a fourth expanded segment and the chips jumped narrower, and the way back is a chip, which stays clickable while hidden (DD-185). The bar rides the drawer's drawer-subhead slot — a strip below the head, outside the scrolling body (DD-180, DD-181). ALR-12 Read state is per group. An arriving alert marks its group unread — a merge re-unreads a read burst, fresh news is news. Opening the drawer is reading it: the panel marks every group read while it lives, so a live feed in an open drawer marks arrivals read as they land (visible-is-read). An unread row is bold with a ring dot in the meta line (label announced, not colour-only); an unread severity rides a dot on its inbox chip, and the bell badge answers unread presence in the highest unread severity's colour (ALR-02). markAllRead is a no-op once every row is read, so the panel's effect settles.

items.title: Java origin
items.text: None. Apache Atlas 2.4.0 has no user-facing alerts surface: its notifications are Kafka hook messages (DV-01, out of scope) and its dashboards show toasts per feature, uncollected. The drawer is Aurelius's own interface (ADR 053).

items.title: Deviations
items.text: # Area Apache Atlas behaviour Aurelius Atlas behaviour Reason Increment DV-66 Interface No alerts surface: feature toasts, Kafka hook messages to clients An alerts drawer collects app-level alerts (runtime and HTTP errors) The drawer is Aurelius's own interface (ADR 053), touches no Atlas endpoint 7.15

items.title: Acceptance
items.text:
• Vitest (nx test aurelius-atlas-ui -c ci, nx test aurelius-atlas-webapp -c ci):
    • badge/badge.component.spec.ts — the dot renders on visible, maps the three severities to the ramp, hides at false; role="status" naming (ALR-02, ALR-10)
    • alert-list/alert-list.component.spec.ts — rows per group with severity classes, count chip at count > 1 only, empty state, the dismiss output, role="log"/aria-live, no clear control in the feed (DD-176), the unread row marker and its label (ALR-12) (ALR-07, ALR-09, ALR-10, ALR-12)
    • alert-inbox/alert-inbox.component.spec.ts — one chip per severity in feed order, totals not unread counts, the unread dot and its label, pressed/hidden chips, the toggle output, the bar's stable shape at full filtering (DD-185), caller labels, the projected action (ALR-11, ALR-12)
    • drawer/drawer.component.spec.ts — the drawer-subhead slot projects between head and body, outside the scrolling body (DD-180)
    • alerts/alerts.service.spec.ts — add appends newest-first, the 60 s window merges by key (count, lastSeen) and a gap starts a new group, the 30-group cap evicts oldest, dismiss/clearAll, the badge severity is the highest present (ALR-02, ALR-03, ALR-06); arrivals/merges unread, markAllRead, the unread top severity, the per-severity counts (ALR-11, ALR-12)
    • alerts/alerts-error-handler.spec.ts — records an error alert and delegates to the inner handler (ALR-04)
    • alerts/alerts-http.interceptor.spec.ts — 5xx and network failure report, 4xx stays silent, the message names method/path/status (ALR-05)
    • alerts/alerts-panel.component.spec.ts — renders open in the drawer outlet, rows from the store, dismiss removes the group, clear-all (in the inbox bar, DD-180) empties, the chips filter the feed and keep the store's totals while filtered, opening marks the feed read (ALR-01, ALR-06, ALR-07, ALR-11, ALR-12)
    • shell/header.component.spec.ts — the bell is the (drawer:alerts) routerLink, lights is-active while open (ALR-01), the badge shows the top unread severity and hides on an empty or read store (ALR-02, ALR-12), the ring animation fires on a new group and is skipped under reduced motion (ALR-02a)
    • routes.spec.ts — the alerts route sits in the drawer outlet (ALR-01)
    • i18n-completeness.spec.ts — every new id exists in both locales (ALR-08)
  • Live (dev server): force a failing /api call, watch the badge appear and the bell ring; open the drawer, see the row; repeat the call, see ×2 merge; clear-all, the badge goes.
  • Gates: nx lint both projects, prod + nl-NL builds, pre-commit.

items.title: 7.16 UI components: details chrome set
items.text:
• Status: in progress
  • Pull request: #110
  • Records: DD-189 (the chip atom is the classification chip), DD-190 (the type-name badge is its own component), DD-191 (details navigation is a shell; the scroll directive stays app-side), DD-192 (the section count bar is section-stats); relies on ADR 053, DD-135, DD-136, DD-154, DD-155, UIC-15

Part of the 7.0 umbrella, whose rules WBP-01 to WBP-07 this slice inherits, and of the design-system track opened by 7.2, whose UIC rule ids (UIC-01..10) 7.13 continued (UIC-11..15); this increment carries the series on (UIC-16..20).

items.title: Scope
items.text:
7.6 shipped the details skeleton with its chrome inline. Four pieces of that chrome — and of the legacy details screen around it — are pure presentation whose data wiring is not needed to build, spec and story them: the same seam 7.13 cut (its "pulled forward" deviation), applied one screen deeper. Port them into aurelius-atlas-ui as dumb, signal-driven components:

  • classification-chip ← apps/atlas/src/app/search/components/classification/ (+ the identical search/components/term/ shell) — the Bulma tags.has-addons chip: icon lead tag, label tag with tooltip, optional propagation tag whose hoverable dropdown projects the sources list, loading state. The legacy ClassificationService/ClassificationSourceService (App Search lookups by guid) are data wiring: name, description, propagated and the sources list arrive as inputs; the sources' rows are caller-projected (DD-189).
  • type-name ← apps/atlas/src/app/search/components/type-name/ — the type badge: icon, typeAlias ?? typeName, optional base-type suffix. 7.13 inlined this badge inside entity-card (UIC-12); the details header (.subtitle.name), the propagated-sources rows, and 7.7's editor all use it standalone, so it is extracted as a component and entity-card consumes it (DD-190).
  • details-navigation ← apps/atlas/src/app/search/details/components/navigation/ — the section-navigation shell: Bulma up-dropdown around a menu (label input, ng-content for the li list, toggle button state is presentational). The legacy DetailsNavigationItem directive (smooth-scroll into view) is DOM behaviour on the app's document — it stays app-side (DD-191).
  • section-stats ← the count bar duplicated in details/default/default-details.component.html (one stat) and details/gov-quality/gov-quality-details.component.html (three stats) — nav.level of heading-link + count items; items: { label, target, count } in, itemClicked(target) out (the nav directive's anchor click, turned into an emit, DD-154's pattern). The heading/count typography pair is the Aurelius shape (DD-192).

Not in scope:

Not delivered here Delivered by Wiring these into the details screen (header chips, nav, count bar) the 2.3+7.6 wiring increment (7.6's deferral table) The sources' media rows (name link + crumbs + type badge, repository-fed) 7.6 wiring — the chip projects them; type-name is its badge (DD-189) DetailsNavigationItem scroll directive, iconsByType the webapp (app meta and DOM behaviour, UIC-15's split) The nine type components, lineage, quality cards, edit affordance 7.6 deferral table (unchanged) details-header composition (title + chips + crumbs + edit action) 2.3+7.6 — it composes these four; spec it where its data (the entity DTO) is media-row, section-heading (Tier 2 of the 7.6 audit) their own increment, keyed when their screens are specced

items.title: Semantics
items.text:
Each rule the behaviour must obey, in plain words, with an id that tests name in the test title (the TS pattern, UIC-11..15's precedent).

Id Rule UIC-16 classification-chip renders the Bulma tags.has-addons chip: the lead tag (caller icon, aria-hidden, the chip's accessible label text) and a label tag carrying label() with title = tooltip(); loading() swaps the label tag for the loader tag. A propagated() chip adds the is-hoverable trigger tag (caller propagatedIcon, title = propagatedLabel()); its dropdown menu projects [chip-sources] under the originLabel() line. Inputs replace the legacy services; the term chip is the same atom with is-info on the lead tag — one component, colour is an input. UIC-17 type-name renders the span.icon-text badge: title = typeAlias ?? typeName; the icon span.icon (caller icon + iconClass()) when showIcon(), the name span (typeAlias ?? typeName) when showTypeName(), and  (typeName) when showBaseTypeName() && typeAlias(). Nothing renders when neither name is set. entity-card's badge is this component (UIC-12's rendered output is unchanged — its spec stays green as the regression proof). UIC-18 details-navigation renders box.is-paddingless > dropdown.is-up.is-right with the toggle button.is-text.is-large (caller toggleIcon; toggles is-active, the Bulma CSS does the rest), and a nav.menu with the menu-label label (caller-supplied, DD-136) + the ul.menu-list holding projected lis. The component owns no scroll, no anchors: items are caller markup, so the app's directive (DD-191) wires them. UIC-19 section-stats renders nav.level with one level-item.has-text-centered per item: p.heading > a (href #target, emits itemClicked(target) on activation) + p.title with the count. items() is the whole input; counts arrive rendered-as-text from the caller. The default-details bar is one item, the gov-quality bar three — one component, both shapes. UIC-20 Every component: chrome strings are caller-supplied inputs with the legacy English defaults (DD-136); icons arrive as IconDefinition inputs (UIC-15); each ships a story, interactive ones a play() test (UIC-10's pattern); the purity gate stays green (DD-131/DD-137). The legacy defaults chosen here are the catalogue's English values of the existing bridge keys (search.components.classification.isPropagated/.originates, search.components.term.term, search.details.components.navigation.details).

items.title: Aurelius origin
items.text:
The Aurelius 17 app (.scratch/aurelius, commit pinned by 7-0), so reviewers can compare:

  • apps/atlas/src/app/search/components/classification/classification.component.{ts,html,scss} — the chip; its classification.service.ts (type-definition lookup) and classification-source/ (repository-fed media rows) are the data wiring not ported; the chip's loading tag and propagated dropdown are
  • apps/atlas/src/app/search/components/term/term.component.{ts,html} — the chip's twin (is-info lead, one label); its term.service.ts is data wiring
  • apps/atlas/src/app/search/components/type-name/type-name.component.{ts,html,scss} — the badge; iconsByType (search/meta) is app meta, an input here
  • apps/atlas/src/app/search/details/components/navigation/details-navigation.component.{ts,html} — the nav shell; details-navigation-item.directive.ts (scrollIntoView) stays app-side (DD-191)
  • apps/atlas/src/app/search/details/default/default-details.component.html
    • details/gov-quality/gov-quality-details.component.html — the two count bars section-stats unifies; details/details.component.html — the chip call sites (classifications-list, the meanings row)

items.title: Deviations
items.text:
None against Apache Atlas: these are Aurelius product components; Atlas's own details UI is its dashboard (ADR 046, the parity reference stays).

Against the Aurelius product, the intended differences are recorded in design-log: DD-189 (the chip is the classification chip — the term variant is the same atom, colour an input; sources project in), DD-190 (the badge is extracted from entity-card, which then consumes it — 7.13's inlining reversed, with UIC-12's spec as the regression proof), DD-191 (the nav is a shell; the scroll directive stays app-side), DD-192 (the count bar is one component for both call sites). Sequencing inside the webapp track, as 7.13's "pulled forward" note — no deviations.md entry.

items.text:
• Vitest (unit), naming UIC ids in the test titles:
    • libs/angular/aurelius-atlas-ui/src/lib/classification-chip/classification-chip.component.spec.ts (UIC-16, UIC-20)
    • libs/angular/aurelius-atlas-ui/src/lib/type-name/type-name.component.spec.ts (UIC-17); entity-card.component.spec.ts unchanged and green as the extraction's regression proof
