items.title: Definition of done, in order
items.text:
1. nx test aurelius-atlas-ui -c ci green (the four specs + entity-card regression).
  2. Stories render; nx test-storybook aurelius-atlas-ui green.
  3. nx lint aurelius-atlas-ui, nx build aurelius-atlas-ui green; purity gate green.
  4. Consumer regressions green (nx test aurelius-atlas-webapp -c ci, frontend example).
  5. libs/angular/aurelius-atlas-ui/README.md and AGENTS.md list the new components; spec status → done, roadmap row flipped, DD-189..192 accepted.

items.title: 7.17 Collector ingest auth
items.text:
• Status: in progress
  • Pull request: #119
  • Records: DD-193 (the two-leg ingest proof: user JWTs for browsers, a shared token for services); extends ADR 039 (TLS proves the channel, the credential proves the writer) and ADR 034 (the one collection point); relies on SHL-11 (the proxy paths), SHL-14 and SPL-11 (the telemetry the proxies carry), ESD-06 (the puller sidecars), APC-05/APC-06 (the login the browser leg gates on)

items.title: Scope
items.text:
The OTel collector's OTLP receivers stop accepting anonymous writes. It delivers:

  • Two ingest legs on dev/observability's collector, each with its own proof of the writer (DD-193):
    • the browser leg (HTTP 4318) authenticates the signed-in user through the collector's oidc extension: Keycloak issuer, signature, and the otel-collector audience. A push with no token, a token from another issuer, or a non-JWT credential is answered 401;
    • the service leg (gRPC 4317, HTTP 4319) requires the shared ingest token through bearertokenauth: a push without it is answered 401 / Unauthenticated.
  • The Keycloak realm's otel-ingest client scope, on the aurelius client's default scopes: its audience mapper stamps aud: otel-collector on user tokens (azp stays aurelius, so the APIs' azp-or-aud validation is unaffected).
  • Delivery per producer class:
    • browsers attach their own access token through the OTLP exporters' headers factory (the OTLP transport rides XHR/fetch outside Angular's HttpClient, so the bearer interceptor cannot cover it); the live Keycloak client attaches in an app initializer, and the factory refreshes per export. The seam is shared, not per-app: createAureliusOtelIngestAuth in aurelius-atlas-observability (the webapp and the example app wire the same seam). The webapp's and the example app's /otel/ proxies pass the Authorization header through untouched — their config, CSP (connect-src 'self') and the SDK's endpoint wiring are unchanged;
    • server-side exporters (Atlas server, FastAPI example, Keycloak) present the shared token through the standard OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS env var, and the slice puller sidecars (postgres, keycloak-infra, elasticsearch) through their exporter's headers block — all on the service leg (4317 gRPC / 4319 HTTP).
  • The collector's host publishes pinned to loopback (4317/4318/4319), the prometheus exporter's publish (:9464) dropped — Prometheus scrapes it inside the compose network.

It explicitly does not deliver: per-service identities on the service leg (one shared secret for headless writers; Keycloak-JWT ingest for them stays a future option, DD-193), pre-login browser telemetry (the login is the telemetry gate — accepted, DD-193), token rotation machinery, production deployment manifests, or auth on the collector's internal telemetry (:8888, scraped in-network).

items.title: Semantics
items.text: Id Rule CIA-01 The collector's OTLP receivers require a credential. The browser leg (4318) answers 401 to a push with no token, a token from an issuer it does not trust, a token without the otel-collector audience, or a non-JWT credential (the service token), and accepts a user token the issuer minted. The service leg (4317/4319) answers 401 / Unauthenticated without the shared ingest token, and accepts with it. TLS stays as ADR 039 states it — the credential stacks on the verified channel, it does not replace it. CIA-02 The browser's credential is its own user token: the SPA attaches it through the OTLP exporters' headers factory (per export, refreshed), and the /otel/ proxies pass Authorization through untouched — a push with a user token through the webapp/example origin reaches the collector authenticated, a token-less push comes back 401 (the proxy injects nothing). SHL-11's forwarding (prefix stripped) and the CSP (connect-src 'self') are unchanged. CIA-03 The collector publishes 4317/4318/4319 on 127.0.0.1 only, and no host publish for the prometheus exporter; producers inside compose stacks reach it over service DNS, never through a published port. CIA-04 Every server-side producer presents the shared token on the service leg: the Atlas server, the FastAPI example, Keycloak's native OTLP, and the three metrics-puller sidecars keep exporting (their telemetry keeps flowing to the collector). CIA-05 Browser telemetry is attributed: the collector's OIDC receiver resolves the token's sub, so a user's OTLP push carries that user's identity and a forged push is attributable to the account that minted the token.

items.title: Java origin
items.text: None. Apache Atlas 2.4.0 ships no OpenTelemetry collector: its telemetry is Dropwizard metrics on the server's own REST port (DV-01's surface, out of scope here). The collector is Aurelius's own architecture (ADR 034); this increment hardens its ingest.

items.title: Deviations
items.text: None against Apache Atlas (no Atlas behaviour is touched; the increment is platform-side). The deliberate posture choices — user JWTs on the browser leg over a shared secret, a shared secret on the service leg over per-service identity, the accepted loss of pre-login telemetry, loopback pinning — are recorded in DD-193, not in deviations.md (which tracks Atlas-parity deltas).

items.title: Acceptance
items.text:
• e2e (nx e2e aurelius-atlas-webapp -c ci, nx e2e aurelius-atlas-frontend-example -c ci):
    • test__otel_proxy_forwards_to_the_collector — a push carrying a real user token through the proxy reaches the collector (SHL-11 forwarding, CIA-02)
    • test__otel_proxy_passes_authorization_through — a token-less push through the proxy is the collector's 401, proving the proxy injects nothing (CIA-01, CIA-02)
    • test__collector_rejects_unauthenticated_ingest — a direct POST /v1/traces to the collector's published browser-leg port with no token answers 401, and the CA-verified TLS handshake to the same port succeeds (CIA-01)
    • test__collector_accepts_a_user_token_on_the_browser_leg — the same POST with a Keycloak-minted user token (the realm's password grant, the otel-ingest audience) answers 2xx (CIA-01, CIA-05, the positive control)
    • test__collector_stamps_the_user_onto_the_telemetry — a probe span pushed with a user token comes back from Tempo with the token's sub on its resource attributes as enduser.id (trace-by-id read-back, GET /api/traces/<id>?encoding=json): the identity rode the data into the queryable backend (CIA-05, DD-194; webapp suite)
    • test__collector_rejects_the_shared_token_on_the_browser_leg — the service credential on the browser leg answers 401: the legs stay distinct proofs (CIA-01)
    • test__collector_accepts_the_shared_ingest_token — the service leg (4319) accepts the shared token (CIA-01, CIA-04)
    • test__collector_publishes_are_loopback_pinned — the published sockets bind 127.0.0.1 (CIA-03)
    • test__producers_keep_flowing_with_the_token — accepted OTLP exports reach the collector within the suite window, proving the server-side producers present the token (CIA-04; additionally proven by every producer keeping its nx serve/e2e runs green — Grafana's stack dashboard shows the pullers and Keycloak flowing)
  • Unit (vitest, aurelius-atlas-observability): createAureliusOtelIngestAuth sends the bearer token of an authenticated session, nothing for a signed-out one or before the client attaches, and the current token when refresh fails (CIA-02, DD-193).
  • Run: the dev stack (nx up aurelius-atlas-dev-observability) plus the producer slices; curl --cacert dev/observability/certs/ca.pem to https://127.0.0.1:4318/v1/traces answers 401 with no header and with the service token, 2xx with a user token; https://127.0.0.1:4319/v1/traces answers 401 with no header, 2xx with the service token.

items.title: 7.18 Collector ingest identity
items.text:
• Status: in progress
  • Pull request: #119
  • Records: DD-196 (per-service ingest identity: Keycloak client-credentials JWTs on the service leg, azp-stamped), DD-202 (one issuer world: producers mint on the TLS listener, the collector validates both); supersedes the service-leg half of DD-193 (user JWTs on the browser leg, the loopback pinning, and the shared-token mechanism all stand); extends ADR 039 and ADR 034; relies on CIA-01..05 (7.17 — the two legs, the OIDC extension, the otel-ingest scope, the DD-194 stamping, the DD-195 boot race)

items.title: Scope
items.text:
The service leg of 7.17 (DD-193) proved that a writer holds the shared secret; it did not prove which writer wrote. This increment gives every graduable headless producer its own Keycloak identity — a client-credentials JWT, audience otel-collector, minted for a dedicated realm client — so a forged service push is attributable to the one client whose secret leaked, and the collector stamps which producer sent every telemetry push. It delivers:

  • Four confidential realm clients on aurelius's model — otel-postgres, otel-keycloak, otel-elasticsearch, otel-atlas-server — service accounts only (no flows), the otel-ingest scope as a default client scope (the same aud: otel-collector mapper as the browser leg), the shared dev client secret ${OTEL_INGEST_CLIENT_SECRET} placeholder in the realm import (the dev-users' pattern, replace-placeholders).
  • The collector's per-service leg: otlp/services (gRPC 4317 + HTTP 4319) swaps bearertokenauth for the oidc extension (same extension, CA, audience as the browser leg — one validator, both legs). The extension's providers list accepts both dev Keycloak listeners (DD-202: a token's iss is the listener that minted it; every automated producer mints at the TLS :8443 listener, the plaintext :8080 provider stays for the human dev browser, ADR 039). A new otlp/legacy receiver pair (gRPC 4320 + HTTP 4321, bearertokenauth, loopback-published) keeps 7.17's shared-token mechanism for the producers that cannot present a Keycloak JWT (below). The contrib image has no compositeauth extension, so a port carries one authenticator — the legs are separate ports by construction (DD-196).
  • Graduated producers (per-service JWTs on the per-service leg):
    • the three slice metrics-pullers (postgres, keycloak-metadata, elasticsearch) present their client credentials through the contrib collector's own oauth2client extension — mint, cache, refresh natively, zero custom code; each puller gains restart: on-failure:15 (the DD-195 race, now issuer-shaped);
    • the Atlas server (Python, logfire 5.2) presents its JWT through a small in-app refresh shim: a ClientCredentialsTokenSource (urllib + cache + refresh-ahead, thread-safe, stdlib-only) feeding per-export headers through logfire's additional_span_processors / MetricsOptions.additional_readers seams (logfire reads the static env headers only; the shim replaces the env-driven OTLP export — DD-196).
  • Staying on the legacy leg (shared token, the refused half of DD-193's graduation, now scoped to exactly these two):
    • Keycloak's native OTLP — the issuer cannot present a token it has not minted yet at cold boot (the chicken-and-egg DD-193 named);
    • the FastAPI example — the same static-header/60s-token wall as the server, for an example app; the shim was built for the server, where it pays.
  • Attribution (enduser.id DD-194, extended): the resource processor stamps otel.ingest.client from the verified token's azp claim; a transform clears enduser.id on service-account pushes (azp prefixed otel-) so human and machine identity stay distinguishable in Tempo and Grafana. The browser leg stamps otel.ingest.client="aurelius".

It explicitly does not deliver: per-service identity for Keycloak-native OTLP or the FastAPI example (DD-196, above), token rotation machinery (a leaked dev secret rotates by re-import + .env.enc bump), a client→leg allowlist on the OIDC extension (the extension verifies credential type, not identity: a user token on the service leg is accepted and stamped azp=aurelius — every push stays authenticated and attributed, CIA-08), per-producer secrets in dev (one shared dev client secret, the clients differ by id), production manifests, or auth on the collector's internal telemetry.

items.title: Semantics
items.text: Id Rule CIA-06 The per-service leg (4317 gRPC / 4319 HTTP, OIDC) rejects a push with no token, the shared ingest token, a token from an untrusted issuer, or a token without the otel-collector audience (401 / Unauthenticated), and accepts a client-credentials JWT minted for an otel-* realm client. CIA-07 Every graduated producer presents its own client's JWT: the three pullers (their oauth2client extension) and the Atlas server (the refresh shim) keep exporting through the suite windows — a producer whose client id, secret, or token URL is misconfigured exports nothing (401 at the receiver, visible in its logs). CIA-08 The legs are credential-typed, not identity-typed: the shared token never reaches an OIDC leg (401) and a JWT never reaches the legacy leg (401); a user token presented on the service leg is accepted and stamped azp=aurelius (accepted posture: authenticated + attributed is the bar, every push carries its writer). CIA-09 The collector stamps the verified writer: service-account pushes carry otel.ingest.client = the client id and enduser.id=""; user pushes carry otel.ingest.client="aurelius" and enduser.id=<sub>; legacy-leg pushes carry neither (empty upsert, DD-194's rule, unchanged). CIA-10 The legacy leg (4320 gRPC / 4321 HTTP, bearertokenauth) is loopback-published like every OTLP port (CIA-03 extended); Keycloak-native and the FastAPI example keep exporting on it with the shared token (CIA-04's surviving half). CIA-11 The OIDC legs (browser + per-service) accept a token from either dev Keycloak listener — the TLS :8443 iss every automated producer mints at (DD-202), and the plaintext :8080 iss the human dev browser carries (ADR 039) — and reject a token from any other issuer (401). The mint target is fixed in each producer's compose/env as a literal, never suite-flipped, so no suite start-order can starve another's telemetry.

items.title: Java origin
items.text: None. Apache Atlas 2.4.0 ships no OpenTelemetry collector (7.17's finding, unchanged); the increment is platform-side.

items.title: Deviations
items.text: None against Apache Atlas (no Atlas behaviour is touched). The posture choices — Keycloak as the service-identity issuer, the shared-token legacy leg for the un-graduable producers, one shared dev client secret, the credential-typed legs — are recorded in DD-196.

items.title: Acceptance
items.text:
• e2e (nx e2e aurelius-atlas-webapp -c ci, nx e2e aurelius-atlas-frontend-example -c ci):
    • test__collector_accepts_a_service_jwt — a client-credentials JWT (the e2e Keycloak, otel-atlas-server) pushed to 4319 answers 2xx, and the probe span reads back from Tempo stamped otel.ingest.client=otel-atlas-server with enduser.id="" (CIA-06, CIA-07, CIA-09 — the webapp suite, Tempo-wired)
    • test__collector_rejects_the_shared_token_on_the_service_leg — the shared token on 4319 answers 401 (CIA-06, CIA-08)
    • test__collector_rejects_a_jwt_on_the_legacy_leg — a service JWT on 4321 answers 401 (CIA-08)

items.title: 7.19 Frontend failure UX
items.text:
• Status: in progress
  • Pull request: — (follows the review of 2026-10-24, DD-214)
  • Records: DD-214 (the review that scoped this); cites 7.1, 7.3, 7.7, 7.14, 7.16, 7.17

items.title: Scope
items.text:
Test-completeness, no new rule ids (DD-214): the frontend's failure semantics are stated (APC-04, SHL-02, SPL-03/04, SHL-14, DD-193) with unproven paths. The review measured the frontend's systematic hole: only 7 of 71 webapp-side specs assert an HTTP error, admin.service and entities.service have zero failure tests, and the observability lib sits at 67% branch. This increment closes the measured holes:

  • aurelius-atlas-data-access — the error matrix for AdminService and EntitiesService (every method today answers success only): 4xx with the Atlas body through atlasErrorFrom, 5xx, and the status-0 network failure (APC-04). The TypeDefsService/AtlasEntitiesService error paths stay as they are — already proven.
  • aurelius-atlas-observability — the branch holes at 67%: the provider resource merge, the metrics options (web-vitals off, interval, pagehide flush), the error handler's non-Error conversions and no-active-span path, the interceptor's no-traceId and status-less-HttpErrorResponse branches, the ingest-auth token-less authenticated session, and a new opentelemetry-session.spec.ts for the storage-denied branches (SHL-14, DD-193).
  • aurelius-atlas-webapp — app.config.spec.ts gains initialize()'s loud failure when /config.json answers non-2xx (SHL-02's other half — today only the success path runs) and metricsUrl's two branches; the header's logout proves a rejecting keycloak.logout() does not surface as an unhandled rejection (SHC-05's failure edge).
  • aurelius-atlas-ui — dark-mode.component.spec.ts gains the real component assertions the one-create-test lacks: the title names the mode and a click cycles it (SPL-03, SPL-04's component side).
  • aurelius-atlas-frontend-example — the editor's save/delete against a real failing server (HttpTestingController, not a spy on the service under test): a 500 keeps the entity open, a 404 on delete surfaces the status; the form's validation gates save() (no request fires); app.config.spec.ts mirrors the webapp's config-failure pair; search.service.spec.ts proves the out-of-order response (late first answer discarded, switchMap cancellation — the interrupted/async category's proof, no production change).

It does not deliver: production-code changes (every test pins behaviour the shipped code has), new e2e scenarios (9.1), the server spine (deferred backlog #1), the context-card parametrised suite (representativeness polish, not failure coverage — deferred with the dashboard notes).

items.title: Semantics
items.text:
No new rule ids. The paths proven here, as stated:

  • APC-04 (7-3): a failed call surfaces {errorCode, errorMessage, errorCause} as the typed Atlas body — the matrix names each service method against 404/400 (Atlas body), 500 (Atlas body), and status 0 (network: atlasErrorFrom yields null, the interceptor's alert path).
  • SHL-02 (7-1): a /config.json that is missing, unreachable, or the wrong shape fails the boot loudly — proven for the non-2xx answer (the parse-rejection half stays in config.spec.ts).
  • SPL-03 / SPL-04 (7-14): the toggle's title states the current theme and a click cycles auto → dark → light; the component renders the service's mode (the service's storage/persistence tests are 7.14's).
  • SHL-14 / DD-193 / CIA-02 (7.16–7.17): the observability branch holes — each named by its own spec (metrics options, resource merge, pagehide flush, exception conversions, traceparent skip, token-less session, storage-denied session id).
  • (no rule id — the example app ships no increment spec, DD-214): the editor's failing save/delete, the form's validation gate, the search service's out-of-order response. Tests carry plain names.

items.title: Java origin
items.text: None new: this increment proves frontend rules whose 7.x specs cite the Aurelius libs/atlas/api (APC), the Aurelius shell boot (SHL-02), and the legacy theme toggle (SPL-03). The example app's editor is workspace boilerplate (no legacy twin, DD-001 lineage).

items.text: None.

items.title: Acceptance
items.text:
Unit (Vitest, run per project; ids in it() titles per the webapp convention):

  • libs/angular/aurelius-atlas-data-access/src/lib/admin.service.spec.ts — appended: surfaces the Atlas error body on a failed call (APC-04) (404, all three methods), surfaces the server fault body (APC-04) (500), surfaces a network failure as a status-0 response (APC-04) (flush(unknown, { status: 0, statusText: "Unknown Error" })).
  • libs/angular/aurelius-atlas-data-access/src/lib/entities.service.spec.ts — appended: the same three, over createOrUpdate/delete/findAll/findOne, each asserting atlasErrorFrom types the body (APC-04).
  • libs/angular/aurelius-atlas-observability/src/lib/ — appended specs naming the branch (SHL-14, DD-193): provider resource merge; metrics webVitals: false, custom interval, pagehide flush; error handler string/serialisable/non-serialisable conversions and the no-active-span span; interceptor no-traceId passthrough and status-less error; ingest-auth authenticated-without-token; new opentelemetry-session.spec.ts (reuse, getItem-denied, setItem-denied).
  • apps/aurelius-atlas-webapp/src/app/app.config.spec.ts — appended: initialize fails loudly when /config.json answers 500 (SHL-02), metricsUrl prefers the explicit endpoint / derives it from traces (SHL-14).
  • apps/aurelius-atlas-webapp/src/app/shell/header.component.spec.ts — appended: ends the session fire-and-forget even when logout rejects (SHC-05).
  • libs/angular/aurelius-atlas-ui/src/lib/dark-mode/dark-mode.component.spec.ts — appended: title names the mode; click cycles auto→dark→light; icon follows the mode (SPL-03, SPL-04).
  • apps/aurelius-atlas-frontend-example/src/app/editor/editor.component.spec.ts — appended (real server, no spies on EntitiesService): a 500 on save keeps the entity open and surfaces the status; a 404 on delete surfaces the status; an over-long name makes the form invalid and save() sends nothing.
  • apps/aurelius-atlas-frontend-example/src/app/app.config.spec.ts — new: the config-failure pair (mirrors the webapp's).
  • apps/aurelius-atlas-frontend-example/src/app/services/search.service.spec.ts — appended: discards a late answer for a superseded query (two queries, first flushed last, the second answer wins).

Gates: nx test aurelius-atlas-data-access -c ci, nx test aurelius-atlas-observability -c ci (branch coverage rises toward the 85% the Sonar gate wants — the review's measurement), nx test aurelius-atlas-ui -c ci, nx test aurelius-atlas-webapp -c ci, nx test aurelius-atlas-frontend-example -c ci green; lint clean. No production-code change, so no new-code coverage dip and no trace-check change (frontend rule ids are named by it() titles, not covers markers — the 117-gap baseline is the trace tool's Python-side scope, unchanged).

items.title: 7.2 Design system
items.text:
• Status: in progress
  • Pull request: #99
  • Records: ADR 053; DD-134, DD-135, DD-136, DD-137, DD-138; relies on ADR 007, DD-131

Part of the 7.0 umbrella, whose rules WBP-01 to WBP-07 this slice inherits and its Acceptance repeats.

items.title: Scope
items.text:
Port the shared components the Aurelius interface's search/browse surface actually uses into aurelius-atlas-ui as dumb, signal-driven components with stories, and make the documented purity gate (DD-131) real for libs/angular.

Every @models4insight/components import in apps/atlas/src sits under app/search/** (29 sites). The in-use set is eight folders — three already exist in the target lib in Angular idiom and are verified and extended, five arrive as ports:

  • accordion (11 uses) — exists; extended with the legacy ariaLabel input, the legacy toggle-content string, real behavioural specs; the swapped collapse()/expand() bug fixed.
  • modal (6 uses) — exists; extended with the legacy card anatomy: [modal-header], [modal-footer] slots, confirmLabel/cancelLabel inputs, backdrop-click close.
  • card + pagination (card grid; ngx-pagination in the shell) — exist; carry the chrome strings (UIC-04) and get real specs.
  • hero (1 use) — the search header: Bulma hero with title/subtitle inputs and [before-title], [after-title], [navigation] slots. The legacy component's embedded router-outlet is app wiring, not component API — it stays in the app (7.5).
  • simple-search-input (9 uses) → search-field — the ControlShell base and its reactive form dissolve into query = model() + querySubmitted = output().
  • sortable-table-shell + sortable-table (7 uses) → sortable-table — headers and rows via content slots with per-column directives; sort, page and selection as model() state; paging through the existing Pagination.

The legacy component-lib translations (components.*, 7 keys) are vendored as fixtures next to the app dictionaries and become the lib's i18n unit ids (DD-136), so the webapp's XLIFF bridge carries component chrome in both locales.

Not in scope:

Not delivered here Delivered by The Shell chrome (nav bar, breadcrumbs, app bar) 7.4 (search), 7.5 (browse) select, quickview (editor anatomy) 7.7 (editor) markdown (drags marked + dompurify into the dependency graph) 7.6 (entity details) tree, date-picker (the only @angular/material users) 7.6 (details), 7.7 (editor) Project/branch/user/permission modals, user-search-*, fuzzy-search-input consumed by no screen of the ported surface; 7.8 if ever Wiring the components into the webapp's screens 7.4 – 7.9 (the app composes; the lib defines, user rule)

items.title: Semantics
items.text:
Id Rule UIC-01 Every component is standalone, OnPush, takes state through input()/model()/output(), and injects no service with side effects (WBP-04) UIC-02 Every component ships a CSF3 story per visual state, and nx build-storybook aurelius-atlas-ui -c ci compiles them all UIC-03 Styling is Bulma utilities and @aurelius/atlas-brand tokens; no literal colours in component styles UIC-04 No @ngx-translate pipe: chrome strings carry i18n attributes whose ids reuse the legacy components.* dictionary keys (DD-136); title/footer text slots accept caller-localised content nodes UIC-05 No @angular/material and no ngx-pagination: sorting is header clicks over model() state, paging is the existing Pagination component UIC-06 The behaviours the legacy Jest specs assert are re-expressed as Vitest specs naming the rule ids in the test names (ADR 053 R5) UIC-07 The purity gate (WBP-02) greps libs/angular as DD-131 states, runs in CI, and passes (DD-137) UIC-08 The lib's peer dependencies match the workspace majors (Angular 22, @fortawesome/angular-fontawesome 5); lib and example app build green UIC-09 The public API grows additively — existing component APIs unchanged, aurelius-atlas-frontend-example builds and tests green (DD-136) UIC-10 The interactive components (accordion, modal, search-field, sortable-table) ship play() stories and nx test-storybook aurelius-atlas-ui passes

UIC-04 and UIC-09 together are the localisation rule for shared chrome: the component owns its string (it is part of the design), the app owns its translation, and one catalogue covers both because the ids are the legacy dictionary paths the XLIFF bridge already keys on.

UIC-09's additive constraint exists because the example app consumes the lib today; 7.2 must not break the app that is the pattern reference until 7.10 retires it. The webapp consumes no lib component yet — once a slice wires one in (7.4+), its extract-i18n run emits the template's @@components.* units into the catalogue the DD-136 bridge already keys, and the completeness spec keeps proving both locales.

items.title: Aurelius origin
items.text:
Cited by path in aureliusenterprise/aurelius at the cloned commit, so a reviewer can compare:

Aurelius Becomes libs/components/src/lib/accordion aurelius-atlas-ui: Accordion (extended) libs/components/src/lib/modal (+ AbstractModal, context object) aurelius-atlas-ui: Modal (extended; context → inputs) libs/components/src/lib/hero (embedded router-outlet) aurelius-atlas-ui: Hero (section + slots only) libs/components/src/lib/simple-search-input (+ ControlShell) aurelius-atlas-ui: SearchField libs/components/src/lib/sortable-table-shell + sortable-table aurelius-atlas-ui: SortableTable (+ column directive) libs/components/src/translations/{en-US,nl-NL}.json (components.*) tests/fixtures/components-*.json → XLIFF @@components.* ids libs/components/src/lib/control-shell (AbstractControlShell) dissolved: Bulma field markup inlined where used sortable-table-shell.service (redux BasicStore: sort, page, selection) dissolved: model() state on the component matSort, ngx-pagination, intersection-observer directive dropped: header-click sorting, Pagination, paging libs/components/src/lib/*/ *.module.ts standalone components (WBP-02)

Against the Aurelius product, the intended differences are recorded in design-log: the scope split of the component library (DD-134), the dissolution of component services into signal state (DD-135), chrome strings moving to the built-in localisation keyed by the legacy dictionary paths (DD-136), and the purity gate made executable over libs/angular (DD-137). No new DV entry: the UI swap itself is DV-64.

• libs/angular/aurelius-atlas-ui/src/lib/**/*.spec.ts (Vitest) — one spec per component, behaviours naming UIC ids in the test names: accordion toggle/ariaLabel, modal open/close/confirm/cancel/backdrop, search-field query two-way + submit + clear, sortable-table sort cycle/paging/selection/empty, hero slots, card/pagination chrome strings. UIC-06.

items.title: Definition of done, in order
items.text:
1. nx test aurelius-atlas-ui -c ci green with the coverage gate; nx lint and nx build aurelius-atlas-ui green on the bumped peer deps.
  2. The purity gate greps libs/angular in CI and passes.
  3. Every story renders in Storybook, light and dark — a reviewer's visual pass.
  4. The example app builds and tests green on the extended lib (UIC-09).
  5. The generator emits the components.* units and the completeness spec proves them in both locales (UIC-04, DD-136).
  6. libs/angular/aurelius-atlas-ui/AGENTS.md and README.md describe the new components, per ADR 003.

items.title: 7.3 API client and auth wiring
items.text:
• Status: in progress
  • Pull request: #100
  • Records: ADR 053; DD-139, DD-140, DD-141, DD-142; relies on ADR 007, ADR 018, ADR 038, DD-004, DD-130, DD-133

Part of the 7.0 umbrella, whose rules WBP-01 to WBP-07 this slice inherits and its Acceptance repeats.

items.title: Scope
items.text:
Give the webapp a real backend: the Atlas REST client in aurelius-atlas-data-access, and the Keycloak wiring the shell deferred (DD-133). This is the slice that closes the 7.0 audit question — how does the Aurelius interface reach the server? — and retargets the webapp's proxies at the server that answers.

The audit's answer shapes the whole slice (DD-139): the Aurelius app has no base URL at all. Every legacy URL is a relative path resolved against <base href>, and the /api/atlas prefix is injected entirely by the deployment proxy (the dev proxy.conf.json, the k8s Apache ProxyPass). Aurelius Atlas is built the other way round: the client owns the base URL (API_BASE_URL, fed from runtime /config.json, DD-130) and the proxy forwards a same-origin prefix untouched.

The client ports the surface the server implements today (DD-140): the type definitions of increment 1.6 (/api/atlas/v2/types/**) and the admin endpoints of 0.5 (/api/atlas/admin/**). It does not port calls to endpoints 2.x–4.x have not built — notably the search client, which the audit found is not an Atlas call at all (the Aurelius search posts to DuckDuckGo App Search engines that Aurelius Atlas does not have), and which arrives in 7.4 redesigned against /v2/search/basic when browse consumes it.

  • aurelius-atlas-data-access: TypeDefsService and AdminService over the implemented endpoints, the typedef cluster of libs/atlas/api/src/lib/types.ts as typed DTOs with the server's camelCase wire names, and the Atlas error shape.
  • apps/aurelius-atlas-webapp: provideApiBaseUrl, provideKeycloak (check-sso + silent-SSO), the bearer-token interceptor, a guard on the app root, and silent-check-sso.html — the provider set proven at the example app, minus what 7.1 already ships.
  • Proxies and dev infrastructure: the dev proxy and the e2e nginx /api/ location retargeted at the Atlas server; the Keycloak client gains the webapp's origins; the e2e stack runs the real Atlas server behind the proxy (DD-142).

Not in scope:

Not delivered here Delivered by Any search call, and the App Search → Atlas search redesign 7.4 (search), against /v2/search/basic (4.1) Entity, relationship, glossary and lineage clients 7.5–7.9, each behind its server increment (2.3+) A server that verifies the bearer token 6.1 (Authentication); 6.2 the authorizer Sign-in enforced per-screen, session user in the UI 7.4/7.5 (the Shell chrome reads /admin/session) Type-definition UI none — the client exists for 7.4's browse first

items.title: Semantics
items.text:
Id Rule APC-01 The client composes every URL from the injected API_BASE_URL token; no endpoint host, port, or /api/atlas prefix is hard-coded in the client (WBP, DD-139) APC-02 Every endpoint the server implements today has exactly one typed client method: the typedefs of /api/atlas/v2/types and version/status/session of /api/atlas/admin (DD-140) APC-03 Client DTOs use the wire names the server writes (camelCase Java getter names), and the typedef cluster carries the fields of AtlasTypesDef (TDM-01, TDM-13) APC-04 A failed call surfaces the Atlas error shape (errorCode, errorMessage, optional errorCause) as a typed error, not a bare HTTP status APC-05 Bootstrap initialises Keycloak with onLoad: "check-sso" and a silent-SSO redirect; an unauthenticated visit to a guarded route redirects to the sign-in page APC-06 Every /api request carries Authorization: Bearer <token>; tokens live in Keycloak's in-memory store, never localStorage (DD-004, ADR 007) APC-07 Token refresh is keycloak-angular's, not a ported loop: no hand-written updateToken scheduler exists in the webapp (WBP-02) APC-08 Both webapp proxies forward /api to the Atlas server with the prefix intact — the dev proxy and the e2e nginx both (DD-139) APC-09 The Keycloak aurelius client's redirect URIs and web origins cover the webapp's dev ports (4300, 4301) and its e2e origin (18444) APC-10 Every client method has a Vitest spec naming it, the guard has one, and the e2e suite proves the guarded flow and a real server response through the proxy

APC-01 is the rule the audit exists to write. A client that hard-codes /api/atlas reproduces the Aurelius coupling to its deployment: it cannot be tested against a stub, and it breaks the moment the API moves. The token already exists in aurelius-atlas-data-access; 7.3 is the slice that plugs it in.

APC-02 and APC-05..07 deliberately stop at the live surface. The legacy client is 65 files of endpoints the Aurelius server answers with a 404 today; porting them would ship a client that lies about the system, and its specs would assert calls nobody serves. The client grows one increment at a time, each method landing with the server increment that answers it.

APC-06 states what the token does today: the server ignores it until 6.1, and the interceptor is proven at the example app, which does verify. Sending a credential the server does not check is a stated condition of the pre-6.1 system (ADR 038 says the same of authorization), not a hidden gap.

items.title: Aurelius origin
items.text:
Cited by path in aureliusenterprise/aurelius at the cloned commit, so a reviewer can compare:

Aurelius Becomes relative URLs + <base href> + deployment proxy (no base URL anywhere) API_BASE_URL token from /config.json, prefix forwarded untouched (DD-139) libs/atlas/api/src/lib/type-def-api.service.ts (atlas/v2/types) TypeDefsService.getTypedefs, getTypeDefByName, per-kind lookups libs/atlas/api/src/lib/get-type-defs/, get-type-by-name/, get-classification-def-by-name/ the same TypeDefsService methods (legacy duplicated service + free function) libs/atlas/api/src/lib/types.ts (typedef cluster: AtlasTypesDef, AtlasEntityDef, AtlasStructDef, AtlasClassificationDef, AtlasEnumDef, AtlasRelationshipDef, AtlasAttributeDef, AtlasConstraintDef, RelationshipEndDef, TypeCategory, Cardinality, IndexType) atlas-typedef.ts DTOs, same wire names (APC-03) libs/atlas/api/src/lib/utils.ts (createHttpParams, nil-filtering) filterParams in the client (the idiom the lib already uses) libs/atlas/api/src/lib/elastic/**, engines/atlas-entity-search.service.ts, the AppSearchService→AtlasEntitySearchService DI alias not ported — 7.4 redesigns it against /v2/search/basic (DD-140) libs/atlas/api/src/lib/{get-lineage-model,get-dashboard,gov-quality}/** not ported — backends Aurelius Atlas does not have libs/authentication (keycloak-js + ReplaySubject auth state + manual updateToken(5) loop + AuthenticationGuard) keycloak-angular: provideKeycloak + createAuthGuard, keycloak-angular's refresh (DD-141) libs/http/authorization-header.interceptor.ts (AuthTokenProvider ctor injection per client) includeBearerTokenInterceptor + INCLUDE_BEARER_TOKEN_INTERCEPTOR_CONFIG on /api libs/shell/shell.ts childRoutes(..., requiresAuth) applying the guard the guard declared once on the webapp root route (DD-141) apps/atlas/proxy.conf.json (/atlas → :21000/api/atlas, prefix rewritten) webapp proxy.conf.json /api → the Atlas server, no rewrite (APC-08) backend/m4i-reverse-proxy (Apache ProxyPass per prefix) the webapp nginx /api/ location, TLS-verified (APC-08, DD-142)

The legacy libs/http is not ported at all: HttpService (an HttpClient subclass), its cache interceptor, and its IE-header interceptor solve problems this workspace's HttpClient + interceptors do not have (WBP-02).

items.title: Deviations
items.text:
None against Apache Atlas: this slice adds a client for the Atlas REST API the server already implements, and the shapes come from the server's parity-tested models.

Against the Aurelius product, three intended differences are recorded in design-log: the client owns the base URL where Aurelius delegated it to the proxy (DD-139); the search client is not ported in this slice and will not be ported as written (DD-140); and the auth wiring is keycloak-angular's, not the Aurelius libs/authentication (DD-141, on the pattern 7.1 set for the rest of Core.imports).

items.title: Acceptance
items.text:
• libs/angular/aurelius-atlas-data-access/src/lib/*.spec.ts (Vitest, HttpTestingController) — every TypeDefsService and AdminService method names its URL and its response type (APC-02, APC-03); the error spec proves the typed Atlas error (APC-04). SHL-13's rule applies here too: coverage gate holds.
  • apps/aurelius-atlas-webapp/src/app/*.spec.ts — the guard redirects an unauthenticated visit and lets an authenticated one through (APC-05); the config spec proves the providers are assembled (APC-06).
  • apps/aurelius-atlas-webapp/e2e/ — an unauthenticated load lands on the Keycloak sign-in page (APC-05); an authenticated session reaches the browse placeholder (APC-05, APC-09); GET /api/atlas/admin/version through the nginx proxy returns the server's version document (APC-08, DD-142), replacing the placeholder assertion that proxied Keycloak.
  • Umbrella checks: nx build, nx test -c ci, nx lint, nx e2e for the app, plus nx test aurelius-atlas-data-access -c ci and nx build aurelius-atlas-data-access.
  • Consumer regression: the example app is the data-access lib's current consumer, so nx test aurelius-atlas-frontend-example -c ci and its build must stay green (UIC-09's rule, applied to the lib).
  • Purity: check-purity covers libs/angular since DD-137, so the ported client is gated — no @models4insight/ import, no state-owning BehaviorSubject.

items.title: Definition of done, in order
items.text:
1. nx serve aurelius-atlas-server + nx serve aurelius-atlas-webapp: signing in through Keycloak lands on /search/browse, and a /api/atlas/v2/types/typedefs call from the browser answers through the proxy.
  2. The client specs and guard specs pass, each naming its APC rule id.
  3. nx e2e aurelius-atlas-webapp passes in all three browsers against the image, with the real Atlas server behind the proxy (DD-142).
  4. The example app's tests and build are untouched-green.
  5. aurelius-atlas-data-access and the webapp's AGENTS.md/README.md describe the new wiring and its removal, per ADR 003.

items.title: 7.5 Browse landing page
items.text:
• Status: in progress
  • Pull request: #101
  • Records: ADR 053; DD-143, DD-144; relies on ADR 007, DD-126, DD-128, DD-134, DD-135, DD-136, DD-140, DD-141, UIC rules (7.2)

Part of the 7.0 umbrella, whose rules WBP-01 to WBP-07 this slice inherits and its Acceptance repeats.

items.title: Scope
items.text:
Port the Aurelius landing page — the browse screen the router redirects to ('' -> /search/browse, SHL-04) — replacing the 7.1 placeholder with the real screen:

  • the hero block (title + description, browse.component.html)
  • the three context cards — business, technical, governance — each with its title, description, exploring text, and info icon (the three section components)
  • the three info modals: a description paragraph plus a static table of (icon, type name, description) rows, composed from the 7.2 aurelius-atlas-ui modal and sortable-table (the modal table data is the legacy tableData constants — static content, localized by dictionary key)

The page is the product's first real screen with zero API dependency: every string lives in the XLIFF bridge already (the search.browse.* keys are all present), and no data is fetched. This is what "the landing page" means for the port: the screen as it renders before any search exists.

Explicitly not delivered here, with the increment that will:

Deferred Lands with Why The cards' search fields (simple-search-input) and the "explore" buttons (directTo*) The search slice (7.4, gated by server 4.1 + 2.3 — DD-140) Both are search navigation: they set SearchService.query/filters and route to /search/results, a screen whose API does not exist yet. Porting the affordance without its destination is the speculative build DD-140 rejects (DD-143) The Shell chrome (header, footer, global nav) The search slice Aurelius wraps every screen in libs/shell, and the header's centrepiece is the global search bar; wiring the chrome is one decision with the search entry point, not two (DD-143) directToUser (governance card: search the signed-in user's e-mail) The search slice Same: search navigation; the e-mail is now available from Keycloak, the results page is not Search client, results, details 7.4 / 7.6, after server 4.1 / 2.3 API not ready (user decision, 2026-10-20: hold all search until the API is ready)

items.title: Semantics
items.text:
Each rule the behaviour must obey, in plain words, with an id that tests name (@pytest.mark.covers(..., rules=["BRW-NN"]); TS/e2e tests name the id in the test title).

Id Rule BRW-01 /search/browse renders the hero block — the search.browse.title heading and the search.browse.description paragraph, keeping the #browse-placeholder id the 7.1 shell tests anchor to — followed by the three context cards in Aurelius's order: business, technical, governance BRW-02 Every visible string on the page carries its legacy dictionary key as its i18n id (@@search.browse.<context>.<key>), with no literal prose in templates (WBP-05); the keys all exist in the XLIFF bridge, so both locales render fully (the completeness spec proves it) BRW-03 Each card's info icon opens that card's info modal: a description paragraph and a table of the legacy static rows — business: data domain / data entity / data attribute; technical: system / collection / dataset / field; governance: domain lead / data owner / data steward — each row an icon, a type name and a description, every string localized by its search.browse.<context>.infoModal.* key; the modal opens on icon click and closes via the ui-lib modal's close affordance BRW-04 The landing page issues no HTTP requests: component specs prove an empty HttpTestingController, and the e2e landing scenario records zero /api calls (the screen exists before its API does) BRW-05 The page is zoneless/Angular-idiom (standalone, OnPush, signals, inject()): modal open state is the ui-lib modal's model signal, card data is static consts, no store, no BehaviorSubject (DD-135, purity gate) BRW-06 No search affordance is ported: no search field, no explore button, no route to results (DD-143); the page's links and buttons are exactly the info-icon opens BRW-07 e2e (authenticated, chromium/firefox/webkit): the landing renders all three cards with localized titles; clicking a card's info icon opens its modal with its type-name rows visible; closing returns to the landing; the nl-NL locale renders the Dutch card titles

items.title: Aurelius origin
items.text:
The Aurelius 17 app (.scratch/aurelius, commit pinned by 7-0), apps/atlas/src/app/search/browse/:

  • browse.component.{ts,html} — the hero + three-card grid (BrowseComponent)
  • business-context/, technical-context/, governance-responsibilities/ — the section components (their directTo* methods and simple-search-input are the deferred affordances)
  • */info-modal/*-info-modal.component.{ts,html} — the static type tables (tableConfig / tableData constants)

items.title: Deviations
items.text:
None against Apache Atlas: this slice is an Aurelius product screen, and Atlas has no equivalent UI.

Against the Aurelius product, one intended difference is recorded in design-log: the landing page is ported statically — search affordances and the Shell chrome arrive with the search slice (DD-143), because the user has put all search work on hold until the server search API (4.1, with 2.3 entity read) exists.

items.title: Acceptance
items.text:
• Vitest (unit, nx test aurelius-atlas-webapp -c ci):
    • search/browse/browse.component.spec.ts — hero + three-card order (BRW-01), no outstanding requests (BRW-04)
    • card component specs (business/technical/governance) — strings render from the catalogue keys (BRW-02), info icon opens the modal (BRW-03), no search affordance in the DOM (BRW-06)
    • info-modal specs — table rows match the legacy tableData (BRW-03)
    • i18n-completeness.spec.ts — every @@search.browse.* id used by the new templates exists in both locale catalogues (BRW-02)
  • e2e (nx e2e aurelius-atlas-webapp): landing cards render (BRW-07), modal open/close flow (BRW-03/BRW-07), nl-NL titles (BRW-02/BRW-07); the 7.1 hero assertions (EN_PLACEHOLDER/NL_PLACEHOLDER on #browse-placeholder) stay green — the hero keeps its id (BRW-01)
  • Purity gate green (BRW-05); example app untouched.

items.title: 7.6 Entity details
items.text:
• Status: in progress
  • Pull request: #109
  • Records: DD-186 (details skeleton: route contract, gated data), DD-187 (the entity client grows with server 2.3), DD-188 (one API base: the client's URLs all ride the API_BASE_URL token, ADR 054); relies on ADR 053, DD-140, DD-143, UIC-11..13 (7.13), WBP rules (7.0)

Part of the 7.0 umbrella, whose rules WBP-01 to WBP-07 this slice inherits and its Acceptance repeats.

items.title: Scope
items.text:
Port the Aurelius entity details screen (search/details) — the screen the router shows for one entity by GUID — as the routed skeleton the data-free webapp can host today, and wire its chrome to the dumb components 7.13 already ships:

  • the route search/details/:guid, replacing the subtree route-by-route pattern 7.1 declared for it (search.routes.ts)
  • the details header: the entity title (name, qualified name as its fallback), the type-name line, and the breadcrumbs trail (the 7.13 breadcrumbs, with activeGuid and the caller-routed itemClicked)
  • the section shell: description box, properties accordion, and the side navigation — the shape of the legacy default details component, composed from Bulma and the 7.13 properties-item
  • AtlasEntitiesService in aurelius-atlas-data-access: the client method set for GET /api/atlas/v2/entity/guid/{guid} (the Atlas EntityREST shape, increment 2.3), built test-first against the wire format read from the Atlas source — the method the screen wires to when 2.3 lands

This is 7.5's gated-slice shape (DD-143), applied to a screen whose content is entirely data: every Aurelius details section reads one resolved entity, and server 2.3 (entity read REST) is planned, not built. The slice that ships the live details screen is the 2.3+7.6 wiring increment, named in the deferral table; it lands the nine type-specific components, the lineage view, and the governance-quality cards.

Explicitly not delivered here, with the increment that will:

Deferred Lands with Why Fetching the entity (resolver, loading, not-found, header data) The 2.3+7.6 wiring increment GET /v2/entity/guid/{guid} is increment 2.3 (planned); a fetch against a 404 is the speculative build DD-140 refuses The nine type-specific components (domain/entity/attribute/field/dataset/collection/system/person/process) The 2.3+7.6 wiring increment They are m4i governance-type layouts (m4i_data_domain, …) — Aurelius's own type model, meaningless without entity data Lineage view, governance-quality cards, data-quality lists/pies The 2.3+7.6 wiring increment (+ lineage backend) Lineage is server 5.1; the quality cards post to Aurelius backends Aurelius Atlas does not have (DD-140) Classifications list, glossary terms (meanings), edit affordance (DATA_STEWARD), people, domains Later 7.x slices (7.8, 7.9) + 3.3/3.4, 6.2 Each is a feature whose server increment is planned, not built Search entry into details (results page) 7.4, after server 4.1 + 2.3 (DD-143) Unchanged: all search is on hold

items.title: Semantics
items.text:
Each rule the behaviour must obey, in plain words, with an id that tests name (TS/e2e tests name the id in the test title; @pytest.mark.covers applies to the client spec, in the lib's Python-free Vitest suite — the rule ids ride the test names, the 7.3 pattern).

Id Rule DET-01 /search/details/:guid renders the details skeleton: the header block (title slot, type-name line, breadcrumbs trail), the description box, the properties accordion, and the side navigation — the legacy default layout's shape (its default-details anatomy), in Aurelius's palette. The :guid is a route parameter the skeleton keeps in a signal; it is the screen's address. DET-02 The skeleton is empty-state, not fake-state (DD-186): with no entity (all states, 2.3 absent), the title falls back to the localized search.details.typeSelect.label ("Entity type" — the chrome's type label), the breadcrumbs trail renders nothing (the 7.13 breadcrumbs empty guard), the description box is empty, and the properties accordion holds zero rows (its count reads 0). No placeholder data, no mock entity, no loading state. DET-03 AtlasEntitiesService.getEntityByGuid(guid) is the one client method for GET {API_BASE_URL}/atlas/v2/entity/guid/{guid} — composed from the injected token, no second base URL anywhere (DD-140's one-method rule, APC-01, the consolidated-server rule of ADR 054/DD-188, the typedefs client's pattern): the wire DTOs (AtlasEntity, its relationships, classificationNames, relationshipAttributes.meanings) are typed from the Apache Atlas 2.4.0 source (intg/.../model/instance/AtlasEntity.java, EntityREST.java), cited at the type. Specs use HttpTestingController — the method is honest against the wire format, and answers 404 against today's server; no screen calls it (DET-02). DET-04 Every chrome string is a @@search.details.* id with entries in both fixture locales (WBP-05, the DD-144 bridge rule); the skeleton uses the keys the bridge already carries (search.details.default.description, search.details.default.properties, search.details.components.properties.key/.value, search.details.components.navigation.details, search.details.typeSelect.label). The completeness gate (SHL-08) proves both locales. DET-05 The screen is zoneless/Angular idiom (standalone, OnPush, signals, inject()) and the dumb parts stay dumb (WBP-02..04, purity gate): the header's crumbs arrive as the 7.13 breadcrumbs component's items/activeGuid inputs; the properties rows are properties-items; the screen owns state, the lib owns rendering. DET-06 The breadcrumbs' itemClicked(guid) navigates the details route to that guid (the caller-routes contract, DD-154's sibling); the skeleton wires the router, the lib component never does. DET-07 The details route is deep-linkable (ALR-01's pattern, the drawer route's proof): a direct visit to /search/details/<guid> (authenticated) renders the skeleton — the URL is the whole state, as 2.3+7.6 will make it. e2e (authenticated): the skeleton renders at the deep link in every browser; the header shows the localized section titles.

items.title: Aurelius origin
items.text:
The Aurelius 17 app (.scratch/aurelius, commit pinned by 7-0), apps/atlas/src/app/search/details/:

  • details.component.{ts,html} — the type-dispatch shell (componentsByType, nine m4i_* types + default), the header (title, type name, classifications, terms, breadcrumbs, the DATA_STEWARD edit icon) — its data services (EntityDetailsService, ElementSearchService, the App Search providers) are the DD-140 stack this slice does not port
  • details-routing.module.ts / details.resolver.ts — the :id route and its resolver (the resolver's fetch is 2.3-gated)
  • default/default-details.component.{ts,html} — the default section layout (description box, property-count level, properties accordion, side nav) — the shape DET-01/02 port
  • components/properties/, components/navigation/ — the properties table (its item is the 7.13 properties-item) and the section nav
  • apps/atlas/src/app/search/components/bread-crumbs/ — the trail, ported in 7.13 as the ui-lib breadcrumbs; details.component.html shows its call site

items.title: Deviations
items.text:
None against Apache Atlas: this slice is an Aurelius product screen; Atlas's own details UI is its dashboard (ADR 046, the parity reference stays).

Against the Aurelius product, one intended difference is recorded in design-log: the details screen is ported as a routed skeleton (DD-186) — its data spine (entity fetch, type dispatch, lineage, quality) arrives with the 2.3+7.6 wiring increment, because the server's entity read REST (2.3) is planned and every Aurelius details section reads one resolved entity. The client method (DET-03) is built test-first against the Atlas wire format so the wiring increment is composition, not design (DD-187).

items.title: Acceptance
items.text:
• Vitest (unit):
    • libs/angular/aurelius-atlas-data-access/src/lib/atlas-entities.service.spec.ts — getEntityByGuid hits …/v2/entity/guid/<guid> with the Atlas headers, maps the DTO, encodes the guid (APC-01's base-url rule, DET-03)
    • search/details/details.component.spec.ts — the skeleton renders at the route (DET-01), empty-state per DET-02 (title fallback, no crumbs, zero property rows), strings from the catalogue (DET-04), itemClicked navigates the route (DET-06), no outstanding HttpTestingController requests (the screen fetches nothing — DET-02's proof)
    • routes.spec.ts — search/details/:guid loads the component (DET-01)
    • i18n-completeness.spec.ts — every @@search.details.* id used by the skeleton exists in both catalogues (DET-04)
  • e2e (nx e2e aurelius-atlas-webapp): the deep link renders the skeleton in every browser, localized titles visible (DET-07)
  • Storybook: the 7.13 components already carry the stories (UIC-15); the screen is app-side, no new story
  • Purity gate green (DET-05); umbrella checks (nx build, nx test -c ci, nx lint, nx e2e, both projects); example app untouched.

items.title: Definition of done, in order
items.text:
1. nx test aurelius-atlas-webapp -c ci and nx test aurelius-atlas-ui -c ci green.
  2. nx build aurelius-atlas-webapp, nx lint both projects, purity gate green.
  3. nx e2e aurelius-atlas-webapp — the deep-link scenario green in the chromium/firefox/webkit matrix.
  4. Spec status → done, roadmap row flipped, design-log DD-186..187 accepted.

items.title: Increment 8.0 — Auxiliary API Foundation
items.text: Field Value Status accepted Author Aurelius Atlas maintainers Date 2026-07-19 ADRs 055 (auxiliary APIs are a named data surface), 036 (per-app OTel exporter chain), 034 (dev Keycloak), 051 (increments) Design log DD-196 (extended here), DD-197 (per-service ingest identities), DD-132

items.title: Objective
items.text:
The legacy Aurelius dashboard consumes small auxiliary APIs alongside the Atlas metadata API (ADR 055). Increments 8.1–8.3 ship them as FastAPI apps. This increment is the shared foundation they all need, extracted from the server so it is written and tested once:

  • aurelius-atlas-otel — the collector ingest leg (DD-196's client-credentials token source + OTLP pipeline), moved out of aurelius-atlas-server so every service gets traces/logs/metrics to the collector with its own Keycloak identity (DD-197).
  • aurelius-atlas-auth — the OIDC verifier the example app prototyped (JWKS refresh, breaker, audience/role checks), ported into a library the auxiliary apps import.
  • Keycloak — one otel-<service> ingest client per auxiliary app.

No HTTP endpoint is added by this increment; the surface rules below govern the two libraries' behaviour, which is the contract the 8.x apps build on.

items.title: Scope
items.text:
In scope: libs/python/aurelius-atlas-otel, libs/python/aurelius-atlas-auth, dev/keycloak/import/master.json, the server's app wiring to the new otel lib.

Out of scope: the auxiliary apps themselves (8.1–8.3), the server's lineage feed (5.1), CSRF (the auxiliary APIs are same-token bearer APIs like the metadata API — the server's ADR 039 cookie/CSRF flow is server-scope; noted in DD-197).

items.title: Foundation behaviour
items.text: ID Rule Java / legacy source Enforced by Deviation AUX-01 An OTLP exporter's session acquires a <azp> for aud=otel-collector client-credentials token — the service's otel-<service> Keycloak identity, DD-196 shape — and attaches it as a bearer header to every export request (Aurelius: DD-196, extended by DD-197) test__export_request_carries_the_bearer_token — AUX-02 The token is refreshed ahead of expiry, cached across requests, and refreshed once (with the old token dropped) on a 401/403 (Aurelius: DD-196) test__token_is_cached_and_refreshed_ahead_of_expiry test__a_401_forces_one_refresh_and_a_retry — AUX-03 When no ingest credentials are configured, the pipeline exports to the console only — dev mode, never a broken collector leg (Aurelius: server app.py, DD-197) test__console_only_without_config — AUX-04 A verified token's roles are the realm roles plus the roles of the service's own audience only: Keycloak namespaces client roles under resource_access.<audience>, so another service's roles never grant access here (DD-132's rule, now library-wide) (Aurelius: example app, DD-132) test__an_external_clients_role_does_not_grant_write test__an_unprefixed_client_role_does_not_grant_write test__realm_roles_apply_under_any_audience — AUX-05 Signature, issuer, and expiry are verified against the realm's published keys (kid selected, alg pinned to RS256); the azp/aud must name the service; the raw-bearer dependency yields the unverified token for forwarding only, never authorisation (Aurelius: example app) test__a_valid_token_is_accepted test__a_forged_signature_is_rejected test__a_token_from_a_foreign_issuer_is_rejected test__an_expired_token_is_rejected test__an_unverified_alg_is_rejected test__a_token_minted_for_another_audience_is_rejected test__require_bearer_yields_the_raw_token_for_forwarding test__a_missing_credential_is_rejected —

items.title: Non-negotiables (workspace-wide, restated for 8.x)
items.text: CIA-07 (every exporter leg carries the per-service ingest token, defined in 7.18's spec) is enforced here by test__export_request_carries_the_bearer_token in the moved suite; the rule id keeps its home in 7-18-collector-ingest-identity.md.

items.title: Data contracts
items.text:
• aurelius_atlas_otel.ingest.build_otlp_pipeline(...) -> IngestPipeline with keyword args endpoint, service_name, deployment_env, token_url, client_id, client_secret, ca_file, protocol — verbatim move of the server's otel_ingest.py; the server imports it now.
  • aurelius_atlas_auth.auth.KeycloakAuth(AuthConfig(server_url, realm, audience, write_role, ...), http) — exposes require_auth / require_write (authorised AuthUser) and require_bearer (raw token, forwarding only), per AUX-04/AUX-05.
  • Keycloak clients otel-data2model, otel-lineage-model, otel-validate-entity join the otel-collector audience group (DD-197).

items.title: Test list
items.text:
• Unit: libs/python/aurelius-atlas-otel/tests/test__ingest.py (moved), libs/python/aurelius-atlas-auth/tests/test__auth.py (new, fake issuer).
  • E2E: none for this increment — the libraries are exercised end-to-end by the 8.1–8.3 app e2e suites against the shared dev Keycloak and collector.
  • Parity: none — the foundation ports Aurelius mechanisms (DD-196/DD-197/DD-132), not Atlas 2.4 behaviour; the example app's auth tests are the reference.

items.title: Acceptance criteria
items.text:
• Every rule id above names a unit test (ADR 049 — aurelius-atlas-trace check green).
  • The server keeps its collector leg through the lib (nx test aurelius-atlas-server -c ci).
  • Keycloak import stays valid JSON; the three clients appear with the collector audience.
  • Ruff, pyright, prettier, commit checks.

items.title: Delivery
items.text:
• Branch: feat/aux-apis-foundation (PR 1 of the 8.x chain).
  • M6: this is shared plumbing for the ADR 055 data surface; the ADR 052 gate applies at 8.1–8.3, where dashboard-visible behaviour lands.

items.title: Open questions
items.text:
• Ingest identity granularity: one otel-<service> client each (DD-197) vs one shared client — chosen per-service for least privilege; secrets scale with service count (accepted).
  • CSRF for the auxiliary APIs: deferred to the webapp increment that serves them; the APIs are bearer-first (CORS + same token), matching the metadata API.

items.title: Increment 8.1 — data2model API
items.text: Field Value Status accepted Author Aurelius Atlas maintainers Date 2026-10-23 ADRs 055 (auxiliary APIs are a named data surface), 051 (increments), 049 (traceability), 052 (parity cites the reference; here the reference is Aurelius source) Design log DD-197 (foundation), DD-209 (provider/route layout), DD-198 (no pandas: pydantic rules, plain rows), DD-132 (audience-scoped roles), DV-68 (native layout)

items.title: Objective
items.text:
Port the legacy Aurelius m4i-data2model service — the model-extraction API the lineage graph draws on — to a FastAPI app: apps/aurelius-atlas-data2model.

POST /extract takes tabular data plus element/relation/view rules and returns an archimate3 model string the webapp's archimate3 parser ingests, plus per-record metadata. The legacy chain is lineage_model → data2model /extract (8.2 ports the caller).

The legacy implementation is a Flask app on m4i-analytics (pandas, graphviz, bokeh). Per DV-68 the analytics library is not ported: the ar3 JSON is built natively, and the archimate_process graphviz layout is replaced by a deterministic native left-to-right layout — coordinates only need to be numbers to the parser (DV-68). The port adds no pandas (DD-198): the request rules are pydantic models, the tabular data stays a plain list of row maps, and the extraction is plain Python — the legacy's pandas DataFrame was its representation, not part of the browser contract. The browser contract — the JSON body of the response and the ar3 model string's shape — is the legacy contract and is cited rule by rule.

items.title: Scope
items.text:
In scope: the app (settings, app factory, /extract, liveness), the ar3 builder and layout, unit tests, parity scenarios read from the Aurelius source, container and e2e (Keycloak-protected, real tokens).

Out of scope: the caller (lineage_model, 8.2), the webapp lineage screen (7.x webapp track), the legacy /parse_dataset endpoint (file upload to pandas — its only caller is the legacy model-editor app, not the lineage chain; not ported), the m4i-analytics library (DV-68).

items.title: Contracts and Rules
items.text: The reference for every rule is the Aurelius source (ADR 055 R4): the legacy service backend/m4i-data2model/m4i_data2model/data2model.py (extract), libs/m4i-analytics/m4i_analytics/model_extractor/ExtractorLanguagePrimitives.py, .../graphs/languages/archimate/ArchimateUtils.py (to_JSON, generate_view), and m4i-analytics-extensions/m4i-graphviz-layouts (layout names).

items.title: Extract
items.text: ID Rule Legacy source Enforced by Deviation DTM-01 POST /extract accepts a JSON body {data: [row…], rules: {elements: […], relations: […], views: […]}} and answers 200 with {metadata: […], model: "<ar3 JSON string>"} — the model is a JSON string inside the JSON body; content type is application/json data2model.py::extract (dumps(result), 'model': ArchimateUtils.to_JSON(model)) test__extract_returns_metadata_and_an_ar3_model_string The legacy Flask returned the JSON document as text/html; the body contract is unchanged DTM-02 Each element rule reads its id_key column: rows with a null id are dropped, the first row per id is kept (per rule), and each yields a node id = id_prefix + str(id), type = the rule's concept_type tag, name = concept_name_prefix + str(name) when concept_name_key is a column else ''; a rule for a column absent from the data yields nothing. Null is JSON null and the legacy's pandas NaN — the JSON request body carries both as null ExtractorLanguagePrimitives._parse_concept_definition, _parse_concept_node test__element_rules_read_their_id_column test__a_null_id_row_is_dropped test__a_rule_for_an_absent_column_yields_nothing A null id yields nothing, not a 'nan' node; a null name yields '', not the legacy's 'nan' string (both recorded below) DTM-03 Every parsed row yields a metadata entry {id, data} with data = {created_by: "Model Extractor API", m4i_id_prefix, m4i_original_id: str(id)} plus each mapping entry {key: value} whose source column exists and is non-null (null as DTM-02), first row per id; the response's metadata is elements, then relations, then views, in rule order _parse_concept_data, _parse_relationship_data, parse_view; data2model.py metadata concat test__metadata_names_the_source_row_per_rule test__metadata_lists_elements_then_relations_then_views — DTM-04 Each relation rule resolves its source/target to the referenced element rule's id_key/id_prefix; rows with a null source or target are dropped, the first row per relation id is kept; an edge id = id_prefix + str(id) from source_prefix + str(source_id) to target_prefix + str(target_id) with @xsi_type = the relationship_type shorthand's tag (lr → lineage_relation); an edge survives only when both endpoints exist as model nodes — its metadata entry is kept either way _parse_relationship_definition, parse_relationship (node-membership filter), fmt_relation in data2model.py test__relation_rules_resolve_their_endpoint_rules test__every_edge_endpoint_is_a_model_node — DTM-05 Model-wide, nodes and edges are deduplicated by id keeping the last occurrence, at the kept row's position, across all rules data2model.py drop_duplicates(subset=['id'], keep='last') test__duplicate_ids_keep_the_last_row — DTM-06 A view whose view_layout is a known layout (archimate_process → left-to-right, archimate_hierarchical → bottom-to-top) is generated; a view with an unknown layout is ignored — no view, no metadata; id_type: "static" produces one view ided by id_value, named by view_name_value data2model.py supported_layouts filter; parse_view static branch test__a_view_with_an_unknown_layout_is_ignored_entirely test__a_static_view_takes_its_id_and_name_from_the_rule — DTM-07 A view's nodes are the ids collected from its view_nodes rules (each rule scans its id_key column: non-null, first per id, in rule order), intersected with the model nodes in model order; empty view_edges means every model edge between the view's nodes, in model order parse_view view_nodes/view_edges scan; generate_view isin filters test__view_nodes_are_collected_by_rule_and_intersected_with_the_model — DTM-08 Node coordinates come from a deterministic native layout (DV-68): ranks by longest path from edge sources, left-to-right x = rank * 320, y stacked by 95 and centred per rank, rounded to integers; items.text: concept_type accepts the Archimate 3.0 tags the legacy ElementType enum publishes; the lineage chain uses lineage_dataset and lineage_process (both layer Other). relationship_type accepts the legacy shorthands (lr → lineage_relation, f → ar3_Flow, …). The full tables are ported as data, not as the enum machinery.

items.title: Objective
items.text:
Port the legacy Aurelius m4i-lineage-model service — the lineage-graph API the webapp's lineage screen calls — to a FastAPI app: apps/aurelius-atlas-lineage-model.

GET / takes guid (required), depth (default 3) and direction (default BOTH), fetches the entity's lineage from an Atlas metadata API (GET {atlas_base_url}/v2/lineage/{guid}), flattens the lineage relations into the 12-column archimate rows, and POSTs them with the fixed lineage rules to data2model /extract (8.1), returning that response body verbatim — the {model, metadata} document the lineage screen consumes. The chain is webapp → lineage_model → data2model /extract.

Per DV-69 the data path is stubbed until the server's lineage feed (5.1): the Atlas base URL is a setting, no increment blocks on 5.1, and the tests use canned lineage fixtures. The caller's bearer token is forwarded to both upstream calls — the legacy's token-passing design (the caller is the browser's own token; 8.1 records why that makes aurelius the audience).

The legacy is a Flask app on m4i-atlas-core (get_lineage_by_guid, LineageInfo dataclasses, requests.post to data2model). The port follows DD-198: pydantic models parse the upstream lineage at the boundary, rows are plain dicts, and the HTTP client is injectable for tests (DD-200).

items.title: Scope
items.text:
In scope: the app (settings, app factory, GET /, liveness), the lineage models and flattening, the fixed rules document, unit tests, a parity scenario, container and e2e (Keycloak-protected; the real data2model container; a canned-file fixture Atlas).

Out of scope: the Atlas lineage feed itself (5.1 — the setting points at it), the webapp lineage screen (7.x track), the legacy aiocache @cached() on the fetch (a dev convenience; the screen refetches on navigation — no cache), the m4i-atlas-core library (only the lineage fetch is ported, as a local httpx call).

items.text: The reference for every rule is the Aurelius source (ADR 055 R4): backend/m4i-lineage-model/m4i_lineage_model/lineage_model.py (lineage_model, fmt_lineage_relation, the rules dict, process_types), libs/m4i-atlas-core/m4i_atlas_core/api/atlas/get_lineage_by_guid.py (path, params), .../entities/atlas/core/lineage_info/LineageInfo.py (camelCase JSON shape), and the webapp caller apps/atlas/src/app/search/details/components/lineage-model/lineage-model.service.ts.

items.title: Upstream lineage shape
items.text: The fetch consumes Atlas's v2/lineage/{guid} camelCase JSON — {guidEntityMap: {guid: {guid, typeName, displayText, …}}, relations: [{fromEntityId, relationshipId, toEntityId}], …} — parsed as pydantic models with extra fields ignored (the legacy's dataclasses_json shape); only the fields the flattening reads are declared (DD-198).

items.title: Objective
items.text:
Port the legacy Aurelius m4i-validate-entity service — the entity governance-quality endpoint the webapp's editor calls while a record is being edited — to a FastAPI app: apps/aurelius-atlas-validate-entity.

The legacy service is a mock (DV-67): POST / accepts the entity, never reads it, and answers a fixed governance-quality document — four cards (dataEntity, definition, domainLead, name), each a list of gov_quality-shaped items with a compliance flag. The browser's editor renders those cards; the compliance verdicts are canned. Increment 8.3 ships that mock contract verbatim, with the workspace's auth (DD-197) and observability (DD-196): the browser contract is kept, real validation is a future server rule (DV-67).

POST / answers 200 application/json with the mock document for any request body; the body is not parsed (the legacy ignores it, and the port keeps that). GET / requires a valid Keycloak bearer token, verified for this app's audience — not the legacy's transparent=True pass-through (DV-75). The app has no upstreams: unlike 8.2's chain, nothing is forwarded.

The legacy is a Flask app on m4i_backend_core (gunicorn, WSGI_PORT 7200). The port follows the 8.x app conventions: FastAPI, the shared aurelius-atlas-auth verifier, app-owned OTel export, TLS, the 21000-series port (21003).

Out of scope: real governance validation (DV-67 — a future server rule), the webapp governance cards (7.x track), the gov_quality ElasticSearch engine the mock's _meta.engine name echoes (the document names it; the app does not call it).
